panels.title: Frame rules — what the image rounds taught
items_html: Attach the medias, or the prompt is fiction. The first run of these eight shots went out with the prompt text saying “copy the attached reference” and no medias array. Every job still ran and still billed. Check the array is populated before submitting, every time.

A framing reference leaks its content. Where only the composition was wanted (C5b, C6, C7) the prompt has to say outright that the room, the people and the colours are new and must not match the reference — otherwise you get the competitor's room back.

Two references means two explicit jobs. Name them by position — “the FIRST attached reference” for framing, “the SECOND” for the product — and give each a sentence of its own. Anything left implicit gets dropped.

Describe the reference from the reference, not from memory of it. C04 burned two generations because the prompt said ref05 was “a high downward angle, tilted down roughly 45 degrees, the product small in frame with a lot of counter around it.” ref05 is none of those things — it is close, shallow and the product is large. The model rendered the description perfectly both times. Open the reference and read it off the picture before writing a single line of camera language.

Anything you do not name gets deleted. C03 g2 lost the countertop because the prompt only said “background — a warm modern kitchen.” If an element must survive, name it, say where it sits in the frame, and ban what replaces it when it goes. Companion shots that share a set need the same block of text, word for word, in both prompts.

Children plus sleepwear trips the NSFW filter. “Christmas pyjamas” killed C5b and C6 outright. “Knitted Christmas jumper and matching lounge trousers” plus “wholesome family Christmas scene” passes, and the output still reads as pyjamas.

Projection needs physics, not decoration. Say it is flat, slightly translucent, wraps and distorts over furniture and corners, brightest on flat walls, fading in recesses — and ban decals, printed wallpaper and stickers. Without that clause the pattern renders as wallpaper.

Hold a room by feeding back your own approved frame. C05, C05b, C06 and C07 all needed one element changed inside a scene that was already right. Passing our own g1 as @Image 1 and writing “CHANGE 1 — …” as the only instruction kept every wall, light and camera identical. Tighter than any re-description.
Vary the grade across the reveals. Three payoff shots in a row in the same palette read as one shot. C5b sits warm-gold, C07 sits blue-dominant; that alone makes the cut feel like three rooms.

ref04 is the product anchor until a real photo exists. product_images/reference/ is empty, so the first pass built C03 and C04 off the render printed on the packshot — which is all white. The competitor frame ref04.png is the only source that shows the flat black perforated mesh lens disc on the top face. Attach it to every shot of the unit and say the black top out loud, or the model renders an all-white dome.
No text in frame, ever. Every prompt ends with the ban. Hook copy goes on in CapCut.

panels.title: Clip rules — what the animation rounds taught
items_html: A video reference imports its own audio. C01 and C02 both came back twice with the reference clip's soundtrack baked in. Nothing in the prompt stops it — the fix is to attach a silenced copy of the reference, which is what the scene_no_audio-*.mp4 files in references/ are. Both shots passed on the first take after the swap.
A video reference has to be at least two seconds long. Anything shorter is rejected outright, so the short scene cuts were padded to 4.5 s before they could be attached at all.

Prose alone will not animate a projection. Every wording of “the pattern drifts across the wall” produced a still pattern. The only lever that moved it was attaching a silenced clip as motion authority and naming it as such.

The take with no video reference won two of seven shots. C04 kept its very first pass and C07 was won by the bare start frame under the guide architecture — SUMMARY line, then beats with explicit time ranges. A reference is not free; it drags its own content in with it.

Count the re-rolls per shot before you commit to a shot. C06 took ten takes and still parked short of the reference; C03 took two. That ratio is the real cost of a shot, and it is worth knowing before the storyboard is locked.
Never overwrite a take. Every take here is still on disk under its own letter, which is the only reason the whole round could be reconstructed — prompts included — after the fact.

det.label: Clip prompt · v1_c01_g3.mp4
det.text:
AUDIO RULE - HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ THIS FIRST: this clip has NO MUSIC OF ANY KIND. No background song, no soundtrack, no score, no melody, no instruments, no singing, no humming, no jingle, no Christmas song, no festive music bed, no ambient musical pad, no strings, no piano, no bells used as music. The audio track contains ONLY real natural sound recorded in that room plus the spoken line. The attached reference video is SILENT and has no audio track at all - take nothing from it but movement. If any music appears anywhere in the 4 seconds the clip is wrong.

TASK: image-to-video. The start image is frame 0.0s. Hold its wardrobe, store, lighting and lens exactly.

[1] SUMMARY
A woman in a supermarket Christmas aisle stops her trolley, reacts in shock and points off-camera; the camera whip-pans right onto a pallet of dark-green product boxes. Handheld vertical UGC. 4 seconds, one continuous take with one whip pan.

[2] GLOBAL STYLE
Real handheld phone footage filmed by a friend walking behind her. Natural retail lighting warmed by the red and gold decorations. Extremely sharp, clean, well exposed. Subtle handheld breathing throughout. The ONLY blur in the clip is the deliberate horizontal motion blur inside the whip pan. No cinematic grade, no film grain, no vignette, no slow motion.

[3] ASSET ROLES
The start image controls the woman's identity, her cream knit sweater and dark jeans, the aisle, the shelving and the lighting. @Image 1 controls ONLY the look of the product pallet the pan lands on: a tall stack of DARK-GREEN cartons with a red banner and a white projector illustration, with red poinsettia and garland on top. Do not copy camera angle or lighting from @Image 1. @Video 1 controls ONLY the camera path and the rhythm of the performance: walk, stop, hand to mouth, point, whip pan right, settle on the product stack. Do not copy the woman, her clothes, the trolley colour, the store or the boxes from @Video 1. @Video 1 is silent - there is no audio, no music and no soundtrack in it to copy.

[4] CHARACTERS
THE WOMAN - long light-brown hair, cream oatmeal knit sweater, dark jeans, seen from behind and slightly to her left. COUNT LOCK: exactly one person on screen for all 4 seconds. No other shoppers, no staff, no children.

[5] LOCATION - every one of these exists in the start image and must survive to the last frame before the pan: a wide polished pale-floor supermarket aisle; decorated Christmas trees with red and gold ornaments standing on top of the left-hand shelves; red baubles hanging from the ceiling; red-accented shelving on the right. THE TROLLEY - the dark grey shopping trolley she is pushing.

[6] FIRST FRAME - exactly the start image: THE WOMAN from behind and slightly left, both hands on THE TROLLEY handle, mid-aisle, walking away from camera.

[7] TIMELINE
0.0-1.0s - camera handheld, follows THE WOMAN from behind at walking pace; THE WOMAN pushes THE TROLLEY forward two steps.
1.0-2.0s - THE WOMAN releases the handle and takes one step forward ahead of THE TROLLEY. THE TROLLEY keeps rolling forward on its own down the aisle, unpushed. Her right hand flies up and covers her mouth; her head turns to her right; her shoulders lift. Camera holds.
2.0-3.0s - THE WOMAN drops the hand from her mouth and throws her right arm straight out, index finger pointing forward and to the right, off the right edge of frame. THE WOMAN speaks. Camera holds.
3.0-4.0s - as her arm reaches full extension the camera WHIP PANS hard to the right with heavy horizontal motion blur; THE WOMAN leaves frame to the left; the pan decelerates and settles on the tall pallet of DARK-GREEN product cartons from @Image 1 standing in the aisle with red poinsettia and garland on top. Tiny push-in and hold.

[8] DIALOGUE
English dialogue. THE WOMAN: "There is no way!" Spoken 2.1-2.9s. Delivery: loud, delighted, genuinely stunned, American accent. This spoken line is the ONLY voice in the clip. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

[9] CAMERA AND OPTICS - single continuous handheld take, vertical 9:16, normal wide-angle phone lens, chest height, about two metres behind THE WOMAN, her body in the centre-left third. One camera movement only: the whip pan right at 3.0s. Do not cut. Do not zoom. Do not orbit. No fisheye, no barrel distortion, no warped shelving or curved floor lines.

[10] LIGHTING - flat overhead retail lighting with warm pools under the decorations, clean white balance, no colour cast change across the clip.

[11] PHYSICS - THE TROLLEY rolls straight and slows gradually under its own momentum after she lets go; it never turns, never tips, never leaves the floor, never stops dead. Her sweater and hair move naturally with her turn.

[12] AUDIO - DRY DOCUMENTARY AUDIO ONLY. The track contains exactly three things and nothing else: low supermarket room ambience, the rattle of trolley wheels on the hard floor, and her single spoken line. Total silence apart from those. NO MUSIC, NO SONG, NO SCORE, NO SOUNDTRACK, NO INSTRUMENTS.

[13] POSITIVE LOCKS - exactly one person. THE TROLLEY continues forward alone after 1.0s. The aisle, the decorated trees on the shelf tops and the hanging red baubles are present in every frame before the pan. The pan lands on cartons that are DARK GREEN with a red banner.
BANNED: any music, any song, any score, any soundtrack, any instrument, any singing; a second shopper, the trolley stopping dead or vanishing, THE WOMAN turning to face the camera, any cut, blue or white or brown or kraft boxes, a shelf of unrelated products, subtitles, on-screen text, slow motion, any blur outside the pan.

det.label: Clip prompt · v1_c02_g3.mp4
det.text:
AUDIO RULE - HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ THIS FIRST: this clip has NO MUSIC OF ANY KIND. No background song, no soundtrack, no score, no melody, no instruments, no singing, no humming, no jingle, no Christmas song, no festive music bed, no ambient musical pad, no strings, no piano, no bells used as music. The audio track contains ONLY real natural sound recorded in that room. The attached reference video is SILENT and has no audio track at all - take nothing from it but movement. If any music appears anywhere in the 4 seconds the clip is wrong.

EXIT RULE - SECOND MOST IMPORTANT: the projector does NOT stay in frame at the end. The hands lift it out of the box and KEEP GOING, carrying it straight up and completely out of the top of the frame. At 4.0s the projector is GONE from the picture and only the open carton is left on the table. The hands never stop, never hold the product up for inspection, never settle, never pause.

SPEED RULE - THIRD MOST IMPORTANT: the hands work at a brisk, confident, real-time pace. This is a normal person opening a box at normal speed, not a careful slow-motion demonstration. The lift is QUICK and decisive. Do not slow anything down.

TASK: image-to-video. The start image is frame 0.0s. Hold its table, box artwork, props and lighting exactly.

[1] SUMMARY
First-person POV: two hands open a tall dark-green Christmas carton on a wooden table, lift the white projector briskly straight up out of it and carry it out of the top of frame. Locked POV looking down. 4 seconds, one take.

[2] GLOBAL STYLE
Real handheld phone POV, warm domestic Christmas light, crisp and sharp, correctly exposed. Very slight handheld drift. Real-time speed throughout. No cinematic grade, no grain, no slow motion, no speed ramp.

[3] ASSET ROLES
The start image controls the table, the carton artwork, the hands, the candle, the props and the light. @Video 1 controls ONLY the mechanics of the unboxing: fingers slide under the front lid flap, flaps fold up and back, hands grip the unit inside, the unit lifts straight up. Do not copy the table, the box design, the room, the hands or the product from @Video 1. Do NOT copy the pacing from @Video 1 - use the faster timeline below. Do NOT copy its ending - in this clip the product leaves the frame.

[4] OBJECTS
THE BOX - a dark-green tuck-top carton standing upright, front panel facing camera, gold THEXMASGLOW banner, the words CHRISTMAS LIGHT PROJECTOR, a white projector on a red circle. About 15 x 15 x 24 cm. Plain interior, no insert, no foam tray, no window.
THE PROJECTOR - inside THE BOX: a matte-white dome-shaped body on a separate white four-legged splayed stand. Set into the top of the dome is a flat circular BLACK perforated mesh disc. The top face is BLACK and stays black for every frame. No front lens, no camera head, no swivel.
THE HANDS - exactly two hands, a cream knit sleeve on the left wrist, a thin gold bracelet on the right wrist.

[5] LOCATION - a dark round wooden table fills the frame. A lit cream pillar candle sits at the top left, holly sprigs with red berries beside it, warm fairy lights out of focus behind. The candle, the holly and the fairy lights must still be in the final frame.

[6] FIRST FRAME - exactly the start image: THE BOX closed and upright, both HANDS gripping its sides.

[7] TIMELINE - brisk real-time pacing, every beat lands on time
0.0-0.7s - camera locked. The fingers of both HANDS slide under the front top flap of THE BOX and lift it sharply; the tuck tongue pops out of the front panel.
0.7-1.4s - the lid flaps fold upward and backward away from camera on the rear fold in one quick motion, staying attached to THE BOX; the dark interior comes into view.
1.4-2.1s - both HANDS drop straight down into THE BOX and grip THE PROJECTOR by its sides, thumbs on the near side. The BLACK perforated mesh disc on its top face is clearly visible.
2.1-3.0s - THE HANDS lift THE PROJECTOR QUICKLY and decisively straight up and out of THE BOX in one brisk continuous vertical pull, clearing the rim in well under a second. The BLACK top face is clearly visible as it rises.
3.0-3.6s - the HANDS DO NOT STOP. They keep rising in the same continuous motion; THE PROJECTOR travels up towards the top edge of frame, first the stand then the dome crossing the edge and leaving the picture.
3.6-4.0s - THE PROJECTOR and both HANDS are completely OUT OF FRAME. The frame holds on the open empty carton on the wooden table, lid flaps folded back, with the candle, the holly and the fairy lights still in shot. Nothing else moves.

[9] CAMERA AND OPTICS - one static POV looking down at the table at roughly 50 degrees, vertical 9:16, normal wide-angle phone lens, very slight handheld drift only. The camera NEVER follows the product upward - it stays exactly where it is and lets the product exit the frame. No push-in, no orbit, no zoom, no tilt, no cut.

[10] LIGHTING - warm indoor candle and fairy-light mix, unchanged for the whole clip.

[11] PHYSICS - cardboard behaves like cardboard: the flaps crease on their folds and stay attached to THE BOX. THE BOX stays flat on the table and does not slide, tip or lift. The box rim rocks very slightly as the product is pulled out quickly, and settles once the hands have gone.

[12] AUDIO - DRY DOCUMENTARY AUDIO ONLY. The track contains exactly two things and nothing else: cardboard flaps creasing and fingers moving on the carton. Total silence apart from those. NO MUSIC, NO SONG, NO SCORE, NO SOUNDTRACK, NO INSTRUMENTS, NO VOICE.

[13] POSITIVE LOCKS - the lid is never lifted off, never removed, never carried aside, never set down. THE BOX never leaves the table. Exactly two hands. The top face of THE PROJECTOR is BLACK. The lift out of the box is fast. THE PROJECTOR exits the top of frame and the last frame shows only the open box on the table.
BANNED: any music, any song, any score, any soundtrack; the product still held in frame at 4.0s; the hands stopping, hovering, settling or presenting the product; the camera tilting or panning up to follow the product; slow motion; a slow or hesitant lift; an all-white product top, a lens on the front, a swivel camera head, a third hand, the candle or the holly disappearing, the box vanishing, a second box, a cut, subtitles, on-screen text.

det.label: Clip prompt · v1_c03_g2.mp4
det.meta: seedance_2_5 · 720p · 4 s · 9:16 · audio on · job eb75d3ea
det.text:
AUDIO RULE - HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ THIS FIRST: this clip has NO MUSIC OF ANY KIND. No background song, no soundtrack, no score, no melody, no instruments, no singing, no humming, no jingle, no Christmas song, no festive music bed, no ambient musical pad, no strings, no piano, no bells used as music. The audio track contains ONLY real natural sound recorded in that room. If any music appears anywhere in the 4 seconds the clip is wrong.

NATURALNESS RULE - SECOND MOST IMPORTANT: these are REAL HUMAN HANDS, not a robot arm and not a CGI animation. Human hands are never perfectly steady and never move on a perfectly straight mechanical line. Throughout the whole descent the hands carry a small living tremor, the wrists flex slightly, the fingers re-seat their grip once, and the object drifts a few millimetres off true as a real person would let it. The descent slows naturally as it nears the marble the way a person eases something down, instead of arriving at constant speed. Nothing about this movement may look mechanical, robotic, motorised, gliding, floating, animated or rigged.

TASK: image-to-video. The start image is frame 0.0s. Hold its kitchen, counter, hands and lighting exactly.

[1] SUMMARY
First-person POV: two real hands hold the white projector high above a marble kitchen counter, then lower it and set it down naturally. Locked POV. 4 seconds, one take.

[2] GLOBAL STYLE
Real handheld phone POV, warm modern kitchen light, extremely sharp and clean, correctly exposed. Very slight handheld drift. Documentary realism. No cinematic grade, no grain, no slow motion.

[3] ASSET ROLES
The start image controls the kitchen, the counter, the hands and the product. It is the only authority on the scene.

[4] OBJECTS
THE PROJECTOR - a matte-white dome-shaped body on a separate white four-legged splayed stand. Set into the top of the dome is a flat circular BLACK perforated mesh disc. The top face is BLACK and stays black for every frame. No front lens, no camera head, no swivel.
THE HANDS - exactly two real human hands holding THE PROJECTOR, entering from the bottom of frame.

[5] LOCATION - hold every one of these, they exist in the start image and must survive to the last frame: a white marble countertop with grey veining fills the lower half of frame and stays there for the whole clip; behind it a warm modern kitchen with tall matte beige-taupe cabinets, a stainless wall oven set into the cabinet run on the left, warm under-cabinet light, and a green garland with small warm fairy lights along the top of the cabinets. The kitchen stays soft and out of focus. Do not remove the countertop. Do not replace the kitchen with a plain wall, a studio backdrop or a dark room.

[6] FIRST FRAME - exactly the start image: THE HANDS holding THE PROJECTOR in the air above the marble counter.

[7] TIMELINE
0.0-0.8s - camera locked. THE HANDS raise THE PROJECTOR upward away from the marble until the bottom of the stand is roughly 35 cm above the counter, with a natural small overshoot and correction at the top of the lift. THE PROJECTOR now sits high in the upper half of frame with a large clear gap of air between the stand feet and the marble. THE PROJECTOR STARTS HIGH - this gap is what the rest of the clip travels through.
0.8-1.2s - the hands pause for a beat and the fingers re-seat their grip on the sides of the dome, the way a person adjusts their hold before setting something down.
1.2-3.0s - THE HANDS lower THE PROJECTOR down through that gap toward the marble in one continuous human descent, carrying a small natural tremor, easing slower and slower as the feet approach the stone.
3.0-3.4s - the four feet of the stand touch the marble; the hands relax their pressure and the object settles flat with a tiny real-world adjustment.
3.4-4.0s - THE HANDS open, release THE PROJECTOR and withdraw downward out of frame, leaving THE PROJECTOR standing alone on the counter.

[9] CAMERA AND OPTICS - one static POV looking down at the counter, vertical 9:16, normal wide-angle phone lens, very slight handheld drift only. No push-in, no orbit, no zoom, no tilt, no cut. Normal wide-angle only - no fisheye, no barrel distortion, no curved cabinet lines.

[10] LIGHTING - warm under-cabinet light plus soft daylight, unchanged for the whole clip.

[11] PHYSICS - THE PROJECTOR is a solid rigid object with real weight and the hands are visibly carrying that weight. It stays essentially upright but is allowed the tiny tilts a real hand-held object has. The marble is hard: contact is a small firm settle. The fingertips whiten very slightly where they press the dome.

RULE ZERO - THE ONLY THING THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS CLIP IS USABLE. READ THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE.
The Christmas light pattern on the walls and on the ceiling MUST BE MOVING, hard and fast, in every single frame. This is the entire purpose of the clip. Every previous attempt failed for exactly one reason: the pattern sat still like wallpaper. If the pattern is still, the clip is worthless.

@Video 1 IS THE MOTION AUTHORITY. It is real footage of this exact projector running. Copy the MOVEMENT of the projected light from @Video 1: its speed, its direction, its restlessness, the way the whole field of glowing shapes slides and swarms across the plaster without ever pausing. Match that amount of movement or exceed it.
TAKE NOTHING ELSE FROM @Video 1 - not its room, not its furniture, not its people, not its framing, not its colours, not its camera move, not its lighting. @Video 1 is completely silent and has no audio track at all; import no sound whatsoever from it. It is a MOVEMENT REFERENCE ONLY.

WHAT THE LIGHT DOES, described so it cannot be mistaken for a texture:
- The whole field of glowing shapes SLIDES BODILY across the wall and across the ceiling, the way light from a spinning projector head sweeps a room. It never locks onto the plaster.
- On top of that sliding, individual shapes POUR DOWNWARD like heavy snowfall filmed through a window at night, and each one spins slowly as it goes and drags a faint soft trail.
- SPEED: a single shape crosses the full height of the wall in ABOUT ONE SECOND. That is fast. A viewer must see it moving within the first quarter second of the clip.
- THE TEST: take any two frames a third of a second apart and lay them on top of each other. NOT ONE glowing shape is in the same place. Not one. If any shape has stayed put, the clip is wrong.
- The moving light also pours down over the tree, the sofa, the floor and across both children's faces and pyjamas as it passes over them, so the brightness on everything in the room is changing continuously.
- THE START IMAGE IS A SINGLE PAUSED FRAME of this moving light. At 0.0s the video RESUMES and the light instantly goes back to sweeping and pouring and never stops - not for one frame, not at the beginning and not at the end.
- "Hold the start image" applies to the ROOM: its walls, doors, furniture, people, colours and framing. It does NOT apply to the light pattern. The light pattern must leave its starting position immediately.

IMAGE QUALITY RULE - SECOND MOST IMPORTANT. The finished clip must look at least as sharp and as clean as the start image. Do not soften it, do not smear it, do not repaint it, do not re-imagine it. Hold the exact sharpness, exposure, contrast and fine detail of the start image: the wood grain of the floor, the panel edges and painted sheen of the white door, the brass of the round knob, the skin texture and fine hairs of the bare forearm, the individual leaves of the green wreath and its red bow. Crisp modern phone footage, in focus from the first frame to the last. BANNED: blur, soft focus, haze, motion smear on objects that are not moving, mushy low-detail surfaces, plastic or waxy skin, a repainted or re-imagined door or hallway, colour shift, washed-out or muddy exposure, upscaling artefacts, a dreamy or filtered look.

AUDIO RULE - THIRD MOST IMPORTANT: this clip has NO MUSIC OF ANY KIND. No background song, no soundtrack, no score, no melody, no instruments, no singing, no humming, no jingle, no Christmas song, no festive music bed, no ambient musical pad, no strings, no piano, no bells used as music. The audio track contains ONLY real natural sound recorded in that room. If any music appears anywhere in the 4 seconds the clip is wrong.

CHILDREN MOTION RULE: the children are ALREADY in full motion at the very first frame they appear. Never standing still, never posed, never frozen. They run, spin, jump and laugh continuously, with a clearly different whole-body pose every half second - arms, legs, heads and faces all changing. Eyes wide, mouths open laughing and shouting. Real children filmed on a phone, not a photograph coming to life.

TASK: image-to-video. The start image is frame 0.0s. Hold its door, hallway, forearm, geometry and materials exactly - but NOT its stillness and NOT the position of its light pattern.

[1] SUMMARY
First-person POV: a hand opens a door and walks into a Christmas living room where light is sweeping and pouring down every wall and the ceiling, two children running and laughing inside; the camera pushes in and tilts up. 4 seconds, one continuous take.

[2] GLOBAL STYLE
Real handheld phone POV walking forward. Warm dim hallway opening into a room lit only by the moving projection. Sharp, clean, correctly exposed, natural handheld bounce. Documentary realism. No cinematic grade, no grain, no slow motion.

[3] ASSET ROLES
The start image controls frame 0.0s: the closed white panelled door, the brass round knob, the bare right forearm, the warm dim hallway, the wood floor and the green wreath with the red bow on the right-hand wall.
@Image 1 controls ONLY what is inside the room once the door is open: the room layout, the tall decorated Christmas tree, the cream sofa, the tall windows, the two children and their red-and-white Fair Isle pyjamas, and the COLOUR and STYLE of the Christmas shapes.
@Video 1 controls ONLY how the projected light MOVES. Nothing else.
Both images are photographs - copy their look, NEVER their stillness.

[4] CHARACTERS
THE BOY - red-and-white Fair Isle pyjamas, centre of the room, running and jumping, mouth wide open laughing.
THE GIRL - matching red-and-white Fair Isle pyjamas, behind him and to his left, spinning and running, laughing.
COUNT LOCK: exactly two children. No adults, no third child, no pets.

[5] LOCATION - a warm double-height living room: tall decorated Christmas tree centre, cream sofa with a knit throw right, tall windows left, patterned rug, presents under the tree. Sweeping, pouring light covers every wall AND the whole ceiling. Its coverage is dense but uneven and constantly changing, because it is moving - that is correct and expected.

[6] FIRST FRAME - exactly the start image: the door CLOSED, no light at its edge, the bare right forearm reaching to the brass knob.

[7] TIMELINE - the light is sweeping and pouring in every single beat
0.0-1.0s - the camera is the person's own eyes. THE RIGHT HAND grips the brass knob, turns it and pushes; the door cracks open and a narrow vertical slice of coloured light appears along the opening edge. Through that slice, glowing shapes are clearly seen racing downward and sideways past the gap.
1.0-2.0s - the door swings inward and wide; the camera steps forward through the doorway. Light is sweeping across the far wall and the tree and raining down over the floor ahead and over the camera's own path.
2.0-3.0s - the camera is fully inside the room. THE BOY is already running across the middle of the room, arms out, mouth wide open laughing, and leaps onto the sofa cushion. THE GIRL spins on the rug behind him to the left, hair flying, laughing and shouting. Behind and around them the field of light keeps sliding and pouring down every wall and across both children, shapes visibly travelling from the top of frame towards the bottom.
3.0-4.0s - the camera keeps moving forward and TILTS UP, bringing the ceiling into the top of frame. The light is sweeping and pouring across the entire ceiling too, streaming towards the far end of the room. THE BOY jumps again with both arms straight up; THE GIRL is still turning below.

[8] CAMERA AND OPTICS - one continuous handheld POV walk, vertical 9:16, normal wide-angle phone lens, eye height. Two movements only: the forward walk from 1.0s and the upward tilt from 3.0s. No cut, no zoom, no orbit. Normal wide-angle only - no fisheye, no barrel distortion, no curved walls. The camera IS the person's eyes: no phone, screen, hand, fingers, thumb or device in the lower part of frame after 1.0s.

[9] LIGHTING - the hallway is warm and dim; the room is dim with the moving projection as the only bright light source. Because the shapes are sweeping and pouring, the bright and dark areas on the walls, the furniture and the children change continuously. Do not flood the room with one flat colour.

[10] PHYSICS - the door swings on its hinges, never lifted off or removed. The sofa cushion compresses when THE BOY lands. Pyjamas and hair swing and lift with their motion.

[11] AUDIO - DRY DOCUMENTARY AUDIO ONLY. Exactly three things and nothing else: the door handle and the door swinging, children laughing and squealing, and quiet room tone. NO MUSIC, NO SONG, NO SCORE, NO SOUNDTRACK, NO INSTRUMENTS.

det.text:
SUMMARY: a boy bounces on his bed in a Christmas bedroom at night while an animated snowfall plays across the wall behind him and the whole ceiling, thrown there by a projector standing on the floor. 4 seconds, one continuous handheld phone take, vertical.

GLOBAL STYLE: crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed. Sharp and in focus from the first frame to the last, at least as sharp as the start image. No blur, no haze, no soft focus.

ASSET ROLES: @Image 1 is frame 0.0s and controls the bedroom, the bed, THE BOY and the colour.

SUBJECTS:
THE BOY - exactly one child in red-and-white Fair Isle pyjamas, standing on the bed.
THE PROJECTOR - a small Christmas projector switched on and running on the bedroom floor, out of shot. Its lens throws one wide cone of coloured light across the room. Everything glowing on the plaster is that cone landing.
THE SCREEN - the wall behind the bed and the whole ceiling together, catching that cone as one continuous surface. The light lands directly on bare plaster and wraps around the corner where wall meets ceiling. No rectangle, no visible screen edge, no television.

WHAT IS PLAYING ON THE SCREEN - this is the point of the clip:
A looping snowfall animation is PLAYING on THE SCREEN for all four seconds, exactly the way a film plays on a cinema screen: the screen itself is fixed to the plaster and holds perfectly still, while the picture playing on it is in constant motion. The animation is a night snowfall - hundreds of small glowing six-point snowflakes and round dots in red, green, blue, gold and white, all falling.
Track these three so the fall is unmistakable:
FLAKE A - a large white six-point flake that begins just above the headboard on the left of the wall. It falls steadily and drifts slightly right, passing the middle of the wall at 2.0s, and fades out low near the skirting board at 4.0s.
FLAKE B - a red flake on the ceiling directly above the headboard. It travels across the ceiling toward the far corner, ending about a third of the way across at 4.0s.
FLAKE C - a small gold dot on the right of the wall. It falls the full height of the wall in the first two seconds, fades out at the bottom, and a fresh gold dot fades in high near the ceiling and falls the same path again.
Every other flake behaves like these three: roughly a quarter of the wall's height every second, downward with a slight sideways drift, each one turning slowly on its own centre and breathing brighter and dimmer on its own timing, each cycling slowly through red, green, blue and gold. Density stays even because a flake fading out at the bottom is matched by one fading in at the top.
Because the wall and the ceiling are one screen fed by one projector lens, the snowfall on the ceiling plays at the same moment and at the same speed as the snowfall on the wall.
The start image is one paused frame of this animation. At 0.0s the projector un-pauses and the snowfall plays. Matching the start image applies to the bedroom, the bed, THE BOY and the colours, not to where any individual flake sits.

TIMELINE:
0.0-1.5s THE BOY bends his knees and pushes off the mattress; both feet leave the duvet, arms swinging up over his head, mouth open laughing. The mattress compresses and springs back.
1.5-2.5s He lands on both feet and drives straight into a second, higher jump, knees tucking.
2.5-4.0s The camera tilts up in one slow smooth move until the ceiling fills the upper half of the frame. THE BOY stays low in frame, still bouncing.

AUDIO: room tone, mattress springs compressing on each landing, bedding rustling, a boy laughing. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS: real-time motion at normal speed - a real boy jumping at real speed and landing with real weight. Exactly one child. One continuous take. The camera makes one move only, a tilt up. THE SCREEN stays bolted to the plaster while the snowfall plays across it. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.

DO NOT INCLUDE: slow motion; a frozen pattern; the whole pattern turning or sliding as one sheet; any music; the projector unit in shot; a second child; a cut; on-screen text.

The field as a whole is ANCHORED. It does not rotate, spin, swing, sweep sideways or slide across the room as one sheet. Its outer boundary stays where it is.

- each flake DRIFTS slowly downward and slightly sideways, about one flake-width every half second, the way real snow falls past a window at night;

- each flake breathes, brightening and dimming on its own timing, never all together;
- each flake's colour cycles slowly through red, green, blue and gold.
Every wall and the ceiling are lit by the SAME projector, so they are one field and behave identically at the same moment. Whatever the flakes on the walls are doing, the flakes on the ceiling are doing at the same instant, at the same speed.
Nothing is painted, printed or stencilled on the plaster. The start image is one paused frame of this; at 0.0s it un-pauses. Matching the start image applies to the room, the furniture, the children and the colours, not to where any individual flake sits.

FREEZE MEANS FREEZE: no drift, no wobble, no micro-motion, no push-in, no handheld shake, no reframe, no zoom, no cut. Normal wide-angle only - no fisheye, no barrel distortion.

[10] LIGHTING - warm white under-cabinet kitchen light for the whole clip; the only lighting change is the RED light emitted by THE PROJECTOR itself from 1.0s onward. The red light is a local glow on the product and the marble immediately around it - it does not repaint the whole kitchen.

[11] PHYSICS - THE PROJECTOR is a rigid object bolted to the spot; it does not shift, rock, rotate or lift when the cable is pushed in. The cable is flexible and bends slightly as it seats.

[12] AUDIO - natural room sound only: a small plastic click as the connector seats. No music, no speech, no score.

[13] POSITIVE LOCKS - the light is RED and only RED. The top face of THE PROJECTOR is BLACK and the red starfield appears ON that black disc. The countertop and the kitchen behind it are visible in every single frame. Exactly two hands. The camera never moves.
BANNED: blue light, white light, green light, amber light, multicoloured or rainbow light; a beam projected onto the ceiling or the walls; the product moving, lifting or rotating; the camera moving in any way; an all-white top face; the countertop or the kitchen disappearing; a third hand; a cut; subtitles; on-screen text; music.

det.text:
Recreate @Image 1 with two changes.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo, the same dim hallway, the same antique brass round doorknob in the same place, the same small pine wreath with the red velvet bow hung on the door, the same oak floorboards, the same woman's forearm entering from the lower right with the thin gold bangle and cream sleeve, her hand closed around the knob, the same camera position and camera height, the same warm low-key evening light.

CHANGE 1 - THE DOOR. It is no longer a white panelled door. It is now a solid dark-stained oak plank door: vertical tongue-and-groove boards with visible grain and clear seams between them, a matte deep walnut finish, two slim black iron strap hinges on the left edge, set in a plain painted cream frame. Same size, same position in frame, same flat-on angle as @Image 1.

CHANGE 2 - the door is FULLY CLOSED and flush in its frame. There is NO gap at the edge of the door and absolutely NO light spilling out - no rainbow strip, no coloured glow, no bright line, no glare anywhere along the door edge, the jamb, the threshold or the floor. The seam between door and frame is a plain dark shadow line only. Nothing behind the door is visible or lit.

SHARPNESS - this frame must be noticeably sharper than @Image 1, which was too soft. Tack sharp edge to edge: every plank seam and every grain line in the oak, the machined edge and the patina of the brass knob, the individual needles of the pine wreath and the woven nap of the red velvet bow, the skin texture and fine hairs on the forearm, the grain of the floorboards. Extremely high quality, perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, deep clean shadows that still hold detail, hyper realistic. BANNED: blur, soft focus, haze, mushy low-detail surfaces, waxy skin, a dreamy or filtered look, motion blur, noise, upscaling artefacts.

Natural handheld UGC look, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, photorealistic, zero motion blur, no CGI look.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

det.meta: seedance_2_5 · 720p · 5 s · 9:16 · audio on · job a2b3eb94
det.text:
SUMMARY: a hand opens a dark wooden door onto a Christmas cabin living room where a projected snow-village picture is PLAYING across the back wall and the whole sloping timber ceiling, two children watching it; the camera steps in and tilts up. 5 seconds, one continuous handheld phone take, vertical.

GLOBAL STYLE: crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed. Sharp and in focus from the first frame to the last, at least as sharp as the start image. No blur, no haze, no soft focus, no washed-out exposure, no colour shift.

ASSET ROLES: the start image is frame 0.0s and controls the closed dark-stained vertical-plank door, the brass round knob, the bare right forearm, the white painted jamb on the left, the dark wood floor and the green wreath with the red bow at the right edge. @Image 1 controls what is inside the room once the door is open: the cabin, the sloping honey-pine ceiling with its dark rafters and ridge beam, the lit Christmas tree on the left, the stone fireplace with stockings on the right, the sofa with the red plaid blanket, the teddy bear on the floor, the two children, and the colour and content of the projected picture. Both images are photographs - copy their look, never their stillness.

SUBJECTS:
THE CHILDREN - exactly two, in pink-and-white striped pyjamas, standing on the wooden floor with their backs to camera facing the wall, one further left and back, one centre and nearer. No third child, no adult, no pet.
THE SOFA - a brown leather sofa standing in the lower right of frame with a red plaid blanket thrown over its back and a cushion on its seat, exactly as in @Image 1. It is close enough for a small child to reach in three steps. It stays exactly where it is for the whole clip - it never slides, never tips, never turns and the blanket stays on it.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running on the floor, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the back wall and both slopes of the ceiling. Everything glowing on the timber and the plaster is that one cone landing.
THE PICTURE - the animated snow-village scene that cone is playing: snow-covered gabled cottages with lit windows and a church steeple low on the back wall, fir trees and a little footbridge between them, chimney plumes above the roofs, ribbons of aurora arching over the village and packed across both ceiling slopes, a sleigh drawn by eight reindeer keystoned across the ceiling, a big ivory moon on the stone chimney breast at the right, a dense field of gold stars of many sizes, a large rayed north star near the ridge beam, long-tailed shooting stars, large gold and cream six-point snowflakes, and a heavy fall of small points of light.

HOW THE PICTURE BEHAVES - THIS IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE CLIP. In every previous attempt the picture sat dead still like printed wallpaper and the clip was worthless. THE PICTURE IS A FILM PLAYING ON A CINEMA SCREEN: the screen is the timber and the plaster and holds perfectly still, while everything inside the picture is in constant motion for all five seconds. The start image is one paused frame of that film; at 0.0s it un-pauses. Matching @Image 1 applies to the cabin, the furniture, the children and the colours, not to where any element of the picture sits.
THE PICTURE AS A WHOLE IS ANCHORED. It does not rotate, spin, swing, sweep sideways or slide across the room as one sheet. Its outer boundary stays where it is. The motion lives INSIDE it, element by element:
- THE CHIMNEY SMOKE - every cottage chimney is smoking. Each plume climbs upward out of its chimney pot, leaning slightly to the right, rising about one cottage-roof height every second, widening and thinning as it climbs and fading out before it reaches the aurora, while a fresh plume forms at the pot behind it. The plumes are never a fixed painted shape.
- THE AURORA - each ribbon ripples ALONG ITS OWN LENGTH, a slow travelling wave running from one end of the ribbon to the other, about a third of the ribbon's length every second, the ribbon swelling brighter and thinner as the wave passes and its lower fringe combing and re-forming. Each ribbon's overall arc stays where it is on the timber; the wave inside it travels. Every ribbon on both ceiling slopes is doing this at the same time.
- THE SLEIGH AND THE EIGHT REINDEER - they are FLYING. The team travels steadily across the ceiling away from where it sits in the start image, toward the ridge beam, covering about a fifth of the ceiling's width every second, so by 5.0s it has crossed most of the way. The reindeer's legs gallop, their heads nod, the sleigh rocks gently behind them, and the whole team rises and dips a little as it goes.
- THE SNOWFLAKES AND THE POINTS OF LIGHT - each one drifts downward and slightly sideways about a quarter of the wall's height every second, the way snow falls past a window at night. Each turns slowly on its own centre as it drifts and breathes brighter and dimmer on its own timing. One that reaches the floor line fades out there while a fresh one fades in high near the ridge, so the density holds even.
- THE SHOOTING STARS - each one streaks across its own patch of ceiling in about half a second, dragging a long fading tail, and is gone; another starts somewhere else. At least five of them cross in the five seconds.
- THE STAR FIELD AND THE NORTH STAR - the small gold stars hold their places and twinkle, each brightening and dimming on its own timing, never all together. The rayed north star pulses slowly and its rays lengthen and shorten.
- THE MOON - the moon is the ONE element that holds its position. It stays exactly where it is on the stone chimney breast for the whole clip and only brightens and dims very slightly. Nothing else in the picture is allowed to hold still.
Because the back wall and both ceiling slopes are lit by the SAME projector, they are one picture and behave identically at the same instant. Whatever the flakes, the aurora and the stars on the wall are doing, the flakes, the aurora and the stars on the ceiling are doing at the same moment and at the same speed. There is never a still ceiling above a moving wall. Nothing is painted, printed or stencilled on the timber.
The projected picture falls only on the back wall and the ceiling. The wooden floor carries only a soft warm spill of that light, never the pattern itself.

CHILDREN MOTION RULE: THE CHILDREN are already moving the moment they appear and never stand still, and neither of them ever faces the camera - their backs are to it, they are watching the picture on the wall and the ceiling. The camera never sees either child's face at any moment: only the backs of their heads and their backs. The nearer child in particular never turns toward the lens, never pivots to face the room, and never ends up chest-on to camera.
THE NEARER CHILD DOES ONE THING AND IT IS THE ONLY THING HE DOES: he GETS ONTO THE SOFA AND BOUNCES ON IT. This is the single most important action in the clip and it is the thing every previous attempt failed: he wandered around the floorboards and never got onto the sofa at all. He walks to the sofa, he climbs up onto the seat cushion, he bounces there - in that order, each part clearly readable, at real child speed with real weight.
THE HARD DEADLINE: BY 2.8s BOTH OF HIS BARE FEET ARE ON THE SOFA'S SEAT CUSHION AND HE IS STANDING ON THE SOFA. From 2.8s to the last frame he is on the sofa and nowhere else - he does not get back down, does not step onto the floor again, does not wander back out into the middle of the room, and the floorboards under him are empty for the rest of the clip. If he is still on the floor after 2.8s the clip is wrong.
He walks STRAIGHT to the sofa on the shortest line and does not detour, drift, circle, turn back or stop on the way. He does not stay standing on the floor, he does not bounce up and down on the spot on the floorboards, he does not point at anything. He reaches the sofa at its NEAR END and steps up onto the SEAT CUSHION from the front of the sofa; he never climbs over the sofa's back rail, never kneels on the back rail, never puts a hand or a knee on top of the back, and never stands on the rolled arm or on the back. Once he is up he is standing on the cushion with his back to camera, high enough that his whole body from the knees up is clearly above the sofa's back rail.

HOW THE BOUNCE LOOKS. It must look like a real small child bouncing on a soft cushion in bare feet. THREE full bounces between 2.8s and 5.0s, roughly half a second each, and nothing held still between them. One bounce is: he sinks into a deep crouch first - knees fold, his bottom drops toward his heels, his torso drops several centimetres and tips forward, both arms swing DOWN and back - then he drives up, his legs straighten, both feet leave the cushion by a hand's width, his torso and head rise clearly, both arms swing UP past his ears and his hair lifts; then he comes down, his feet press into the cushion, his knees fold to absorb the landing and his whole body compresses straight into the next crouch. His head visibly rises and falls with every bounce. The cushion dents under his feet as he lands and springs back as he leaves it, the seat gives under his weight, the red plaid blanket on the back rail shivers and shifts a little with each landing, and he rocks slightly off-balance on the soft cushion and corrects it with his arms - nothing about him is rigid or symmetrical or held. The three bounces are not identical: each is a little higher than the last and lands slightly further along the cushion. His arms are never held out stiff and still, he is never posed, and he is never motionless on the sofa for even a quarter of a second.
THE FURTHER CHILD keeps turning slowly on the spot where she is, arms out, head tipped back at the ceiling. A clearly different whole-body pose every half second for both of them.

DOOR GAP RULE - THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN THIS PROMPT: absolutely nothing is animated on, in or beside the doorway. The vertical gap that opens between the door's opening edge and the white painted jamb is EMPTY - it shows only the plain lit room behind it. In that gap, and on the door's opening edge, on the door face, on the white jamb and on the architrave, there are at NO moment any particles, any falling snow, any flakes, any glitter, any sparkles, any specks, any light points, any twinkles, any shimmer, any streaks, any dust motes, any bloom, any glowing strip, any coloured edge and any rainbow fringe. Nothing is emitted from the gap, nothing drifts down it, nothing floats in it, nothing rises out of it. No vertical column or line of light or particles appears anywhere along the opening. The door edge and the jamb stay plain painted white wood for every single frame, exactly as they are in the start image. The projected snow and the projected picture exist ONLY on the back wall and the sloping ceiling deep inside the room and never appear on, over, across, in front of or beside the doorway, the door, the jamb or the gap. The light coming through the gap is a plain flat warm wash on the floor with no texture and no moving detail in it.

TIMELINE:
0.0-1.0s the camera is the person's own eyes and holds still. The bare right hand grips the brass knob, turns it and pushes; the door cracks open and a narrow vertical slice of the room appears along the opening edge. Through that slice the far wall of the room is visible, lit and in colour. Nothing is rendered inside the gap itself and nothing moves in it.
1.0-2.0s the door swings inward and wide and the person filming takes one clear step forward through the doorway. The cabin opens up ahead: the tree on the left, the fireplace on the right, the village playing across the back wall. THE NEARER CHILD is ALREADY WALKING TOWARD THE SOFA from the very first frame he is visible - four quick barefoot steps on a straight line to his right across the floorboards, his back to camera the whole way, and he is standing at the near end of the sofa with a hand on its seat by 2.0s. He does not pause, does not turn around and does not look back at the camera on the way.
2.0-2.8s the camera holds still in the closer position and this beat contains ONE action only: THE NEARER CHILD CLIMBS ONTO THE SOFA. From the front of the sofa's near end he lifts one bare foot up onto the SEAT CUSHION, rolls his weight over it, brings the other foot up beside it and straightens to standing on the cushion with his back to camera, his whole body from the knees up clearly above the back rail. Nothing else happens to him in this beat - he does not walk, does not turn, does not stop. By 2.8s he is standing on the cushion. The further child turns on the spot with her arms out. The smoke climbs, the aurora ripples, the reindeer gallop on across the ceiling, the flakes keep falling.
2.8-5.0s the camera tilts up in one slow smooth move until the sloping timber ceiling fills the upper half of the frame, the aurora rippling along both slopes and the sleigh still flying across it. THE NEARER CHILD BOUNCES ON THE SEAT CUSHION for this entire beat - crouch, spring up with both feet off the cushion and both arms swinging up past his ears, land, fold straight into the next crouch and spring again, and again - three full bounces filling this whole beat with no still moment anywhere between them, facing the wall, landing back on the same cushion each time. He is on the sofa for every frame of this beat and the floor where he used to stand is empty. The further child keeps turning on the floor. The children stay low in frame and keep moving.

AUDIO: room tone, two children laughing and squealing, bare feet on a wooden floor, the soft click of a door latch and the door swinging. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS: real-time motion at normal speed throughout - real children moving at real speed with real weight, a real door swinging at real speed. The nearer child is standing on the sofa's seat cushion by 2.8s and is on the sofa for every frame from 2.8s to the end, still mid-bounce in the last frame. His feet leave the ground only once he is standing on the cushion. His knees bend before every rise and fold again on every landing, and his head, hair and arms all move with each bounce. Both children have their backs to the camera for every frame. Exactly two children. One continuous take with no cut. The camera makes one move per beat and no more. The picture's outer boundary holds still while every element inside it moves. Wall and ceiling always move together. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.

DO NOT INCLUDE: a child facing the camera; a child's face visible at any moment; the nearer child turning toward the lens; a child standing rooted on the floorboards; a child hopping up and down on the spot on the floor; the nearer child never reaching the sofa; the nearer child still on the floor after 2.8s; the nearer child standing in the middle of the room in the last second; the nearer child walking toward the sofa and then veering away from it; the nearer child stopping, pausing or turning back on his way to the sofa; the nearer child getting back down off the sofa; a child jumping off the sofa, jumping onto the floor, falling, tumbling or landing on the boards; a child climbing the sofa back or the arm; a hand or a knee on the sofa's back rail; a child hauling herself over the back of the sofa; feet on the sofa arm; a child standing motionless on the sofa; a child standing on the sofa with her arms held out stiff and still; a posed, stiff or mannequin-like stance; a child rising off the cushion without bending her knees first; feet that stay glued to the cushion; a body that moves up and down as one rigid piece; two identical repeated bounces; a cushion that does not dent under her feet; the sofa sliding, tipping or turning; the blanket falling off the sofa; a frozen or still pattern; chimneys that are not smoking; an aurora that sits still; a sleigh and reindeer parked in one place; flakes that only twinkle without travelling; a still ceiling above a moving wall; the whole picture rotating, spinning, sweeping or sliding as one sheet; slow motion; floating or weightless movement; any music; a glowing strip, sparkle, glitter, shimmer, twinkle, bloom or rainbow fringe on the door edge, the door face, the jamb, the architrave or the frame; snow, flakes, particles, specks, light points, streaks or any moving detail inside the door gap or along the opening edge; a vertical column or line of particles or light down the gap; anything emitted from, drifting down or floating in the gap; the projected pattern appearing on or beside the doorway; the projected pattern lying on the floor; the projector unit in shot; a third child; an adult; blur; a cut; on-screen text; subtitles.

det.html:
Mechanics, measured

4.05 s · 24 fps · 720×1280 · 0 cuts. Interframe difference across the top of frame is 12.46 against 0.35 on the deliberately static C04 — the projected field is moving as hard as it did in take 1 (13.32). Child motion checked at 1.8 / 2.2 / 2.6 / 2.9 / 3.05 / 3.2 / 3.5 / 3.8 / 3.95 s: she walks right with her back to camera, reaches the sofa at ~2.2 s, climbs on at ~2.6 s and bounces with her arms up from ~3.0 s to the last frame. Neither child faces the lens at any point.

Review note

New projection, walls and ceiling only. It is one readable Christmas night scene now instead of a field of floating icons: a snow-covered village low on the pine walls, aurora ribbons climbing off the walls onto the ceiling, Santa's sleigh and eight reindeer across the sloped ceiling with a light trail, a big ivory moon by the fireplace, and a heavy fall of light points over all of it. The floor, the cowhide rug, the sofa and the gifts carry no projected shapes at all — only warm spill. On "distopyan": what makes your three references read that way is the cold cyan-violet vortex, so the prompt bans cyan, teal, electric blue, violet and grey outright and bans outer space, nebula, galaxy, spiral vortex, tunnel by name. The structure is theirs, the palette is warm gold, cream, red, emerald and rose. Those screenshots are saved as ref12–ref14 but were deliberately not attached — attaching them would have imported the look you rejected. Frame 1 is untouched as you instructed, so it is still dark with the wreath sliding off the right edge. Take 3 — the ceiling. On take 2 the aurora rendered as hard-edged opaque vertical curtains that ignored the slope, hid the pine boards and swallowed the rafters and the ridge beam, so the ceiling read as a flat backdrop with a sticker on it. Three clauses inside CHANGE 2 were edited and nothing else: the aurora now lies along the slope and kinks at the ridge, the sleigh is keystoned and foreshortens towards it, and a new block states that the light is translucent with the planks, grain, rafters and ridge visible through it, that the beams stay darker and cut their own shadow lines, and that it falls off with distance so the corners fade to bare pine. Everything you approved is byte-identical. Take 4 — and the lesson. Take 3 kept the room paragraph byte-identical and the room still came out different, because re-running an edited text prompt regenerates the whole picture. When one region of an approved frame is wrong the job is an image edit, not a text re-roll: take 4 attaches v2_c05_r2.png itself, names what must not move, and names the ceiling as the single change. Bottom half is the same frame now — same tree, sofa, fireplace, floor and both children in the same pyjamas and poses — with the fixed ceiling above it. Take 5 — density. Take 4's ceiling was physically right but thin, so a lot of bare pine showed between the shapes. Same method again — an image edit, this time of v2_c05_r4.png, because its room and its light-on-timber behaviour both had to survive. Seven layers were named: five or six overlapping aurora bands, hundreds of gold stars at many sizes, a big rayed north star near the ridge, four or five long-tailed shooting stars, large gold and cream six-point snowflakes, wisps of glowing cloud, and a much heavier fall of light points — with the sleigh and the eight reindeer pinned where they already were, the warm-palette bans kept, and r4's translucency / keystone / falloff block carried over so packing the ceiling full could not undo the take-4 fix. The static-projection problem, addressed. Your note was that the wall and ceiling animations did not move in video 1. No video reference here — you banned those on C5/C6/C7. Instead the projection is now a named subject broken into individually tracked elements, each with a start point, a path, a stated rate and an end point: chimney smoke rising one cottage-roof height per second and leaning right, the aurora rippling along its own length a third of its length per second with the arc itself staying put, the sleigh and eight reindeer flying a fifth of the ceiling's width per second with galloping legs and a rocking sleigh, flakes drifting a quarter of the wall's height per second and turning on their own centres, at least four shooting stars, and a twinkling star field. The device that carries it is a single line: the timber and plaster are a cinema screen holding still, and the start image is one paused frame of the film playing on it. The moon is named as the one element allowed to hold its position, which gives the model a contrast and makes everything else's motion legible. The wall and the ceiling are stated to be one projector and therefore one field moving at the same instant at the same speed — video 1 moved the wall and left the ceiling still. The door-edge rainbow sparkle strip is banned by name. Take 1 rejected — the near kid. Your note: she faces the camera and looks stuck there jumping; you wanted her to go to the couch and jump on it. Fixed with six surgical edits and nothing else: THE SOFA is now a named subject (the brown leather sofa with the red plaid blanket that is already in v2_c05_r5.png, three steps away, immovable) so the thing she jumps on exists in the scene instead of popping in; the children motion rule says neither child ever faces the lens and the nearer one does exactly one thing in order — walks, climbs, bounces; the three beats from 1.0 s on carry those three actions with time ranges; and the locks and ban list close off facing the camera, standing rooted, hopping on the spot on the floor and never reaching the sofa. The whole projection block, all six per-element bullets, the camera moves, the door-edge rule and the sharpness locks are byte-identical to take 1. One flag rather than a re-roll: from ~3.2 s she is bouncing on the rolled back of the sofa rather than the seat cushion. It reads fine, but it is not literally what the prompt asked for.

det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, light quality and style in a completely different room, with a different child and a much bigger projection. Wholesome family Christmas scene, a child at home with his family at Christmas.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same framing that shows the wall behind the bed and the ceiling above it both in shot, and the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself.

CHANGE 1 - THE CHILD. A different child from @Image 1: a boy of about eight with short dark curly hair, fully dressed for winter in a warm red-and-white knitted Christmas jumper, matching knitted lounge trousers and thick knitted socks. He is standing up on top of the bed, knees bent and both arms raised out to his sides, caught mid-bounce, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling, laughing. Clearly standing on top of the bed, not sitting on its edge.

CHANGE 2 - THE ROOM. A child's attic bedroom: a low sloped ceiling on both sides clad in white-painted planks with exposed dark timber beams running up to the ridge, a small dormer window with a dark snowy night outside and a warm fairy-light garland around it, a low wooden bed set against the knee wall made up with a deep green cover, a cream knitted throw and plaid pillows, a knitted stocking pinned to the beam above the headboard, a small lit Christmas tree standing on the floor beside the bed, a soft round rug on wide floorboards, and a low bookshelf of picture books tucked under the slope.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION, and this is the part that matters most. It is ONE enormous cinematic Christmas night scene - a single continuous picture, NOT scattered floating icons - and it is far bigger, denser and more beautiful than in @Image 1. It reads as one unbroken field across the whole wall behind the bed, both white-planked sloped ceiling planes and the dark timber beams, wrapping around the corner where wall meets slope without a break, with no visible edge, no rectangle and no screen. Built in layers, all of them present at once: LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a snow-covered village at night - rows of little gabled cottages with warm gold lit windows, a church steeple, thin curls of chimney smoke, snow-laden pine trees along the lanes, a tiny frozen pond, all glowing warm gold and cream; ABOVE THE VILLAGE, wide soft aurora ribbons in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose sweeping up the walls in long slow curves and carrying over onto the ceiling; ACROSS THE CEILING OVERHEAD, Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer, seen side-on in glowing warm gold, large enough to read the antlers, the harness and the curved front of the sleigh, with a long bright tapering trail of light streaming behind the runners; a big soft ivory full moon glowing high on the slope above the dormer window; warm gold five-point stars scattered across the ceiling with two or three long-tailed shooting stars streaking through them; and over all of it a heavy fall of hundreds of tiny bright points of light drifting down the walls like real snow caught in a beam. Recreate @Image 1's camera, light quality and style in a completely different room, with a much bigger projection.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing of a whole tall room seen from a doorway, the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two children - a boy standing TURNED AROUND FACING THE CAMERA, front-on, his face fully visible and lit by the coloured light, looking towards the lens with a delighted open-mouthed smile, arms slightly out in wonder, and a girl beside him seen from behind, still looking up at the projected wall.

Both children are fully dressed for winter in warm forest-green and cream fair-isle knitted Christmas jumpers with a band of reindeer across the chest, matching cream knitted lounge trousers and thick red knitted socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas.

CHANGE 1 - THE ROOM. A classic American family room in a traditional house: warm greige painted walls with white painted wainscoting panelling to waist height and white trim, a high vaulted ceiling clad in white-painted shiplap boards with exposed white-painted rafters rising to a dark stained ridge beam, a full-height red brick fireplace on the right with a low fire burning and a chunky white painted mantel with knitted stockings hanging from it, a deep navy roll-arm sofa with red tartan cushions and a cream cable-knit throw, a braided wool rug over wide oak floorboards, a tall real Christmas tree in the left corner with warm white lights and red and gold baubles, wrapped gifts under it, and a tall white-trimmed window behind the tree showing a dark blue snow-covered night outside.

CHANGE 2 - THE PROJECTION, and this is the part that matters most. It is ONE enormous cinematic Christmas night scene - a single continuous picture, NOT scattered floating icons - and it is far bigger, denser and more beautiful than in @Image 1. It reads as one unbroken field across every painted wall, the whole vaulted shiplap ceiling and its white rafters and ridge beam, and the red brick of the fireplace, with no visible edge, no rectangle and no screen. Built in layers, all of them present at once: LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a snow-covered village at night - rows of little gabled cottages with warm gold lit windows, a church steeple, thin curls of chimney smoke, snow-laden pine trees along the lanes, a tiny frozen pond, all glowing warm gold and cream; ABOVE THE VILLAGE, wide soft aurora ribbons in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose sweeping up the walls in long slow curves and carrying over onto the ceiling as five or six broad overlapping bands layered over each other so there is very little bare ceiling left between them, where they lie flat ALONG the slope and run with the direction of the shiplap boards instead of hanging as vertical curtains, and visibly kink and change direction where the two sloping halves of the ceiling meet at the ridge beam; ACROSS THE CEILING OVERHEAD, Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer, seen side-on in glowing warm gold, large enough to read the antlers, the harness and the curved front of the sleigh, with a long bright tapering trail of light streaming behind the runners, the whole team lying on the sloping plane so it is keystoned and stretched by the ceiling's angle and foreshortens as it recedes towards the ridge; a big soft ivory full moon glowing high on the wall beside the fireplace; one big brilliant north star high near the ridge with long rays spreading out of it; a dense field of warm gold five-point stars at many different sizes, hundreds of them, from tiny pinpricks to a few large bright ones with soft radiating rays, with four or five long-tailed shooting stars crossing at different angles with bright tapering trails; large soft glowing six-point snowflakes in warm gold and cream at several different sizes, the nearest big enough to read every arm, drifting across both slopes; faint wisps of glowing cloud between the aurora bands; and over all of it a heavy fall of hundreds of tiny bright points of light drifting down the walls like real snow caught in a beam. It stays ONE continuous night-sky picture, richly packed and busy, not scattered separate icons. THE PALETTE IS WARM: warm gold, cream white, deep Christmas red, emerald green and soft rose, richly saturated against the greige paint and the white boards. NO cold colours - no cyan, no teal, no electric blue, no violet, no grey. It must NOT look like outer space, a nebula, a galaxy, a spiral vortex, a tunnel or anything science-fiction, alien or dystopian - it is a warm storybook Christmas night sky. Every element is a separate glowing shape sitting on the surface - nothing is painted, printed, stencilled or wallpapered, and nothing is a flat repeating texture. HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE CEILING, and this has to be exactly right: it is projected light landing on a real boarded surface, not paint and not a sticker. The light is TRANSLUCENT - the shiplap boards, their seams and their subtle grain, and every white-painted rafter and the dark ridge beam, all stay clearly visible THROUGH the coloured light across the whole ceiling, and the rafters and the ridge beam break the light with their own hard shadow lines where they stand proud of the boards. Every shape up there is soft-edged and feathered with no hard opaque border, and is distorted by the surface it lands on - keystoned, stretched and skewed by the two sloping planes and bending sharply at the ridge line. The light also falls off with distance: it is brightest and most saturated where the beam first strikes and gets steadily fainter, softer and paler across the rest of the ceiling, so the far end is much dimmer than the near end and the corners fade to bare board. Even packed full, the ceiling must still read unmistakably as two sloping boarded planes meeting at a ridge beam, never as a flat backdrop or a printed panel. Two or three faint volumetric shafts of coloured light hang visibly in the air of the room, so the beam itself is seen in the space.

CHANGE 3 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The oak floorboards, the braided rug, the navy sofa, the tree and the gifts carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children's faces and their knitted jumpers catch that spill so both faces read clearly.

CHANGE 4 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no side table, no stool, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain floor and the edge of the rug.

RULE ZERO - THE ONLY THING THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS CLIP IS USABLE. READ THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE.
The Christmas light pattern on the walls and on the ceiling MUST BE MOVING, hard and fast, in every single frame. This is the entire purpose of the clip. Every previous attempt failed for exactly one reason: the pattern sat still like wallpaper. If the pattern is still, the clip is worthless.

@Video 1 IS THE MOTION AUTHORITY. It is real footage of this exact projector running. Copy the MOVEMENT of the projected light from @Video 1: its speed, its direction, its restlessness, the way the whole field of glowing shapes slides and swarms across the plaster without ever pausing. Match that amount of movement or exceed it.
TAKE NOTHING ELSE FROM @Video 1 - not its room, not its furniture, not its people, not its framing, not its colours, not its camera move, not its lighting. @Video 1 is completely silent and has no audio track at all; import no sound whatsoever from it. It is a MOVEMENT REFERENCE ONLY.

WHAT THE LIGHT DOES, described so it cannot be mistaken for a texture:
- The whole field of glowing shapes SLIDES BODILY across the wall and across the ceiling, the way light from a spinning projector head sweeps a room. It never locks onto the plaster.
- On top of that sliding, individual shapes POUR DOWNWARD like heavy snowfall filmed through a window at night, and each one spins slowly as it goes and drags a faint soft trail.
- SPEED: a single shape crosses the full height of the wall in ABOUT ONE SECOND. That is fast. A viewer must see it moving within the first quarter second of the clip.

- The moving light also pours down over the tree, the sofa, the floor and across both children's faces and knitwear as it passes over them, so the brightness on everything in the room is changing continuously. The projected picture is never a still mural or a painted scene held on the wall: the entire picture - every star, every shape, every band of colour - is travelling.
- THE START IMAGE IS A SINGLE PAUSED FRAME of this moving light. At 0.0s the video RESUMES and the light instantly goes back to sweeping and pouring and never stops - not for one frame, not at the beginning and not at the end.
- "Hold the start image" applies to the ROOM: its walls, doors, furniture, people, colours and framing. It does NOT apply to the light pattern. The light pattern must leave its starting position immediately.

IMAGE QUALITY RULE - SECOND MOST IMPORTANT. The finished clip must look at least as sharp and as clean as the start image. Do not soften it, do not smear it, do not repaint it, do not re-imagine it. Hold the exact sharpness, exposure, contrast and fine detail of the start image: the wood grain of the floor, the panel edges and painted sheen of the navy door, the brass of the round knob and its escutcheon, the skin texture and fine hairs of the bare forearm, the individual leaves of the green wreath and its red bow. BANNED: blur, soft focus, haze, motion smear on objects that are not moving, mushy low-detail surfaces, plastic or waxy skin, a repainted or re-imagined door or hallway, colour shift, washed-out or muddy exposure, upscaling artefacts, a dreamy or filtered look.

AUDIO RULE - THIRD MOST IMPORTANT: this clip has NO MUSIC OF ANY KIND. No background song, no soundtrack, no score, no melody, no instruments, no singing, no humming, no jingle, no Christmas song, no festive music bed, no ambient musical pad, no strings, no piano, no bells used as music. The audio track contains ONLY real natural sound recorded in that room. If any music appears anywhere in the 4 seconds the clip is wrong.

CHILDREN MOTION RULE: the children are ALREADY in full motion at the very first frame they appear. Never standing still, never posed, never frozen. They run, spin, jump and laugh continuously, with a clearly different whole-body pose every half second - arms, legs, heads and faces all changing. Eyes wide, mouths open laughing and shouting. Real children filmed on a phone, not a photograph coming to life.

TASK: image-to-video. The start image is frame 0.0s. Hold its door, hallway, forearm, geometry and materials exactly - but NOT its stillness and NOT the position of its light pattern.

[1] SUMMARY
First-person POV: a hand opens a door and walks into a Christmas living room where light is sweeping and pouring down every wall and the ceiling, two children running and laughing inside; the camera pushes in and tilts up. 4 seconds, one continuous take.

[2] GLOBAL STYLE
Real handheld phone POV walking forward. Warm dim hallway opening into a room lit only by the moving projection. Sharp, clean, correctly exposed, natural handheld bounce. Documentary realism. No cinematic grade, no grain, no slow motion.

[3] ASSET ROLES
The start image controls frame 0.0s: the closed navy five-panel door in its cream frame, the brass round knob on its brass escutcheon, the bare right forearm, the warm dim hallway, the wood floor and the green wreath with the red bow hanging on the door.
@Image 1 controls ONLY what is inside the room once the door is open: the room layout, the tall decorated Christmas tree on the left, the dark sofa with its cream knit throw at the left edge, the red brick fireplace with its stockings on the right, the tall window, the two children and their forest-green and cream fair-isle knitwear, and the COLOUR and STYLE of the Christmas shapes.
@Video 1 controls ONLY how the projected light MOVES. Nothing else.
Both images are photographs - copy their look, NEVER their stillness.

[4] CHARACTERS
THE BOY - forest-green and cream fair-isle knit sweater with cream knitted lounge trousers, centre of the room, running and jumping, mouth wide open laughing.
THE GIRL - matching forest-green and cream fair-isle knitwear, behind him and to his left, spinning and running, laughing.
COUNT LOCK: exactly two children. No adults, no third child, no pets.

[5] LOCATION - a warm American family room with a vaulted white plank ceiling on dark rafters: tall decorated Christmas tree on the left, dark sofa with a cream knit throw at the left edge, red brick fireplace with garland and stockings on the right, tall window behind the tree, braided rug, presents under the tree. Sweeping, pouring light covers every wall AND the whole ceiling. Its coverage is dense but uneven and constantly changing, because it is moving - that is correct and expected.

[6] FIRST FRAME - exactly the start image: the door CLOSED, the hallway lit only by its own warm dim light, the bare right forearm reaching to the brass knob.

[7] TIMELINE - the light is sweeping and pouring in every single beat
0.0-1.0s - the camera is the person's own eyes. THE RIGHT HAND grips the brass knob, turns it and pushes; the door swings away from the camera and the room behind it comes into view. The projection is ALREADY running at full strength on the far wall and across the whole ceiling before the door moves - the widening doorway simply uncovers more of a display that was already there, the way drawing a curtain back uncovers a view. Nothing lights up, ignites, spreads, ripples or switches on as the door opens, and nothing glows along the edge of the door, along the door frame or in the gap.

THE GIRL spins on the rug behind him to the left, hair flying, laughing and shouting. 3.0-4.0s - the camera keeps moving forward and TILTS UP, bringing the ceiling into the top of frame. The light is sweeping and pouring across the entire ceiling too, streaming towards the far end of the room. THE BOY jumps again with both arms straight up; THE GIRL is still turning below.
