det.label: Image prompt · v5_c07_g2.png
det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, light quality and style in a completely different room, with different children and a much bigger projection. Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas. @Image 1 owns the camera, the framing, the poses and the light. @Image 2 is a photograph of a REAL HOUSE and owns the architecture of the room and nothing else - its ceiling, its beams, its walls, its stair, its railings and its proportions are to be copied as built; ignore its daylight, its lamps, its time of day and the fact that it is not decorated.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing that shows a whole enormous double-height room with its full ceiling in shot, the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two poses - a girl JUMPING ON THE SOFA, caught mid-air above the cushions, knees bent, arms flung up, hair lifted, the cushion compressed under where she pushed off; and a boy standing on the rug in front of the sofa, seen from behind and slightly to the side, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling with his arms out in wonder. Both are small in frame, in scale with the huge room - keeping them small preserves the sense of how big the space is.

CHANGE 1 - THE CHILDREN. Different children: the girl is about eight with long straight blonde hair, the boy is about five with short blond hair. Both are fully dressed for winter in bright red and cream nordic-star knitted Christmas jumpers with a band of eight-point stars across the chest, matching cream knitted lounge trousers and thick navy knitted socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas.

CHANGE 2 - THE ROOM. The room is the real house photographed in @Image 2. Build its architecture exactly as it is built there, as a real room a real builder made: a tall double-height living space whose ceiling is flat smooth cream plaster crossed by four heavy square-sawn pale oak beams running left to right at even spacing, each one a real chunky timber with square corners and visible grain where it lands on the wall, and one large rectangular flush skylight set into the plaster between the first two beams; a first-floor gallery landing crossing the left and centre of the room at mid height, its railing made of slim black metal balusters under a black top rail with a plain cream fascia below it; a straight run of stairs on the right coming down towards the camera with pale oak treads and the same slim black baluster railing; tall black-framed windows filling the right-hand wall to full height; pale limewashed plaster walls; and underneath the gallery an open kitchen with a white marble waterfall island, open shelving with pottery and a full-height pale oak cabinet run. Terracotta saltillo tile floor laid in a square pattern, a large faded Persian rug in rust, cream and terracotta, a big cream linen sectional sofa, a chunky rustic reclaimed-wood low coffee table, and a large olive tree in a terracotta pot in the right foreground. The ceiling of this room is FLAT - there is no vault, no ridge and no sloping ceiling plane anywhere in it. Copy the proportions, the beam spacing, the skylight, the railings and the stair from @Image 2 exactly - this is a photograph of a room that exists, and the finished picture must still read as that room.

TWO THINGS CHANGE FROM @Image 2. First, it is night: the tall windows show a dark blue snow-covered night outside, there is no daylight and no sunlight anywhere in the room, every lamp, pendant and downlight in the house is switched off and dark, and the projection is the only light. Second, the room is decorated for Christmas: a very tall slim real Christmas tree standing in front of the tall windows with warm white lights, plain red wooden ornaments and brown paper wrapped gifts underneath, a thick evergreen garland with pine cones and red ribbon wound along the gallery railing and down the stair rail, plain cream knitted stockings hanging from the gallery rail, and a bowl of plain red wooden ornaments on the coffee table. Nothing else about the room changes.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION, and this is the part that matters most. It is ONE enormous cinematic Christmas night scene - a single continuous picture, NOT scattered floating icons - and it is far bigger, denser and more beautiful than in @Image 1. It reads as one unbroken field across every limewashed plaster wall, the whole flat plaster ceiling and its four heavy square oak beams, and the fascia and railing of the gallery landing, with no dark unlit wedge and no hard diagonal seam anywhere in the frame, with no visible edge, no rectangle and no screen. Built in layers, all of them present at once: LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a snow-covered village at night - rows of little gabled cottages with warm gold lit windows, a church steeple, thin curls of chimney smoke, snow-laden pine trees along the lanes, a tiny frozen pond, all glowing warm gold and cream, and running through the village an enormous glowing gold steam train with a row of lit carriages, curving out of the houses and climbing away up the wall on a long viaduct, a long white plume of smoke trailing back over the rooftops from its funnel; ABOVE THE VILLAGE, wide soft aurora ribbons in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose sweeping up the walls in long slow curves and carrying over onto the ceiling as five or six broad overlapping bands layered over each other so there is very little bare ceiling left between them, where they lie flat ALONG the ceiling plane and run with the direction of the oak beams instead of hanging as vertical curtains, and visibly break and step where each heavy beam crosses them; ACROSS THE CEILING OVERHEAD, Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer, seen side-on in glowing warm gold, large enough to read the antlers, the harness and the curved front of the sleigh, with a long bright tapering trail of light streaming behind the runners, the whole team lying flat on the ceiling plane so it is keystoned and stretched by the ceiling's angle and foreshortens as it recedes across the room; a big soft ivory full moon glowing high on the wall above the gallery landing; one big brilliant north star high beside the skylight with long rays spreading out of it; a dense field of warm gold five-point stars at many different sizes, hundreds of them, from tiny pinpricks to a few large bright ones with soft radiating rays, with four or five long-tailed shooting stars crossing at different angles with bright tapering trails; large soft glowing six-point snowflakes in warm gold and cream at several different sizes, the nearest big enough to read every arm; faint wisps of glowing cloud between the aurora bands; and over all of it a heavy fall of hundreds of tiny bright points of light drifting down the walls like real snow caught in a beam; and layered through all of it, long ribbons of glowing gold bunting and glowing red-and-cream striped candy canes turning slowly end over end as they drift, a wide sweeping arc of glowing gold musical notes and tiny bells curving across the upper wall, huge ornate six-point ice crystals the size of a dinner plate each faceted with fine internal lines turning slowly as they cross the ceiling, and a second deeper shoal of tiny stars far behind the first so the whole field has real depth. It stays ONE continuous night-sky picture, richly packed and busy, not scattered separate icons. THE PALETTE IS WARM: warm gold, cream white, deep Christmas red, emerald green and soft rose, richly saturated against the pale plaster and the oak beams. NO cold colours - no cyan, no teal, no electric blue, no violet, no grey. It must NOT look like outer space, a nebula, a galaxy, a spiral vortex, a tunnel or anything science-fiction, alien or dystopian - it is a warm storybook Christmas night sky. Every element is a separate glowing shape sitting on the surface - nothing is painted, printed, stencilled or wallpapered, and nothing is a flat repeating texture. HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right: it is projected light landing on real plaster and real timber, not paint and not a sticker. The light is TRANSLUCENT - the plaster and its fine surface texture, and every heavy square oak beam with its grain and its square corners, all stay clearly visible THROUGH the coloured light, and each beam breaks the light with its own hard shadow line where it stands proud of the plaster. Every shape is soft-edged and feathered with no hard opaque border, and is keystoned, stretched and skewed by the ceiling plane and stepping where it crosses each beam. The light falls off with distance: brightest where the beam first strikes, then steadily fainter, softer and paler, with the far corners fading to bare plaster. Even packed full, the ceiling must still read unmistakably as a real flat plaster ceiling crossed by four heavy oak beams with a skylight set between them, never as paint, a sticker or a printed panel. Three or four faint volumetric shafts of coloured light hang visibly in the air of the room, so the beam itself is seen in the space.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The terracotta tile floor, the Persian rug, the cream sectional sofa, the olive tree, the Christmas tree and the gifts carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children catch that spill so their knitted jumpers read clearly.

CHANGE 5 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no round side table, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain rug and floor.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, tack sharp edge to edge, perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, nothing blurry or soft, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

det.text:
Keep the attached image exactly as it is - the same room, the same camera position, distance and angle, the same woman in the same pose near the top of the same ladder with both arms up, the same inflatable Santa taped flat to the ceiling with the same silver duct tape, the same curved staircase, garland, stockings, marble fireplace, gold mirror, Christmas tree, blue velvet sofa and rug, the same lighting, and the same clean empty band of ceiling across the top sixth of the frame. Change only these two things:

1. HER CLOTHES: instead of the cream sweater and black leggings she is wearing matching Christmas American-flag pyjamas - a pyjama top with bold red and white horizontal stripes and a navy blue yoke across the shoulders covered in small white stars, and matching red and white striped pyjama bottoms, soft brushed cotton, slightly loose the way real pyjamas fit. Same body, same hair, same pose, same thick grey wool socks, same roll of duct tape in her left hand.

2. A UNITED STATES FLAG: a real fabric United States flag hangs flat against the plain cream wall in the background behind her, clearly readable stars and stripes, hanging straight and still. It does not cover the Christmas tree, the fireplace or the staircase, and it does not reach up into the empty band of ceiling at the top of the frame.

Everything else in the picture stays exactly as it is. Same neutral white balance with no orange cast, same iPhone snapshot look, tack sharp and in focus everywhere, absolutely nothing blurry, no background blur.
CLIP IN THE CUT — v6_c01_g1.mp4

det.label: Clip prompt · v6_c01_g1.mp4
det.text:
Real home video, shot on a hand-held iPhone by a person standing in the room a few steps behind her, phone held upright at chest height. One continuous shot. The camera stays in exactly the same spot for the whole clip with only tiny natural hand sway and micro-jitter - the small live breathing wobble of real hand-held phone footage, never a steady locked-off tripod look. It does not reframe, does not follow her, does not tilt, pan, zoom or push in. No phone, hand, fingers, thumb or arm ever appears in the foreground.

HARD RULE, THIS ONE FIRST: the whole clip is ONE single unbroken shot from the first frame to the last. No cut, no jump cut, no second angle, no scene change, no transition, no dissolve at any point. The motion runs continuously - every moment grows out of the moment before it, and her body never resets, jumps position or teleports between one part and the next.

For the first second she is just taping the inflatable Santa to the ceiling - both hands up, pressing and smoothing, nothing dramatic.

Then, without any pause or break in the movement, she loses her footing and falls off the ladder to the floor. Her arms are still up and still coming down out of the taping motion as her balance goes - the taping and the fall are one unbroken piece of movement, not two separate actions.

The fall has real weight. An ordinary woman's balance goes, gravity takes her, and she is on the floor in well under a second - fast, heavy, a bit ugly, exactly like real footage of someone coming off a ladder. Her limbs are heavy and human, not floaty or rubbery, and she never hangs in the air. The ladder goes over with her and clatters onto the rug.

She lands hard and the movement carries straight on into stillness without a break - she settles, rocks slightly as her weight comes to rest, and stays down on the floor for the rest of the clip, not moving much, just stunned and breathing. Her chest is still moving and she is still there when the clip ends.

The inflatable Santa stays taped to the ceiling the whole time.

No slow motion. No speed ramp, no speed change of any kind - the clip plays at one constant real-time speed from start to finish. No zoom, no push-in, no pan, no tilt. No captions or text.

Audio: room tone only, no music - the tape, a short gasp, the ladder hitting the floor, then her breathing.

det.text:
Recreate @Image 1 with two changes.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo, the same dim hallway, the same antique brass round doorknob in the same place, the same small pine wreath with the red velvet bow hung on the door, the same oak floorboards, the same woman's forearm entering from the lower right with the thin gold bangle and cream sleeve, her hand closed around the knob, the same camera position and camera height, the same warm low-key evening light.

CHANGE 1 - THE DOOR. It is no longer a white panelled door. It is now a classic American four-panel door painted a deep oxblood red in a soft eggshell finish: crisp raised mouldings around four flat recessed panels, clean painted surfaces with the faintest brush texture, an antique brass knob and a matching antique brass escutcheon plate, set in a plain painted cream frame. Same size, same position in frame, same flat-on angle as @Image 1.

CHANGE 2 - the door is FULLY CLOSED and flush in its frame. There is NO gap at the edge of the door and absolutely NO light spilling out - no rainbow strip, no coloured glow, no bright line, no glare anywhere along the door edge, the jamb, the threshold or the floor. The seam between door and frame is a plain dark shadow line only. Nothing behind the door is visible or lit.

THE WREATH - it hangs on the FACE of the door, centred on the upper half of the door and comfortably inside the frame with clear painted door visible all the way around it. It must NOT be cut off by the right edge of the picture and must NOT drift onto the door frame or the wall. The whole circle of the wreath and the whole red velvet bow are visible.

EXPOSURE - brighter and warmer than @Image 1, which came out too dark. The hallway is dim but comfortably readable: the oxblood paint reads clearly as a deep red rather than black, the brass knob catches a warm highlight, the oak floorboards and the forearm are clearly lit, and the shadows stay deep but still hold detail. Do not crush the blacks and do not let any part of the frame go to a flat dark mass.

SHARPNESS - this frame must be tack sharp edge to edge: every moulding edge and panel corner in the door, the machined edge and the patina of the brass knob, the individual needles of the pine wreath and the woven nap of the red velvet bow, the skin texture and fine hairs on the forearm, the grain of the floorboards. Extremely high quality, perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic. BANNED: blur, soft focus, haze, mushy low-detail surfaces, waxy skin, a dreamy or filtered look, motion blur, noise, upscaling artefacts.

Natural handheld UGC look, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, photorealistic, zero motion blur, no CGI look.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

Recreate @Image 1's camera, light quality and style in a completely different room, with a much bigger projection. @Image 1 owns the camera, the framing, the poses and the light. @Image 2 is a photograph of a REAL HOUSE and owns the architecture of the room and nothing else - its ceiling, its rafters, its walls, its stair, its railings and its proportions are to be copied as built; ignore its daylight, its lamps, its time of day and the fact that it is not decorated.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing of a whole tall room seen from a doorway, the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two children - a boy standing TURNED AROUND FACING THE CAMERA, front-on, his face fully visible and lit by the coloured light, looking towards the lens with a delighted open-mouthed smile, arms slightly out in wonder, and a girl beside him seen from behind, still looking up at the projected wall.

Both children are fully dressed for winter in warm deep plum and oatmeal cable-knit Christmas jumpers with a cream snowflake yoke across the shoulders, matching soft grey knitted lounge trousers and thick red knitted socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas.

CHANGE 1 - THE ROOM. The room is the real house photographed in @Image 2, seen from the doorway. Build its architecture exactly as it is built there, as a real room a real builder made: an enormous double-height great room whose ceiling is a cathedral vault of smooth cream plaster in two long slopes meeting at a ridge that runs away from the camera, crossed by two pairs of dark walnut-stained timber rafters, each pair rising as an inverted V to meet at the ridge with a matching collar beam below it, and small recessed downlights set flush into the plaster between them; a first-floor gallery landing crossing the right-hand half of the room at mid height, its railing made of clear glass panels held in slim black metal posts under a dark timber top rail; an open-tread pale oak staircase descending from that landing towards the camera with the same glass-and-black-post railing and black wall sconces on the wall beside it; a tall arched window with dark muntins set high on the right above the stair; a pale plaster back wall at the centre carrying a black arched double glazed door of many small panes; and along the left an open kitchen with pale oak slab cabinetry, a full-height integrated cabinet run, a cream island with a stone waterfall front, four woven rattan counter stools and two big woven rattan dome pendants hanging on long black cords. Wide warm oak plank floor, a large pale grey sectional sofa wrapping the right foreground, a round dark-stained wood coffee table and a large greige rug. Copy the proportions, the rafter pairs, the ridge, the glass railing, the stair and the arched door from @Image 2 exactly - this is a photograph of a room that exists, and the finished picture must still read as that room.

TWO THINGS CHANGE FROM @Image 2. First, it is night: the arched window and the glazed door show a dark blue snow-covered night outside, there is no daylight anywhere in the room, every downlight, pendant and sconce in the house is switched off and dark, and the projection is the only light. Second, the room is decorated for Christmas: a tall real Christmas tree standing against the pale plaster back wall beside the arched door with warm white lights and antique gold and cream ornaments and wrapped gifts beneath it, a thick evergreen garland with pine cones and antique gold ribbon wound along the gallery railing and down the stair rail, cream knitted stockings hanging from the gallery rail, and a large evergreen wreath with a cream bow on the arched door. Nothing else about the room changes.

CHANGE 2 - THE PROJECTION, and this is the part that matters most. It is ONE enormous cinematic Christmas night scene - a single continuous picture, NOT scattered floating icons - and it is far bigger, denser and more beautiful than in @Image 1. It reads as one unbroken field across every plaster wall, the whole high vaulted plaster ceiling, the dark walnut rafters and their collar beams, and the underside and railing of the gallery landing, with no visible edge, no rectangle and no screen. Built in layers, all of them present at once: LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a snow-covered village at night - rows of little gabled cottages with warm gold lit windows, a church steeple, thin curls of chimney smoke, snow-laden pine trees along the lanes, a tiny frozen pond, all glowing warm gold and cream, and rising out of the middle of the village one enormous glowing gold Christmas tree of light climbing the full height of the wall above the rooftops, its branches hung with big ornate baubles that turn slowly on their threads and a bright star at its crown; ABOVE THE VILLAGE, wide soft aurora ribbons in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose sweeping up the walls in long slow curves and carrying over onto the ceiling as five or six broad overlapping bands layered over each other so there is very little bare ceiling left between them, where they lie flat ALONG the slope and run with the direction of the rafters instead of hanging as vertical curtains, and visibly kink and change direction where the two sloping halves of the ceiling meet at the ridge; ACROSS THE CEILING OVERHEAD, Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer, seen side-on in glowing warm gold, large enough to read the antlers, the harness and the curved front of the sleigh, with a long bright tapering trail of light streaming behind the runners, the whole team lying on the sloping plane so it is keystoned and stretched by the ceiling's angle and foreshortens as it recedes towards the ridge; a big soft ivory full moon glowing high on the plaster wall above the gallery landing; one big brilliant north star high near the ridge with long rays spreading out of it; a dense field of warm gold five-point stars at many different sizes, hundreds of them, from tiny pinpricks to a few large bright ones with soft radiating rays, with four or five long-tailed shooting stars crossing at different angles with bright tapering trails; large soft glowing six-point snowflakes in warm gold and cream at several different sizes, the nearest big enough to read every arm, drifting across both slopes; faint wisps of glowing cloud between the aurora bands; and over all of it a heavy fall of hundreds of tiny bright points of light drifting down the walls like real snow caught in a beam; and layered through all of it, long ribbons of glowing gold bunting and glowing red-and-cream striped candy canes turning slowly end over end as they drift, a wide sweeping arc of glowing gold musical notes and tiny bells curving across the upper wall, huge ornate six-point ice crystals the size of a dinner plate each faceted with fine internal lines turning slowly as they cross the ceiling, and a second deeper shoal of tiny stars far behind the first so the whole field has real depth. It stays ONE continuous night-sky picture, richly packed and busy, not scattered separate icons. THE PALETTE IS WARM: warm gold, cream white, deep Christmas red, emerald green and soft rose, richly saturated against the pale plaster and the dark walnut rafters. NO cold colours - no cyan, no teal, no electric blue, no violet, no grey. It must NOT look like outer space, a nebula, a galaxy, a spiral vortex, a tunnel or anything science-fiction, alien or dystopian - it is a warm storybook Christmas night sky. Every element is a separate glowing shape sitting on the surface - nothing is painted, printed, stencilled or wallpapered, and nothing is a flat repeating texture. HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE CEILING, and this has to be exactly right: it is projected light landing on real plaster and real timber, not paint and not a sticker. The light is TRANSLUCENT - the cream plaster and its fine surface texture, and every dark walnut rafter, every collar beam and the ridge line of the vault, all stay clearly visible THROUGH the coloured light across the whole ceiling, and the rafters and the collar beams break the light with their own hard shadow lines where they stand proud of the plaster. Every shape up there is soft-edged and feathered with no hard opaque border, and is distorted by the surface it lands on - keystoned, stretched and skewed by the two sloping planes and bending sharply at the ridge line. The light also falls off with distance: it is brightest and most saturated where the beam first strikes and gets steadily fainter, softer and paler across the rest of the ceiling, so the far end is much dimmer than the near end and the corners fade to bare plaster. Even packed full, the ceiling must still read unmistakably as a real plastered cathedral vault with dark walnut rafter pairs and their collar beams crossing it, never as a flat backdrop or a printed panel. Two or three faint volumetric shafts of coloured light hang visibly in the air of the room, so the beam itself is seen in the space.

CHANGE 3 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The warm oak floorboards, the greige rug, the grey sectional sofa, the round coffee table, the tree and the gifts carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children's faces and their knitted jumpers catch that spill so both faces read clearly.

CHANGE 4 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no side table, no stool, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain floor and the edge of the rug.

det.text:
TASK: image-to-video. 5 seconds. One continuous handheld phone POV take, vertical 9:16. The start image is frame 0.0s: a closed oxblood red door with a wreath, a hand on the brass knob.

THE PICTURE ON THE WALLS IS A CLOSED SET
The start image does not show the room, so read the room ONLY from @Image 1. Everything thrown onto the walls and ceiling is already drawn in @Image 1. You are not designing a projection - you are making the one in @Image 1 move. Invent nothing. If a thing is not in the list below, it does not exist in this clip.

THE COMPLETE LIST OF WHAT IS PROJECTED, AND WHAT EACH ONE DOES

Moving layer - these travel across the plaster:
- Six-point snowflakes, white and pale gold. They fall steadily and continuously, top to bottom, new ones entering above as others slide out below. They never hang still. They are FLAT LIGHT LYING ON THE PLASTER and they never leave it: a flake slides down the face of the ceiling or the face of a wall and stays welded to that surface for its whole journey. It is a stain of light on a solid surface, not a falling object. There is no snow in the air of the room, none between the camera and the walls, none in front of the children, the sofa, the staircase or the tree, and none landing on the floor or on anyone.
- Candy canes, red and white striped. They drift down with the snow, tumbling slowly end over end as they go.
- Shooting stars, gold with a tail. They streak across, the tail thinning out behind them, and fade; fresh ones set off elsewhere.
- The aurora ribbons, green and pink and magenta, laid along and between the dark rafters. A bright swell runs the length of each ribbon end to end, the way a wave runs down a shaken rope, and the ribbons themselves creep sideways.
- The fine gold star specks filling the gaps. The whole field creeps slowly and the specks twinkle in and out.
- The gold line of musical notes on their staff, along the right-hand rafter. The notes travel along the staff like sheet music sliding past.
- The reindeer team and sleigh, gold, to the left of the moon. They gallop steadily across and finish a long way from where they set off.

Holding layer - these keep their exact positions and only twinkle:
- The moon, bright and full, centre right. It holds and only breathes brighter and dimmer.
- The church with the tall steeple, right of the moon. Holds; its windows twinkle.
- The snowy village houses low on the left wall. Hold; their lit windows twinkle.
- The big gold Christmas tree and the slimmer cone tree behind it on the left wall. Hold; their lights twinkle.
- The street lamps among the houses. Hold; they flicker faintly.

ADD NOTHING. No smoke and no chimney plumes of any kind. No extra buildings, no extra trees, no extra figures, no angels, no bells, no letters, no numbers, no new shapes. Nothing appears that is not on the list.

EVERY PROJECTED SHAPE IS PAINT, NOT AN OBJECT. All of it is flat light lying on whatever surface it lands on. It skews and stretches with the slope of that surface, it bends over the rafters, it breaks where a wall meets the ceiling. Nothing ever floats free of a surface into the air of the room.

WHAT ELSE HOLDS: the real room. The plaster, the rafters, the staircase and its gallery landing, the door, the wooden floor, the rug, the sofa, the real Christmas tree and its lights, the framing, the colours. The projected picture's outer edge stays put - it never rotates, spins, swings or slides across the room as one sheet. Only the things inside it travel.

@Image 1 is the authority on the room and on every projected shape: its layout, its staircase, its furniture, its two children, and the exact set, style and colour of the projected shapes. It is a photograph - copy its look, never its stillness.

BEATS
0.0-0.8s - The hand turns the brass knob and pushes the door away from camera. Behind it the room is ALREADY running: snow already falling, the aurora already swelling, the reindeer already crossing. The widening gap simply uncovers more of something that was already going, like pulling a curtain off a window. Nothing ignites, switches on, spreads or grows as the door opens, and nothing glows along the door edge, frame or gap.
0.8-2.0s - The door swings wide and the camera walks through. The snow keeps falling at the same steady rate it already had, down the face of the far wall. It stays on that wall - it does not cross the open air of the room and it does not drift toward the camera.
2.0-3.3s - Inside. The two children are both already in motion and stay in motion. Projected shapes slide down the walls behind them and pass across their backs and faces.
3.3-5.0s - The camera keeps walking and TILTS UP until the rafters fill the top of frame. The ceiling is the busiest surface in the clip: snow pouring down it, the swell running along every aurora ribbon, the notes sliding along the staff, the reindeer crossing it, the specks twinkling.

CAMERA - eye height, normal wide-angle phone lens, natural handheld bounce. Exactly two moves: the walk from 0.8s, the tilt up from 3.3s. No cut, no zoom, no orbit, no fisheye, no curved walls. The camera is the person's eyes - no phone, screen, hand or device in frame after 0.8s.

THE CHILDREN - exactly two, both visible from 2.0s on, no adults, no third child, no pets. Deep plum and oatmeal cable-knit knitwear, as in @Image 1. They never stand still and never pose.

SHARPNESS - hold the sharpness, exposure and fine detail of the start image: the wood grain of the floor, the panel edges and sheen of the red door, the brass knob, the skin of the bare forearm, the wreath needles. Crisp phone footage, in focus first frame to last.

AUDIO - dry documentary sound only: the handle, the door swinging, children laughing, quiet room tone. NO music, no song, no score, no instruments, no bells used as music.

BANNED - snow, snowflakes or any particles falling through the open air of the room; volumetric or three-dimensional snow; anything drifting between the camera and the walls; snow passing in front of the children, the sofa, the staircase, the rug or the real tree; snow settling on the floor, the furniture or anyone's hair or shoulders; any projected shape that appears to leave the surface it is painted on; any projected shape that is not on the list above; smoke; a shape that stays in the same place on the plaster when the list says it travels; a projection that appears to move only because the camera moves; shapes that only twinkle when the list says they travel; a parked sleigh; a still aurora; a still or empty ceiling when the camera tilts up; the whole picture rotating, spinning or sliding as one sheet; a pattern that looks printed, painted, stencilled or like wallpaper; light that moves for a moment then stops; a glow, seam or bright line along the door edge, frame or gap; light that grows or fills the room as the door opens; any music; blur or soft focus; children standing still or posed; jellyfish, fish, coral, bubbles or any underwater imagery; a room lit entirely blue; the projector unit visible; a third child; an adult; a cut; subtitles; on-screen text.

THE PICTURE IS A FILM PLAYING ON A CINEMA SCREEN: the screen is the plaster and holds perfectly still, while everything inside the picture is in constant motion for all four seconds. Build its architecture exactly as it is built there, as a real room a real builder made: an enormous double-height great room whose ceiling is a cathedral vault of smooth cream plaster in two long slopes meeting at a ridge that runs away from the camera, crossed by two pairs of dark walnut-stained timber rafters, each pair rising as an inverted V to meet at the ridge with a matching collar beam below it, and small recessed downlights set flush into the plaster between them; a first-floor gallery landing crossing the right-hand half of the room at mid height, its railing made of clear glass panels held in slim black metal posts under a dark timber top rail; an open-tread pale oak staircase descending from that landing towards the camera with the same glass-and-black-post railing and black wall sconces on the wall beside it; a tall arched window with dark muntins set high on the right above the stair; a pale plaster back wall at the centre carrying a black arched double glazed door of many small panes; and along the left an open kitchen with pale oak slab cabinetry, a full-height integrated cabinet run, a cream island with a stone waterfall front, four woven rattan counter stools and two big woven rattan dome pendants hanging on long black cords. It is ONE enormous cinematic Christmas night scene - a single continuous picture, NOT scattered floating icons - and it is far bigger, denser and more beautiful than in @Image 1. It reads as one unbroken field across the entire two-storey pale plaster back wall, the plaster walls either side of it, the whole high vaulted plaster ceiling, the dark walnut rafters and their collar beams and the underside and railing of the gallery landing, with no dark unlit wedge and no hard diagonal seam anywhere in the frame, with no visible edge, no rectangle and no screen. ACROSS THE CEILING OVERHEAD, Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer, seen side-on in glowing warm gold, large enough to read the antlers, the harness and the curved front of the sleigh, with a long bright tapering trail of light streaming behind the runners, the whole team lying on the sloping plane so it is keystoned and stretched by the ceiling's angle and foreshortens as it recedes towards the ridge; a big soft ivory full moon glowing high on the plaster wall above the gallery landing; one big brilliant north star high near the ridge with long rays spreading out of it; a dense field of warm gold five-point stars at many different sizes, hundreds of them, from tiny pinpricks to a few large bright ones with soft radiating rays, with four or five long-tailed shooting stars crossing at different angles with bright tapering trails; large soft glowing six-point snowflakes in warm gold and cream at several different sizes, the nearest big enough to read every arm; faint wisps of glowing cloud between the aurora bands; and over all of it a heavy fall of hundreds of tiny bright points of light drifting down the walls like real snow caught in a beam; and layered through all of it, long ribbons of glowing gold bunting and glowing red-and-cream striped candy canes turning slowly end over end as they drift, a wide sweeping arc of glowing gold musical notes and tiny bells curving across the upper wall, huge ornate six-point ice crystals the size of a dinner plate each faceted with fine internal lines turning slowly as they cross the ceiling, and a second deeper shoal of tiny stars far behind the first so the whole field has real depth. It stays ONE continuous night-sky picture, richly packed and busy, not scattered separate icons. THE PALETTE IS WARM: warm gold, cream white, deep Christmas red, emerald green and soft rose, richly saturated against the pale plaster and the dark walnut rafters. NO cold colours - no cyan, no teal, no electric blue, no violet, no grey. It must NOT look like outer space, a nebula, a galaxy, a spiral vortex, a tunnel or anything science-fiction, alien or dystopian - it is a warm storybook Christmas night sky. Every element is a separate glowing shape sitting on the surface - nothing is painted, printed, stencilled or wallpapered, and nothing is a flat repeating texture. HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right: it is projected light landing on real plaster and real timber, not paint and not a sticker. The light is TRANSLUCENT - the plaster and its fine surface texture, and every dark walnut rafter, every collar beam and the ridge line of the vault, all stay clearly visible THROUGH the coloured light, and the rafters and the collar beams break the light with their own hard shadow lines where they stand proud. Every shape is soft-edged and feathered with no hard opaque border, and is keystoned, stretched and skewed by the surface it lands on. The light falls off with distance: brightest where the beam first strikes, then steadily fainter, softer and paler, with the far corners fading to bare plaster. Even packed full it must still read as projected light on a real plastered vault with real timber rafters crossing it, never as paint, a sticker or a printed panel. Three or four faint volumetric shafts of coloured light hang visibly in the air of the room, so the beam itself is seen in the space.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The warm oak floorboards, the greige rug, the grey sectional sofa, the round coffee table and the tree carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children catch that spill so their knitted jumpers read clearly.

CHANGE 5 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no round side table, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain rug and floor.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, tack sharp edge to edge, perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, nothing blurry or soft, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

Recreate @Image 1's camera, light quality and style in a completely different room, with a much bigger projection. @Image 1 owns the camera, the framing, the poses and the light. @Image 2 is a photograph of a REAL HOUSE and owns the architecture of the room and nothing else - its ceiling, its beams, its walls, its stair, its railings and its proportions are to be copied as built; ignore its daylight, its lamps, its time of day and the fact that it is not decorated.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing of a whole tall room seen from a doorway, the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two children - a boy standing TURNED AROUND FACING THE CAMERA, front-on, his face fully visible and lit by the coloured light, looking towards the lens with a delighted open-mouthed smile, arms slightly out in wonder, and a girl beside him seen from behind, still looking up at the projected wall.

Both children are fully dressed for winter in warm rust-orange and cream fair-isle knitted Christmas jumpers with a band of little pine trees across the chest, matching oatmeal knitted lounge trousers and thick cream knitted socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas.

CHANGE 1 - THE ROOM. The room is the real house photographed in @Image 2, seen from the doorway. Build its architecture exactly as it is built there, as a real room a real builder made: a tall double-height living space whose ceiling is flat smooth cream plaster crossed by four heavy square-sawn pale oak beams running left to right at even spacing, each one a real chunky timber with square corners and visible grain where it lands on the wall, and one large rectangular flush skylight set into the plaster between the first two beams; a first-floor gallery landing crossing the left and centre of the room at mid height, its railing made of slim black metal balusters under a black top rail with a plain cream fascia below it; a straight run of stairs on the right coming down towards the camera with pale oak treads and the same slim black baluster railing; tall black-framed windows filling the right-hand wall to full height; pale limewashed plaster walls; and underneath the gallery an open kitchen with a white marble waterfall island, open shelving with pottery and a full-height pale oak cabinet run. Terracotta saltillo tile floor laid in a square pattern, a large faded Persian rug in rust, cream and terracotta, a big cream linen sectional sofa, a chunky rustic reclaimed-wood low coffee table, and a large olive tree in a terracotta pot in the right foreground. Copy the proportions, the beam spacing, the skylight, the railings and the stair from @Image 2 exactly - this is a photograph of a room that exists, and the finished picture must still read as that room.

TWO THINGS CHANGE FROM @Image 2. First, it is night: the tall windows show a dark blue snow-covered night outside, there is no daylight and no sunlight anywhere in the room, every lamp, pendant and downlight in the house is switched off and dark, and the projection is the only light. Second, the room is decorated for Christmas: a tall real Christmas tree standing in front of the tall windows with warm white lights and terracotta and antique copper baubles and wrapped gifts underneath, a thick evergreen garland with pine cones and terracotta ribbon wound along the gallery railing and down the stair rail, cream knitted stockings hanging from the gallery rail, and a bowl of terracotta and antique copper baubles on the coffee table. Nothing else about the room changes.

CHANGE 2 - THE PROJECTION, and this is the part that matters most. It is ONE enormous cinematic Christmas night scene - a single continuous picture, NOT scattered floating icons - and it is far bigger, denser and more beautiful than in @Image 1. It reads as one unbroken field across every plaster wall, the whole flat plaster ceiling and its four heavy square oak beams, and the fascia and railing of the gallery landing, with no visible edge, no rectangle and no screen. Built in layers, all of them present at once: LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a snow-covered village at night - rows of little gabled cottages with warm gold lit windows, a church steeple, thin curls of chimney smoke, snow-laden pine trees along the lanes, a tiny frozen pond, all glowing warm gold and cream, and turning slowly above the rooftops one enormous glowing gold fairground carousel of prancing reindeer, its scalloped canopy strung with tiny bells and its centre pole a bright column of light, and on the frozen pond below it a wide ring of glowing gold ice skaters circling one behind another, each one trailing a long bright curved arc of light across the ice; ABOVE THE VILLAGE, wide soft aurora ribbons in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose sweeping up the walls in long slow curves and carrying over onto the ceiling as five or six broad overlapping bands layered over each other so there is very little bare ceiling left between them, where they lie flat ALONG the ceiling plane and run with the direction of the oak beams instead of hanging as vertical curtains, and visibly break and step where each heavy beam crosses them; ACROSS THE CEILING OVERHEAD, Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer, seen side-on in glowing warm gold, large enough to read the antlers, the harness and the curved front of the sleigh, with a long bright tapering trail of light streaming behind the runners, the whole team lying flat on the ceiling plane so it is keystoned and stretched by the ceiling's angle and foreshortens as it recedes across the room; a big soft ivory full moon glowing high on the wall above the gallery landing; one big brilliant north star high beside the skylight with long rays spreading out of it; a dense field of warm gold five-point stars at many different sizes, hundreds of them, from tiny pinpricks to a few large bright ones with soft radiating rays, with four or five long-tailed shooting stars crossing at different angles with bright tapering trails; large soft glowing six-point snowflakes in warm gold and cream at several different sizes, the nearest big enough to read every arm, drifting across the whole ceiling; faint wisps of glowing cloud between the aurora bands; and over all of it a heavy fall of hundreds of tiny bright points of light drifting down the walls like real snow caught in a beam; and layered through all of it, long ribbons of glowing gold bunting and glowing red-and-cream striped candy canes turning slowly end over end as they drift, a wide sweeping arc of glowing gold musical notes and tiny bells curving across the upper wall, huge ornate six-point ice crystals the size of a dinner plate each faceted with fine internal lines turning slowly as they cross the ceiling, and a second deeper shoal of tiny stars far behind the first so the whole field has real depth; and beyond even that, great slow-turning glowing gold snow globes the size of a car drifting across the upper wall, each one holding its own tiny lit village inside it, a long glowing gold paper-chain garland of angels linked hand to hand curving right across the ceiling from one corner to the other, whole flights of glowing gold robins and doves crossing in loose Vs at three different depths, glowing gold ribbons of ivy and holly with bright red berries winding up every corner of the room, and a slow steady rise of glowing gold sparks lifting off the village chimneys and climbing the full height of the wall to join the star field, so every surface is so full that the eye cannot rest on any single thing. It stays ONE continuous night-sky picture, richly packed and busy, not scattered separate icons. THE PALETTE IS WARM: warm gold, cream white, deep Christmas red, emerald green and soft rose, richly saturated against the pale plaster and the oak beams. NO cold colours - no cyan, no teal, no electric blue, no violet, no grey. It must NOT look like outer space, a nebula, a galaxy, a spiral vortex, a tunnel or anything science-fiction, alien or dystopian - it is a warm storybook Christmas night sky. Every element is a separate glowing shape sitting on the surface - nothing is painted, printed, stencilled or wallpapered, and nothing is a flat repeating texture. HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE CEILING, and this has to be exactly right: it is projected light landing on real plaster and real timber, not paint and not a sticker. The light is TRANSLUCENT - the plaster and its fine surface texture, and every heavy square oak beam with its grain and its square corners, all stay clearly visible THROUGH the coloured light across the whole ceiling, and each beam breaks the light with its own hard shadow line where it stands proud of the plaster. Every shape up there is soft-edged and feathered with no hard opaque border, and is distorted by the surface it lands on - keystoned, stretched and skewed by the ceiling plane and stepping where it crosses each beam. The light also falls off with distance: it is brightest and most saturated where the beam first strikes and gets steadily fainter, softer and paler across the rest of the ceiling, so the far end is much dimmer than the near end and the corners fade to bare plaster. Even packed full, the ceiling must still read unmistakably as a real flat plaster ceiling crossed by four heavy oak beams with a skylight set between them, never as a backdrop or a printed panel. Two or three faint volumetric shafts of coloured light hang visibly in the air of the room, so the beam itself is seen in the space.

CHANGE 3 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The terracotta tile floor, the Persian rug, the cream sectional sofa, the olive tree, the Christmas tree and the gifts carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children's faces and their knitted jumpers catch that spill so both faces read clearly.

CHANGE 4 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no side table, no stool, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain floor and the edge of the rug.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, tack sharp edge to edge, perfect lighting, perfectly exposed with both children's faces clearly readable, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, nothing blurry or soft, no CGI look.

det.text:
TASK: image-to-video, 5 seconds, one continuous handheld phone POV take, vertical 9:16. Frame 0.0s is the start image: a closed forest green two-panel door with a wreath, a hand on the antique brass knob. @Image 1 is the room behind that door and the authority on its layout, beams, stair, furniture, two children, colours, and on the exact set and style of every projected shape.

THE MOVING PICTURE IS THE SUBJECT OF THIS CLIP. The walls and the ceiling are a cinema screen with a film playing on them. The plaster and the pale oak beams hold perfectly still; the picture lying on them is running for all five seconds. @Image 1 is one paused frame of that film, and at 0.0s it un-pauses.

Four things carry the motion, and all four are running from the first frame to the last:

SMOKE. Every cottage chimney in the little village is smoking hard enough to see plainly. Each plume boils up out of its pot, leans to the right, climbs a full cottage-roof height every second and widens and thins away, while the next plume is already forming behind it.

THE AURORA. Each ribbon behaves like a long silk curtain hung in a slow draught: a swell travels along the ribbon from one end to the other, about a third of its length every second, brightening and thinning the ribbon as it passes and combing its lower fringe into new folds. The ribbon's arc stays where it is on the plaster; the swell inside it travels.

THE SLEIGH. Santa's sleigh and its team of reindeer are FLYING. They travel across the ceiling, about a fifth of the ceiling's width every second, so that by 5.0s the team has crossed most of the way. Legs gallop, heads nod, the sleigh rocks behind them, the long tapering trail of light streams off the runners, and the whole team rises and dips as it goes. The team is never parked.

THE SNOW. Every snowflake and point of light drifts downward and slightly sideways, about a quarter of the wall's height every second, the way snow falls past a window at night, each one turning slowly on its own centre and breathing brighter and dimmer on its own timing. One that reaches the floor line fades out there as a fresh one fades in high near the beams, so the density never thins.

Everything else in the picture travels as well: the gold sparks lifting off the chimneys and climbing to the star field, the great fairground carousel turning with its reindeer rising and falling on their poles, the skaters circling the frozen pond and laying bright arcs behind them, the shooting stars streaking and fading, the candy canes and faceted ice crystals tumbling end over end, the snow globes turning, the birds beating across in loose Vs. Only the moon and the north star hold their positions; those two simply breathe brighter and dimmer.

The walls and the ceiling are lit by ONE projector and are therefore ONE picture: whatever the wall is doing, the ceiling is doing at the same instant and at the same speed. The picture's outer boundary is anchored - it never rotates, spins, swings or slides across the room as one sheet; only the things inside it travel. All of it is flat light lying on the surfaces: it skews with their slope, bends over the beams and breaks where wall meets ceiling. Nothing ever leaves a surface - no snow in the open air of the room, none between camera and wall, none in front of the children, the sofa, the stair or the real tree, none settling on the floor or on anyone.

BEATS
0.0-0.7s - The hand turns the brass knob and pushes the door away from camera. The room behind it is already running; the widening gap only uncovers more of something that was already going, like pulling a curtain off a window. Nothing ignites, switches on or spreads as the door opens. The door edge and frame stay plain painted wood - no glowing strip, no coloured fringe, no bright seam in the gap.
0.7-3.2s - The camera walks through and on across the rug. THE BOY, the child facing the camera at 0.0s, turns on the spot away from the lens, runs three or four quick real steps and LAUNCHES HIMSELF UP ONTO the cream linen sectional sofa, landing on his knees on the cushions with both arms flying up, laughing; the cushions compress under him and spring back. THE GIRL stays where she is, seen from behind, shifting her weight and turning her head to watch him.
3.2-5.0s - The boy keeps bouncing on the cushions, pushing up and dropping back with his arms above his head, while the camera tilts up to the oak beams. The ceiling is the busiest surface in the frame: snow pouring across it, the swell running along every aurora ribbon, the sleigh team crossing it, the specks twinkling.

CAMERA - eye height, normal wide-angle phone lens, natural handheld bounce. Two moves only: the walk from 0.7s, the tilt up from 3.2s. The camera is the person's eyes; no phone, screen, hand or device in frame after 0.7s.

THE CHILDREN - exactly two, both visible from 1.7s on, no adults, no third child, no pets. Rust-orange and cream fair-isle knitted jumpers with a band of little pine trees across the chest, oatmeal knitted lounge trousers, thick cream knitted socks, as in @Image 1.

SHARPNESS - hold the sharpness, exposure and fine detail of the start image: the panel edges and eggshell sheen of the forest green door, the brass knob and its escutcheon, the skin of the forearm and its thin gold bangle, the wreath needles. Crisp phone footage, in focus first frame to last.

AUDIO - dry documentary sound only: the handle, the door swinging, running feet on tile and rug, a body landing on cushions, children laughing, quiet room tone. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS - real-time motion at normal speed throughout. One continuous take. The picture is visibly in motion in every single frame - at the start, in the middle and in the last second. The boy ends the clip on the sofa, not standing where he began. Sharp focus to the final frame.

BANNED - a still or frozen picture; chimneys without smoke; an aurora that sits still; a sleigh and reindeer parked in one place; flakes that twinkle but never travel; a still ceiling above a moving wall; a projection that appears to move only because the camera moves; light that moves for a moment and then stops; the whole picture rotating, spinning or sliding as one sheet; a pattern that looks printed, painted, stencilled or like wallpaper; a glow, seam or bright line along the door edge, frame or gap; light that grows or fills the room as the door opens; particles falling through the open air of the room; volumetric or three-dimensional snow; snow in front of the children, the sofa, the stair, the rug or the real tree; snow settling on anyone; any projected shape that leaves the surface it lies on; the boy still standing front-on at the end; children posed or standing still; jellyfish, fish, coral, bubbles or underwater imagery; a room lit entirely blue; the projector unit visible; slow motion; blur or soft focus; any music; a cut; a third child; an adult; subtitles; on-screen text.

SUBJECTS:
THE GIRL - exactly one child, a girl of about seven with shoulder-length light brown hair, in a warm rust-orange and cream fair-isle knitted Christmas jumper with a band of little pine trees across the chest, matching oatmeal knitted lounge trousers and thick cream knitted socks, standing on the bed with her arms thrown wide. No second child, no adult, no pet.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running on the bedroom floor, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the wall and both sloping plaster ceiling planes. Everything glowing on the plaster and the oak is that one cone landing.
THE PICTURE - the animated scene that cone is playing: a snow village low along the wall with gabled cottages with lit windows, a church steeple, snow-laden pine trees and a frozen pond, plumes above the chimneys, an enormous glowing gold fairground carousel of prancing reindeer turning above the rooftops, a ring of glowing gold ice skaters circling the frozen pond below it, wide aurora ribbons in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose lying along both ceiling slopes and kinking at the ridge, Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer keystoned across the slope, a big soft ivory moon high on the slope above the gable window, one big brilliant north star near the ridge, a dense field of warm gold stars of many sizes, long-tailed shooting stars, glowing gold candy canes, bunting, big faceted ice crystals, slow-turning snow globes, a paper-chain garland of angels, loose Vs of gold robins and doves, and a heavy fall of small glowing gold and cream six-point snowflakes and points of light.

THE PICTURE IS A FILM PLAYING ON A CINEMA SCREEN: the screen is the plaster and the oak and holds perfectly still, while everything inside the picture is in constant motion for all five seconds. 0.0-2.2s the camera is aimed HIGH at the start, weighted to the top of the wall and the sloping plaster ceiling so the projected picture fills most of the frame and THE GIRL is small and low near the bottom edge. Wall and ceiling always move together. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.

SUMMARY: two children play in a double-height Christmas great room while a projected snow-village picture is PLAYING across the walls and the whole flat cream plaster ceiling and its four heavy square oak beams, thrown there by a projector standing in the room. 4 seconds, one continuous handheld phone take, vertical.

GLOBAL STYLE: crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed. Sharp and in focus from the first frame to the last, at least as sharp as the start image. No blur, no haze, no soft focus, no washed-out exposure, no colour shift.

ASSET ROLES: @Image 1 is frame 0.0s and controls the great room, the flat cream plaster ceiling crossed by four heavy square-sawn pale oak beams with a flush rectangular skylight set between them, the first-floor gallery landing with its slim black metal balusters under a black top rail, the straight run of pale oak stairs on the right, the tall black-framed windows filling the right-hand wall with snow outside, the pale limewashed plaster walls, the open kitchen with its white marble waterfall island, the terracotta saltillo tile floor, the large faded Persian rug in rust, cream and terracotta, the big cream linen sectional sofa, the chunky rustic reclaimed-wood low coffee table, the large olive tree in its terracotta pot, the lit Christmas tree with its presents, the children and the colour.

SUBJECTS:
THE SMALLER CHILD - a boy of about five with short sandy brown hair, on the rug at the front left, back to camera, facing the wall, turning on the spot with his arms out.
THE OTHER CHILD - a girl of about eight with long wavy light brown hair, standing up on the cream linen sofa cushions, back to camera, with both arms raised toward the wall, bouncing on the spot.
Both in warm rust-orange and cream fair-isle knitted Christmas jumpers with a band of little pine trees across the chest, matching oatmeal knitted lounge trousers and thick cream knitted socks. Exactly two children. No third child, no adult, no pet.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running in the room, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the walls and the whole ceiling. Everything glowing on the plaster and the oak is that one cone landing.
THE PICTURE - the animated scene that cone is playing: a snow village low along the walls with gabled cottages with lit windows, a church steeple, snow-laden pine trees and a frozen pond, plumes above the chimneys, an enormous glowing gold fairground carousel of prancing reindeer turning above the rooftops, a ring of glowing gold ice skaters circling the frozen pond below it, wide aurora ribbons in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose sweeping up the walls and lying along the ceiling with the direction of the oak beams, Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer keystoned across the ceiling, a big soft ivory moon high on the wall above the gallery landing, one big brilliant north star beside the skylight, a dense field of warm gold stars of many sizes, long-tailed shooting stars, glowing gold candy canes, bunting, big faceted ice crystals, slow-turning snow globes, a paper-chain garland of angels, loose Vs of gold robins and doves, and a heavy fall of small glowing gold and cream six-point snowflakes and points of light.

HOW THE PICTURE BEHAVES - THIS IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE CLIP. In every previous attempt the picture sat dead still like printed wallpaper and the clip was worthless. THE PICTURE IS A FILM PLAYING ON A CINEMA SCREEN: the screen is the plaster and the oak and holds perfectly still, while everything inside the picture is in constant motion for all four seconds. The start image is one paused frame of that film; at 0.0s it un-pauses. Matching @Image 1 applies to the great room, the furniture, the children and the colours, not to where any element of the picture sits.
THE PICTURE AS A WHOLE IS ANCHORED. It does not rotate, spin, swing, sweep sideways or slide across the room as one sheet. Its outer boundary stays where it is. The motion lives INSIDE it, element by element, and every one of these is moving at the same time:
- THE CHIMNEY SMOKE - every cottage chimney in the village is smoking. Each plume climbs upward out of its chimney pot, leaning slightly to the right, rising about one cottage-roof height every second, widening and thinning as it climbs and fading out before it reaches the aurora, while a fresh plume forms at the pot behind it. The plumes are never a fixed painted shape.
- THE RISING SPARKS - the glowing gold sparks lift off the village chimneys continuously and climb the full height of the wall to join the star field, drifting a little sideways as they rise and fading out near the top, with fresh ones leaving the pots for the whole clip.
- THE AURORA - each ribbon ripples ALONG ITS OWN LENGTH, a slow travelling wave running from one end of the ribbon to the other, about a third of the ribbon's length every second, the ribbon swelling brighter and thinner as the wave passes and its lower fringe combing and re-forming. Each ribbon's overall arc stays where it is on the plaster; the wave inside it travels. Every ribbon on the walls and on the ceiling is doing this at the same time.
- THE SLEIGH AND THE REINDEER - they are FLYING. The team travels steadily across the ceiling away from where it sits in the start image, covering about a fifth of the ceiling's width every second, so by 4.0s it has crossed most of the way. The reindeer's legs gallop, their heads nod, the sleigh rocks gently behind them, the long tapering trail of light streams behind the runners, and the whole team rises and dips a little as it goes. The team is never parked.
- THE CAROUSEL - the great glowing gold fairground carousel above the rooftops TURNS, about a quarter of a full turn every second, its prancing reindeer swinging round with it and rising and falling on their poles as they pass, its scalloped canopy turning with them and its centre pole pulsing brighter and dimmer.
- THE ICE SKATERS - the ring of glowing gold skaters circles the frozen pond one behind another, covering about a third of the ring every second, each one leaning into the curve and laying down a long bright curved arc of light behind it that slowly fades off the ice as a fresh one is drawn.
- THE SHOOTING STARS - they streak across at their different angles, the tail thinning out behind them, and fade; fresh ones set off elsewhere for the whole clip.
- THE SNOWFLAKES AND THE POINTS OF LIGHT - each one drifts downward and slightly sideways about a quarter of the wall's height every second, the way snow falls past a window at night. Each turns slowly on its own centre as it drifts and breathes brighter and dimmer on its own timing. One that reaches the floor line fades out there while a fresh one fades in high near the beams, so the density holds even.
- THE CANDY CANES, THE BUNTING, THE ICE CRYSTALS, THE SNOW GLOBES, THE ANGEL GARLAND AND THE BIRDS - all of them travel slowly across the surfaces they are painted on, the candy canes and the big faceted ice crystals turning end over end as they go, the snow globes turning slowly on their own centres, the birds beating their wings as their loose Vs cross.
- THE STAR FIELD - the small gold stars hold their places and twinkle, each brightening and dimming on its own timing, never all together.
- THE MOON AND THE NORTH STAR - these two are the ONLY elements that hold their positions. They stay exactly where they are for the whole clip and only brighten and dim very slightly. Nothing else in the picture is allowed to hold still.
Because the walls and the whole ceiling are lit by the SAME projector, they are one picture and behave identically at the same instant. Whatever the flakes, the aurora and the stars on the wall are doing, the flakes, the aurora and the stars on the ceiling are doing at the same moment and at the same speed. There is never a still ceiling above a moving wall. Nothing is painted, printed or stencilled on the plaster or the oak.

TIMELINE:
0.0-1.0s the person filming takes one clear step forward; the frame moves in and settles. THE OTHER CHILD bounces on the sofa cushions with both arms up, laughing. THE SMALLER CHILD turns on the rug with his face tipped up.
1.0-2.0s the camera holds in the closer position. THE OTHER CHILD pushes up harder and drops back down onto the cushion, her knees bending and springing back. THE SMALLER CHILD keeps turning and tips his head further back.
2.0-4.0s the camera tilts up in one slow smooth move past the top of the tree until the beamed ceiling fills the upper half of the frame, the aurora rippling along it and the sleigh team still flying across it. Both children stay low in the frame and keep moving.

AUDIO: room tone, two children laughing and squealing, feet thumping on the sofa cushions, socked feet on a rug. (no BGM). No music, no song, no score, no instruments, no bells used as music. No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS: real-time motion at normal speed throughout - real children moving at real speed with real weight. Exactly two children, and their knitted jumpers read clearly. One continuous take with no cut. The camera makes one move per beat and no more. The picture's outer boundary holds still while every element inside it moves. Walls and ceiling always move together. THE OTHER CHILD stays on the sofa. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.

DO NOT INCLUDE: a frozen or still pattern; chimneys that are not smoking; an aurora that sits still; a sleigh and reindeer parked in one place; a carousel that does not turn; skaters that do not circle; flakes that only twinkle without travelling; a still ceiling above moving walls; the whole picture rotating, spinning, sweeping or sliding as one sheet; a projection that appears to move only because the camera moves; slow motion; floating or weightless movement; any music; children standing still; a third child; an adult; the projector unit in shot; jellyfish, fish, coral or bubbles; blur; a cut; on-screen text; subtitles.

det.label: Image prompt · v8_c01_g5.png
det.text:
Extremely high quality candid vertical iPhone photo taken from the floor of a double-height Christmas living room, looking up and across at a woman standing on the mezzanine landing, evening. We see her from below and slightly to the side, her raised arms and the high ceiling in front of her.

FRAMING AND ANGLE: the camera stands on the living-room floor MUCH closer in to the stairs than a wide establishing shot, tilted up, so the woman and the inflatable she is taping fill most of the picture and the room reads as context around them rather than as the subject. The mezzanine landing crosses the frame with its black metal railing along it, and the woman stands on that landing behind the railing DEAD CENTRE on the vertical axis of the frame, framed from roughly the waist up and very large in the picture - she is the biggest thing in the photograph and the taped inflatable is directly above and ahead of her, also near the centre, so her reaching arm and the inflatable together sit in the middle of the frame. A short stretch of the open white staircase still enters the lower right corner, and the living-room floor is still clearly visible below her in the lower part of the picture, so the drop from the landing to the floor reads plainly. She is NOT on a ladder - there is no ladder anywhere in the picture.

THE KEY ELEMENT: a large inflatable Santa Claus decoration is TAPED FLAT TO THE HIGH WHITE CEILING above the double-height space, lying on its back against the plaster and facing down into the room, held by a mess of criss-crossed silver duct tape strips over its legs, arms and hat. It is clearly fixed to the ceiling. It hangs out over the open double-height void rather than over the landing. One corner has started to peel, with a long strip of tape hanging down.

HER POSE - THIS IS THE POINT OF THE PICTURE: she is leaning far out over the landing railing to reach it. Her hips are pressed against the top rail, her weight is tipped forward past it and out over the open void, her feet still on the landing behind her with her heels lifting, one hand gripping the rail and the other stretched up and out pressing a fresh strip of silver duct tape onto Santa's shoulder, a roll of duct tape in her gripping hand. She is visibly overreaching and off balance, the rail the only thing holding her, empty air and the floor below her.

THE ROOM - COPY IT FROM THE FIRST ATTACHED PHOTOGRAPH: the room in this picture is the EXACT SAME ROOM as the first attached photograph, same house, same light, same furniture in the same places - a double-height white modern American farmhouse living room - white painted walls, a wall of tall black-framed windows at the right with a dark winter garden behind them, a white open-tread staircase with slim black metal spindles, a mezzanine landing with a matching black rail and a green garland with red bows wound along it, a white plaster fireplace on the ground floor, a tall green Christmas tree with warm white lights and red and gold baubles standing in the double-height space, pale wide-plank oak floor, a light linen sofa and a cream rug.

A UNITED STATES FLAG: a real fabric United States flag hangs flat against the white wall in the background under the landing, clearly readable stars and stripes, hanging straight and still, about the size of a large poster. It does not cover the Christmas tree or the fireplace and it does not reach up into the empty band of ceiling at the top of the frame.

HER CLOTHES: matching American-flag Christmas pyjamas - a pyjama top with bold red and white horizontal stripes and a navy blue yoke across the shoulders covered in small white stars, and matching red and white striped pyjama bottoms, soft brushed cotton, slightly loose the way real pyjamas fit - with thick grey wool socks. She is mid 30s with dark brown hair in a loose low bun.

There is no projected light anywhere - the ceiling, the walls and the staircase are plain painted plaster and plain timber, completely clean, no projected patterns, no snowflakes, no stars, no coloured light spilling on any surface. The room is lit only by the Christmas tree, the fireplace and ordinary warm lamps.

COLOUR - READ THIS CAREFULLY: neutral white balance, the way an iPhone auto-corrects a warm room. The picture is NOT orange, NOT amber, NOT sepia, NOT golden-hour, and there is no warm colour cast laid over the whole frame. The ceiling and the walls read as clean white paint, the window frames and the rail read as true black, the oak floor reads as natural wood, the flag keeps true red, white and navy. The Christmas tree lights, the fireplace and the lamps are warm points of light sitting inside a neutrally balanced room - they do not tint the rest of the picture.

LIGHTING AND QUALITY: bright, clean and evenly lit - plenty of light on the high ceiling, on the landing and on her, no dark corners, no heavy shadows. Shot on an iPhone and straight out of the camera roll: an ordinary everyday snapshot, not a magazine photo and not a rendered image. Modern phone-camera look - wide dynamic range, lifted shadows, clean highlights, accurate colour. Extremely high quality, tack sharp and in focus everywhere, crisp detail in the duct tape, the inflatable vinyl sheen and the weave of her pyjamas, realistic skin and fabric texture. Absolutely nothing blurry: no motion blur, no soft focus, no background blur, no grain, no film look, no cinematic grade, no vignette, no bloom. Normal wide-angle lens, vertical lines vertical and parallel, no fisheye distortion.

FRAMING: leave a generous clean band of plain empty ceiling across the very top of the image - roughly the top fifth of the frame - completely empty and free of Santa, of tape, of beams, of garland and of any other object, so a caption can sit there. Make that room by tilting the camera up slightly, NOT by pulling the camera back and NOT by shrinking the woman - she stays close and large and centred exactly as described above.

No captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

det.label: Clip prompt · v8_c01_g2.mp4
det.meta: seedance_2_5 · 1080p · 5 s · 9:16 · audio on · job b497f18e
det.text:
Single continuous handheld iPhone shot, 5 seconds, vertical 9:16, filmed by someone standing on the living room floor below and holding the phone up — real held-phone look with natural handheld sway, no cuts, no zoom, no lens push-in, framing locked exactly as in the start frame for the whole clip.

Start frame: a woman in American-flag pajamas stands on the upstairs balcony, leaning her hips against the dark wooden top rail, both arms stretched up over her head, pressing strips of silver duct tape onto the white ceiling to hold up a big inflatable Santa. Below her: the two-storey living room with the lit fireplace, the American flag on the wall, the decorated Christmas tree and the white sofa.

ACTION TIMELINE:
0.0–1.0s — Up on her toes, she smooths one more strip of silver tape onto the ceiling with her palm, then gives the inflatable Santa a quick test tug to check it is holding, leaning her whole weight forward into the wooden top rail.
1.0–1.5s — The section of the dark wooden top rail she is leaning on splits with a loud crack and swings away from her, and she pitches forward over the balcony edge, eyes wide, both hands clamping onto the inflatable Santa.
1.5–2.5s — She drops down into the living room, the inflatable Santa peeling straight off the ceiling and coming with her — the silver tape strips tearing free and trailing, the green garland and a red bow sliding off the broken rail behind her.
2.5–3.4s — She misses the sofa completely and lands flat on her back on the wooden living room floor in front of it, hitting the floor and settling straight down with no bounce, and the big inflatable Santa flops down on top of her, covering her from the waist up.
3.4–5.0s — She shoves the inflatable Santa's head sideways off her face, hair everywhere, looks straight up at the camera and bursts out laughing, still flat on her back on the floor with the Santa across her lap. End frame: her laughing on the floor under the inflatable, the empty broken balcony rail above her.

AUDIO: her real voice, lip-synced, matching her appearance — a short surprised yelp as the rail gives way, then breathless laughing at the end; the sharp crack of splitting wood; duct tape ripping off the ceiling; the squeaky rubbery scuff of the big inflatable; the heavy flat thud of her body landing on the wooden floor; the fireplace crackling quietly under everything. (no BGM). No subtitles.

REALISM — HARD RULES: she keeps exactly the same face, hair and American-flag pajamas as the start frame the whole clip. The living room stays pixel-faithful to the start frame — same fireplace, same flag, same Christmas tree, same sofa, same windows, same warm lamp light. The inflatable Santa stays the same size, colours and printed face the whole clip and never deforms into a different character. Real weight and gravity on the fall — she drops straight down, she is never thrown or launched sideways. She lands on the wooden floor, NOT on the sofa - she never touches the sofa at any point in the clip. Real phone-camera look, slight sensor noise, mild motion blur on the fall, no cinematic bokeh, no slow motion, no text overlays, no watermark.

POSITIVE LOCKS: everything plays at real-time speed. One continuous take from 0.0s to 5.0s. The camera never moves from where it is in the start frame.
