det.text:
Copy the FIRST attached reference photo EXACTLY: same camera position, same top-down-ish angle, same distance, same vertical 9:16 framing, same table surface at the same height and same angle, same two hands resting on the box in the same position and same grip, same arms entering frame the same way. Keep OUR product box exactly as it appears in the FIRST reference and in the SECOND attached reference: a tall upright rectangular tuck-top carton, square footprint, roughly 15 x 15 x 24 cm, forest green body, dark red band across the top with a gold THEXMASGLOW wordmark, cream serif headline CHRISTMAS LIGHT PROJECTOR, a gold star-and-tree burst over a printed render of a smooth white dome-topped cylindrical projector on a separate white four-legged splayed stand base, slim red remote printed beside it, gold village skyline along the bottom, no transparent window. Keep the box at the same position, scale and angle it occupies in the FIRST reference. Change only three things.

FIRST - THE HANDS. A woman's hands, about 32, slender fingers, narrow wrists, smooth bare skin, short clean natural nails with no polish, no jewellery of any kind - no rings, no bangle, no watch - the cuffs of a soft dove-blue wool sweater pushed back at both wrists. Same position on the box, same grip, same arms entering the frame the same way, same scale.

SECOND - THE TABLE. The surface under the box is no longer bare timber. It is now a warm honey cherry table top: a golden red-brown timber with a fine close straight grain and a gentle natural colour variation through it, finished in a soft satin lacquer that gives a low even sheen rather than a mirror, with a simple rounded edge. Same height, same angle, same amount of the surface visible as in the FIRST reference.

THIRD - THE BACKGROUND. Behind and above the table, a softly defocused snowy New England cottage Christmas parlour: walls in white painted beadboard above a soft dove-blue painted dado rail, a red brick fireplace with a simple white painted mantel and cream knitted stockings hanging from it, a decorated Christmas tree with warm white fairy lights and bright red and antique silver ornaments standing off to one side, a narrow plate rail high on the wall carrying a row of blue-and-white transferware plates, all well out of focus so the box stays the clear subject.

Dress the honey cherry table more festively: a sprig of fir and a few red berries, two or three small bright red and antique silver baubles, a short cream candle, a soft warm string light trailing across the satin cherry, all at the edges of frame so the box stays the clear subject.

Shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, photorealistic, extremely high quality, tack-sharp focus on the box and the hands, crisp legible detail in the printing on the carton, perfect natural realistic lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, nothing blurry or soft, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

The wordmark printed on the red band must read exactly THEXMASGLOW - eleven letters, T-H-E-X-M-A-S-G-L-O-W, correctly spelled, sharp and legible, with no invented or misspelled brand name anywhere on the carton.

det.label: Clip prompt · v8_c02_g1.mp4
det.text:
AUDIO RULE - HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ THIS FIRST: this clip has NO MUSIC OF ANY KIND. No background song, no soundtrack, no score, no melody, no instruments, no singing, no humming, no jingle, no Christmas song, no festive music bed, no ambient musical pad, no strings, no piano, no bells used as music. The audio track contains ONLY real natural sound recorded in that room. The attached reference video is SILENT and has no audio track at all - take nothing from it but movement. If any music appears anywhere in the 4 seconds the clip is wrong.

BOTH HANDS RULE - SECOND MOST IMPORTANT: this is a TWO-HANDED lift and it is the thing the last take got wrong. From the moment the hands take hold of the projector inside the box until it has left the top of the frame, BOTH hands are on it at once - one hand on the left side of the dome, the other hand on the right side of the dome, thumbs on the near side, fingers curled around the far side. The left hand never lets go, never opens, never drops back to the table, never rests on the box rim or on a lid flap, and never leaves the product for a single frame. Both hands rise together, both hands carry it out of the top of frame together. This is never a one-handed lift.

EXIT RULE - THIRD MOST IMPORTANT: the projector does NOT stay in frame at the end. The hands lift it out of the box and KEEP GOING, carrying it straight up and completely out of the top of the frame. At 4.0s the projector is GONE from the picture and only the open carton is left on the table. The hands never stop, never hold the product up for inspection, never settle, never pause.

SPEED RULE - FOURTH MOST IMPORTANT: the hands work at a brisk, confident, real-time pace. This is a normal person opening a box at normal speed, not a careful slow-motion demonstration. The lift is QUICK and decisive. Do not slow anything down.

TASK: image-to-video. The start image is frame 0.0s. Hold its table, box artwork, props and lighting exactly.

[1] SUMMARY
First-person POV: two hands open a tall dark-green Christmas carton on a warm honey cherry dining table, lift the white projector briskly straight up out of it and carry it out of the top of frame. Locked POV looking down. 4 seconds, one take.

[2] GLOBAL STYLE
Real handheld phone POV, warm domestic Christmas light, crisp and sharp, correctly exposed. Very slight handheld drift. Real-time speed throughout. No cinematic grade, no grain, no slow motion, no speed ramp.

[3] ASSET ROLES
The start image controls the table, the carton artwork, the hands, the candle, the props and the light. @Video 1 controls ONLY the mechanics of the unboxing: fingers slide under the front lid flap, flaps fold up and back, hands grip the unit inside, the unit lifts straight up. Do not copy the table, the box design, the room, the hands or the product from @Video 1. Do NOT copy the pacing from @Video 1 - use the faster timeline below. Do NOT copy its ending - in this clip the product leaves the frame.

[4] OBJECTS
THE BOX - a dark-green tuck-top carton standing upright, front panel facing camera, a dark red band across the top with a gold THEXMASGLOW wordmark, the cream serif words CHRISTMAS LIGHT PROJECTOR, a gold star-and-tree burst over a printed white dome-topped projector on a white four-legged splayed stand, a gold village skyline along the bottom, no transparent window. About 15 x 15 x 24 cm. Plain interior, no insert, no foam tray.
THE PROJECTOR - inside THE BOX: a matte-white dome-shaped body on a separate white four-legged splayed stand. Set into the top of the dome is a flat circular BLACK perforated mesh disc. The top face is BLACK and stays black for every frame. No front lens, no camera head, no swivel.
THE HANDS - exactly two hands, a woman's, with the cuff of a soft dove-blue wool sweater pushed back at each wrist and no jewellery of any kind - no rings, no bangle, no watch.

[5] LOCATION - a warm honey cherry dining table fills the frame: golden red-brown timber with a fine close straight grain, a soft satin lacquer and a simple rounded edge. A lit cream pillar candle sits at the left, fir sprigs with red berries and small bright red and antique silver baubles beside it, and behind it, softly out of focus, white painted beadboard above a soft dove-blue painted dado rail, a red brick fireplace with a simple white painted mantel, a narrow plate rail high on the wall carrying a row of blue-and-white transferware plates, hanging cream knitted stockings, and a decorated Christmas tree with warm white lights and bright red and antique silver ornaments. The candle, the fir, the berries, the baubles, the defocused fireplace and the defocused tree must still be in the final frame.

[6] FIRST FRAME - exactly the start image: THE BOX closed and upright, both HANDS gripping its sides.

[7] TIMELINE - brisk real-time pacing, every beat lands on time
0.0-0.7s - camera locked. The fingers of both HANDS slide under the front top flap of THE BOX and lift it sharply; the tuck tongue pops out of the front panel.
0.7-1.4s - the lid flaps fold upward and backward away from camera on the rear fold in one quick motion, staying attached to THE BOX; the dark interior comes into view.
1.4-2.1s - both HANDS drop straight down into THE BOX and grip THE PROJECTOR by its sides, thumbs on the near side. The BLACK perforated mesh disc on its top face is clearly visible.
2.1-3.0s - THE HANDS lift THE PROJECTOR QUICKLY and decisively straight up and out of THE BOX in one brisk continuous vertical pull, clearing the rim in well under a second. The BLACK top face is clearly visible as it rises.
3.0-3.6s - the HANDS DO NOT STOP. They keep rising in the same continuous motion; THE PROJECTOR travels up towards the top edge of frame, first the stand then the dome crossing the edge and leaving the picture.
3.6-4.0s - THE PROJECTOR and both HANDS are completely OUT OF FRAME. The frame holds on the open empty carton on the warm honey cherry dining table, lid flaps folded back, with the candle, the fir, the berries, the defocused fireplace and the defocused tree still in shot. Nothing else moves.

[9] CAMERA AND OPTICS - one static POV looking down at the table at roughly 50 degrees, vertical 9:16, normal wide-angle phone lens, very slight handheld drift only. The camera NEVER follows the product upward - it stays exactly where it is and lets the product exit the frame. No push-in, no orbit, no zoom, no tilt, no cut.

det.text:
HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ THIS FIRST: the pictures on the walls and the vaulted ceiling are A MOVIE THAT IS PLAYING, not a pattern painted on the plaster. @Image 1 is ONE PAUSED FRAME of that movie. At 0.0s it un-pauses and keeps running to the last frame. Smoke pours, the aurora ripples, the sleigh flies, the balloons climb, the snow globes turn, the snow falls - continuously, in every single frame. If the shapes on the walls and ceiling hold still, the clip has failed.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home at Christmas.

TASK: image-to-video, one continuous handheld phone POV take, vertical 9:16. Frame 0.0s is the start image: a closed six-panel dove-blue door with a wreath, a hand on the brass knob. @Image 1 is the great room behind that door and the authority on its layout, rafters, furniture, the two children, their clothes, the colours, and the exact set and style of every projected shape.

THE SIX MOVING THINGS - all six running from the first frame to the last.

SMOKE. Every cottage chimney in the little village pours smoke like a real wood fire on a cold still evening: it boils out of the pot, leans right, climbs and widens and thins away, and the next plume is already forming behind it.

THE AURORA. The gold, emerald and deep rose ribbons ripple like a long silk curtain hung in a draught - a slow swell travels the length of each ribbon, brightening it as it passes and combing its lower fringe into new folds. The arc stays where it is on the plaster; the swell inside it travels.

THE SLEIGH. Santa's sleigh and its eight reindeer are FLYING ACROSS THE CEILING the way a plane crosses the sky. Legs gallop, heads nod, the sleigh rocks, the long trail of light streams off the runners, the team rises and dips. They start near one side of the vault and finish far across it. Never parked.

THE BALLOONS. The colossal glowing bauble-shaped hot-air balloon and the three smaller balloons behind it RISE, the way paper lanterns rise on a still night: steadily up the wall and on over the vault, lanterns swinging underneath, ribbons of light trailing below.

THE SNOW GLOBES. Each glass globe TURNS slowly on its stand, and the snow inside every one of them is swirling and settling, like a globe someone has just shaken.

THE SNOW. The big soft six-point flakes and the tiny points of light fall the way heavy snow falls past a window at night - down and slightly sideways, each turning on its own centre. One fades out at the floor line as a fresh one fades in high near the ridge, so the density never thins.

Everything else travels too: gold sparks lifting off the chimneys, shooting stars streaking and fading, candy canes and faceted ice crystals tumbling end over end, gold bunting rippling, robins and doves beating across in loose Vs. Only the ivory moon and the one brilliant north star hold position; those two simply breathe brighter and dimmer.

ONE PROJECTOR, ONE PICTURE: whatever the wall is doing, the vault is doing at the same instant and the same speed. The picture's outer boundary is anchored - it never rotates, spins or slides across the room as one sheet; only the things inside it travel. It is flat light lying on the surfaces: it skews with their slope, bends over the rafters and breaks where wall meets vault. Nothing ever leaves a surface, and nothing is projected on the floor, rug, sofa, table, tree or gifts.

THE VAULT IS FULL. The ceiling carries as much moving picture as the walls do, everywhere it appears in frame and above all in the closing seconds: aurora, the flying sleigh, climbing balloons, pouring snow and twinkling stars run right up to the ridge and into both corners. No bare un-animated patch of cream plaster anywhere in the closing framing.

0.0-0.8s - The hand turns the knob and pushes the door away from camera. The room behind it is already running; the widening gap only uncovers more of a movie that was already playing. Nothing ignites or spreads as the door opens, and the door edge and frame stay plain painted wood - no glowing strip, no coloured fringe, no bright seam in the gap.
0.8s to the end - ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN CAMERA MOVE, exactly like a person walking into a room with their chin lifting the whole way. The camera walks steadily forward while its aim rises smoothly at a constant rate, so the frame climbs from the floor to the dark walnut rafters and the cream vault in one continuous sweep. Walk and rise happen together at the same steady pace for the whole span; the camera never pauses, never holds and never re-starts, and there is no second move. All through it the smoke pours, the aurora ripples, the sleigh flies on across the vault, the balloons keep climbing, the globes keep turning and the snow keeps falling.
Inside that single move: THE BOY, the child facing camera at 0.0s, turns away from the lens, runs three or four quick real steps and LAUNCHES HIMSELF UP ONTO the pale grey sectional sofa on the right, landing on his knees with both arms flying up, laughing, then keeps bouncing there until the last frame. THE GIRL stays where she is, seen from behind, turning her head to follow him. Projected shapes slide down the walls behind them and pass across their backs.

CAMERA - eye height, normal wide-angle phone lens, natural handheld bounce. One move for the whole clip. No stop, no second move, no cut, no zoom, no orbit, no fisheye, no curved walls. The camera is the person's eyes; no phone, screen or device in frame after 0.8s.

EXACTLY TWO CHILDREN, no adults, no third child, no pets. Hold the sharpness and exposure of the start image - the panel edges of the dove-blue door, the brass knob, the bare forearm and its thin gold bangle. Crisp phone footage, in focus first frame to last.

AUDIO - dry documentary sound only: the handle, the door swinging, running feet, a body landing on cushions, children laughing, quiet room tone. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS - real-time motion at normal speed. One continuous take. One single smooth camera move. The projected picture is visibly in motion in every single frame, at the start, in the middle and in the last second. The vault is covered in moving picture at the end. The boy ends the clip bouncing on the sofa. Sharp focus to the final frame.

det.text:
Wholesome family Christmas scene, a child at home with his family at Christmas.

SUMMARY: a boy bounces on his bed in an attic Christmas bedroom at night while a projected snow-village picture is PLAYING across the left wall and the whole plaster ceiling, thrown there by a projector standing on the floor. 5 seconds, one continuous handheld phone take, vertical.

GLOBAL STYLE: crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed. Sharp and in focus from the first frame to the last, at least as sharp as the start image. No blur, no haze, no soft focus, no washed-out exposure, no colour shift.

ASSET ROLES: @Image 1 is frame 0.0s and controls the attic bedroom, the flat plaster centre panel and its two knuckle lines, the four flush recessed downlights in that centre panel, the bed with its dove-blue wool quilt and cream linen pillows, the wide upholstered headboard, the sliding barn door, the small lit Christmas tree, the large oat flat-weave rug, the window with its garland, the stocking, THE BOY and the colour.

SUBJECTS:
THE BOY - exactly one child, about six years old with short dark brown hair, in a warm dove-blue and cream nordic knitted Christmas jumper with a row of cream stags across the yoke, charcoal knitted lounge trousers and thick red knitted socks, standing on the bed with his arms thrown wide. No second child, no adult, no pet.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running on the bedroom floor, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the wall and the whole plaster ceiling. Everything glowing on the plaster is that one cone landing.
THE PICTURE - the animated scene that cone is playing: snow-covered village cottages with lit windows, a church with a tall steeple, snow-laden pines and a frozen pond low on the LEFT wall, thin curls of smoke above their chimneys, ribbons of aurora in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose arching across the flat centre panel and both shallow side slopes of the ceiling, Santa's sleigh drawn by eight flying reindeer with a long tapering trail keystoned across the ceiling at the upper left, a colossal glowing gold hot-air balloon shaped like a great ribbed Christmas bauble with lit lanterns hung round its wicker basket and a long ribbon of light streaming down behind it, three smaller balloons climbing behind it at three different depths, a big soft ivory full moon over on the right, one big brilliant north star, a dense field of warm gold five-point stars of many sizes, long-tailed shooting stars, and a heavy fall of large soft glowing six-point snowflakes and tiny points of light.

HOW THE PICTURE BEHAVES - THIS IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE CLIP. In every previous attempt the picture sat dead still like printed wallpaper and the clip was worthless. THE PICTURE IS A FILM PLAYING ON A CINEMA SCREEN: the screen is the plaster and holds perfectly still, while everything inside the picture is in constant motion for all five seconds. The start image is one paused frame of that film; at 0.0s it un-pauses. Matching @Image 1 applies to the bedroom, the bed, THE BOY and the colours, not to where any element of the picture sits.
THE PICTURE AS A WHOLE IS ANCHORED. It does not rotate, spin, swing, sweep sideways or slide across the room as one sheet. Its outer boundary stays where it is. The motion lives INSIDE it, element by element:
- THE CHIMNEY SMOKE - every cottage chimney on the left wall is smoking. Each thin curl climbs upward out of its chimney pot, leaning slightly to the right, rising about one cottage-roof height every second, widening and thinning as it climbs and fading out before it reaches the aurora, while a fresh curl forms at the pot behind it. The plumes are never a fixed painted shape.
- THE RISING SPARKS - a slow steady rise of glowing gold sparks lifts off the village chimneys and climbs the full height of the wall to join the star field, drifting slightly sideways as it goes, new sparks leaving the chimneys continuously so the column never empties.
- THE AURORA - each ribbon ripples ALONG ITS OWN LENGTH, a slow travelling wave running from one end of the ribbon to the other, about a third of the ribbon's length every second, the ribbon swelling brighter and thinner as the wave passes and its lower fringe combing and re-forming. Each ribbon's overall arc stays where it is on the plaster; the wave inside it travels. Every ribbon on the ceiling is doing this at the same time.
- THE SLEIGH AND THE REINDEER - they are FLYING. The team travels steadily across the ceiling away from the upper left corner where it sits in the start image, toward the far side of the ceiling, covering about a fifth of the ceiling's width every second, so by 5.0s it has crossed most of the way. The reindeer's legs gallop, their heads nod, the sleigh rocks gently behind them, the long tapering trail streams out behind, and the whole team rises and dips a little as it goes.
- THE BALLOONS - the colossal gold bauble-shaped hot-air balloon CLIMBS. It rises steadily up the wall and onto the ceiling, about a sixth of the wall's height every second, swaying very gently from side to side as it climbs; the lit lanterns hung round its wicker basket swing on their hooks and the long ribbon of light streaming down behind it ripples and trails. The three smaller balloons climb behind it at their three different depths, each at its own slightly slower rate, so the group opens out as it rises.
- THE SNOWFLAKES AND THE POINTS OF LIGHT - each one drifts downward and slightly sideways about a quarter of the wall's height every second, the way snow falls past a window at night. Each turns slowly on its own centre as it drifts and breathes brighter and dimmer on its own timing. One that reaches the skirting board fades out there while a fresh one fades in high near the knuckle line, so the density holds even. Track this one so the fall is unmistakable: a large cream six-point flake that begins just above the headboard, falls steadily and drifts slightly right, passes the middle of the wall at 2.5s and fades out low near the skirting at 5.0s.
- THE SHOOTING STARS - the long-tailed shooting stars streak across, their tails thinning out behind them, and fade; fresh ones set off elsewhere.
- THE STAR FIELD - the small gold stars hold their places and twinkle, each brightening and dimming on its own timing, never all together.
- THE MOON AND THE NORTH STAR - these two are the ONLY elements that hold their positions. They stay exactly where they are on the right for the whole clip and only brighten and dim very slightly. Nothing else in the picture is allowed to hold still.
Because the wall and the whole ceiling are lit by the SAME projector, they are one picture and behave identically at the same instant. Whatever the flakes, the aurora and the stars on the wall are doing, the flakes, the aurora and the stars on the ceiling are doing at the same moment and at the same speed. There is never a still ceiling above a moving wall. Nothing is painted, printed or stencilled on the plaster.

TIMELINE - THE CAMERA MAKES EXACTLY TWO MOVES AND NO MORE, and they are the opposite of the other clips in this set: this one starts high and comes DOWN.
0.0-2.2s the camera is aimed HIGH at the start, weighted to the top of the wall and the flat plaster ceiling panel so the projected picture fills most of the frame and THE BOY is small and low near the bottom edge. From 0.0s the camera TILTS DOWN in one slow steady continuous move, the aurora rippling and the sleigh flying across the panel as it goes, until the bed and THE BOY fill the lower half. THE BOY bends his knees and pushes off the mattress; both feet leave the quilt, arms swinging up over his head, mouth open laughing. The mattress compresses and springs back.
2.2-5.0s the tilt ends and the camera PULLS BACK a little in one slow steady move, the frame opening slightly wider so a little more of the bedroom comes in at the edges - a small gentle zoom out, nothing sudden. THE BOY lands on both feet and drives straight into a second, higher jump, knees tucking, then a third; he never stops moving and the body motion carries straight across the seam between the two camera moves.

AUDIO: room tone, mattress springs compressing on each landing, bedding rustling, a boy laughing. (no BGM). No subtitles.

The camera makes exactly two moves: a slow tilt DOWN, then a small gentle pull back. The picture's outer boundary holds still while every element inside it moves. Wall and ceiling always move together. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.

det.label: Image prompt · v8_c07_g1.png
det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, light quality and style in a completely different room, with different children and a much bigger projection. Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas. @Image 1 owns the camera, the framing, the poses and the light. @Image 2 is a photograph of a REAL HOUSE and owns the architecture of the room and nothing else - its ceiling, its rafters, its walls, its stair, its railings and its proportions are to be copied as built; ignore its daylight, its lamps, its time of day and the fact that it is not decorated.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing that shows a whole enormous double-height room with its full ceiling in shot, the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two poses - a girl JUMPING ON THE SOFA, caught mid-air above the cushions, knees bent, arms flung up, hair lifted, the cushion compressed under where she pushed off; and a boy standing on the rug in front of the sofa, seen from behind and slightly to the side, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling with his arms out in wonder. Both are small in frame, in scale with the huge room - keeping them small preserves the sense of how big the space is.

CHANGE 1 - THE CHILDREN. Different children: the girl is about eight with long dark brown hair in two loose braids, the boy is about five with short dark brown hair. Both are fully dressed for winter in warm dove-blue and cream nordic knitted Christmas jumpers with a row of cream stags across the yoke, matching charcoal knitted lounge trousers and thick red knitted socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas.

CHANGE 2 - THE ROOM. The room is the real house photographed in @Image 2 - the same house seen earlier in this ad, now from the middle of the great room. Build its architecture exactly as it is built there, as a real room a real builder made: an enormous double-height great room whose ceiling is a cathedral vault of smooth cream plaster in two long slopes meeting at a ridge that runs away from the camera, crossed by two pairs of dark walnut-stained timber rafters, each pair rising as an inverted V to meet at the ridge with a matching collar beam below it, and small recessed downlights set flush into the plaster between them; a first-floor gallery landing crossing the right-hand half of the room at mid height, its railing made of clear glass panels held in slim black metal posts under a dark timber top rail; an open-tread pale oak staircase descending from that landing towards the camera with the same glass-and-black-post railing and black wall sconces on the wall beside it; a tall arched window with dark muntins set high on the right above the stair; a pale plaster back wall at the centre carrying a black arched double glazed door of many small panes; and along the left an open kitchen with pale oak slab cabinetry, a full-height integrated cabinet run, a cream island with a stone waterfall front, four woven rattan counter stools and two big woven rattan dome pendants hanging on long black cords. Wide warm oak plank floor, a large pale grey sectional sofa wrapping the right foreground, a round dark-stained wood coffee table and a large greige rug. Copy the proportions, the rafter pairs, the ridge, the glass railing, the stair and the arched door from @Image 2 exactly - this is a photograph of a room that exists, and the finished picture must still read as that room.

TWO THINGS CHANGE FROM @Image 2. First, it is night: the arched window and the glazed door show a dark blue snow-covered night outside, there is no daylight anywhere in the room, every downlight, pendant and sconce in the house is switched off and dark, and the projection is the only light. Second, the room is decorated for Christmas: a very tall real Christmas tree standing against the pale plaster back wall beside the arched door with warm white lights and bright red and antique silver ornaments and wrapped gifts beneath it, a thick evergreen garland with pine cones and red velvet ribbon wound along the gallery railing and down the stair rail, cream knitted stockings hanging from the gallery rail, and a large evergreen wreath with a red velvet bow on the arched door. Nothing else about the room changes.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION, and this is the part that matters most. It is ONE enormous cinematic Christmas night scene - a single continuous picture, NOT scattered floating icons - and it is far bigger, denser and more beautiful than in @Image 1. It reads as one unbroken field across the entire two-storey pale plaster back wall, the plaster walls either side of it, the whole high vaulted plaster ceiling, the dark walnut rafters and their collar beams and the underside and railing of the gallery landing, with no dark unlit wedge and no hard diagonal seam anywhere in the frame, with no visible edge, no rectangle and no screen. Built in layers, all of them present at once: LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a snow-covered village at night - rows of little gabled cottages with warm gold lit windows, a church steeple, thin curls of chimney smoke, snow-laden pine trees along the lanes, a tiny frozen pond, all glowing warm gold and cream, and rising up the wall above the rooftops one colossal glowing gold hot-air balloon shaped like a great ribbed Christmas bauble, its wicker basket hung all round with lit lanterns and a long ribbon of light streaming down behind it, with three smaller balloons climbing behind it at three different depths; ABOVE THE VILLAGE, wide soft aurora ribbons in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose sweeping up the walls in long slow curves and carrying over onto the ceiling as five or six broad overlapping bands layered over each other so there is very little bare ceiling left between them, where they lie flat ALONG the slope and run with the direction of the rafters instead of hanging as vertical curtains, and visibly kink and change direction at the ridge; ACROSS THE CEILING OVERHEAD, Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer, seen side-on in glowing warm gold, large enough to read the antlers, the harness and the curved front of the sleigh, with a long bright tapering trail of light streaming behind the runners, the whole team lying on the sloping plane so it is keystoned and stretched by the ceiling's angle and foreshortens as it recedes towards the ridge; a big soft ivory full moon glowing high on the plaster wall above the gallery landing; one big brilliant north star high near the ridge with long rays spreading out of it; a dense field of warm gold five-point stars at many different sizes, hundreds of them, from tiny pinpricks to a few large bright ones with soft radiating rays, with four or five long-tailed shooting stars crossing at different angles with bright tapering trails; large soft glowing six-point snowflakes in warm gold and cream at several different sizes, the nearest big enough to read every arm; faint wisps of glowing cloud between the aurora bands; and over all of it a heavy fall of hundreds of tiny bright points of light drifting down the walls like real snow caught in a beam; and layered through all of it, long ribbons of glowing gold bunting and glowing red-and-cream striped candy canes turning slowly end over end as they drift, a wide sweeping arc of glowing gold musical notes and tiny bells curving across the upper wall, huge ornate six-point ice crystals the size of a dinner plate each faceted with fine internal lines turning slowly as they cross the ceiling, and a second deeper shoal of tiny stars far behind the first so the whole field has real depth; and beyond even that, great slow-turning glowing gold snow globes the size of a car drifting across the upper wall, each one holding its own tiny lit village inside it, a long glowing gold paper-chain garland of angels linked hand to hand curving right across the ceiling from one corner to the other, whole flights of glowing gold robins and doves crossing in loose Vs at three different depths, glowing gold ribbons of ivy and holly with bright red berries winding up every corner of the room, and a slow steady rise of glowing gold sparks lifting off the village chimneys and climbing the full height of the wall to join the star field, so every surface is so full that the eye cannot rest on any single thing. It stays ONE continuous night-sky picture, richly packed and busy, not scattered separate icons. THE PALETTE IS WARM: warm gold, cream white, deep Christmas red, emerald green and soft rose, richly saturated against the pale plaster and the dark walnut rafters. NO cold colours - no cyan, no teal, no electric blue, no violet, no grey. It must NOT look like outer space, a nebula, a galaxy, a spiral vortex, a tunnel or anything science-fiction, alien or dystopian - it is a warm storybook Christmas night sky. Every element is a separate glowing shape sitting on the surface - nothing is painted, printed, stencilled or wallpapered, and nothing is a flat repeating texture. HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right: it is projected light landing on real plaster and real timber, not paint and not a sticker. The light is TRANSLUCENT - the plaster and its fine surface texture, and every dark walnut rafter, every collar beam and the ridge line of the vault, all stay clearly visible THROUGH the coloured light, and the rafters and the collar beams break the light with their own hard shadow lines where they stand proud. Every shape is soft-edged and feathered with no hard opaque border, and is keystoned, stretched and skewed by the surface it lands on. The light falls off with distance: brightest where the beam first strikes, then steadily fainter, softer and paler, with the far corners fading to bare plaster. Even packed full it must still read as projected light on a real plastered vault with real timber rafters crossing it, never as paint, a sticker or a printed panel. Three or four faint volumetric shafts of coloured light hang visibly in the air of the room, so the beam itself is seen in the space.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The warm oak floorboards, the greige rug, the grey sectional sofa, the round coffee table and the tree carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children catch that spill so their knitted jumpers read clearly.

CHANGE 5 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no round side table, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain rug and floor.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, tack sharp edge to edge, perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, nothing blurry or soft, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

det.label: Clip prompt · v8_c07_g1.mp4
det.text:
Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas.

SUMMARY: two children play in a double-height Christmas great room while a projected snow-village picture is PLAYING across the back wall and the whole vaulted plaster ceiling and its dark timber rafters, thrown there by a projector standing in the room. 4 seconds, one continuous handheld phone take, vertical.

GLOBAL STYLE: crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed. Sharp and in focus from the first frame to the last, at least as sharp as the start image. No blur, no haze, no soft focus, no washed-out exposure, no colour shift.

ASSET ROLES: @Image 1 is frame 0.0s and controls the great room, the cathedral vault of cream plaster and its two pairs of dark walnut-stained rafters and collar beams, the open-tread pale oak staircase and its garlanded glass railing on the right, the tall arched window high on the right with snow outside, the pale plaster back wall with its black arched glazed door and wreath, the lit Christmas tree with its bright red and antique silver ornaments and its presents, the pale grey sectional sofa wrapping the right foreground, the round dark wood coffee table, the greige rug, the warm oak plank floor, the children and the colour.

SUBJECTS:
THE SMALLER CHILD - a boy of about five with short dark brown hair, on the rug at the front left, back to camera, facing the wall, turning on the spot with his arms out.
THE OTHER CHILD - a girl of about eight with long dark brown hair in two loose braids, standing up on the sofa cushions in front of the garlanded staircase on the right, back to camera, with both arms raised toward the wall, bouncing on the spot.
Both in warm dove-blue and cream nordic knitted Christmas jumpers with a row of cream stags across the yoke, charcoal knitted lounge trousers and thick red knitted socks, so their knitted jumpers read clearly. Exactly two children. No third child, no adult, no pet.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running in the room, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the back wall and the whole vaulted ceiling. Everything glowing on the plaster and the timber is that one cone landing.
THE PICTURE - the animated scene that cone is playing: a snow village across the back wall with snow-covered cottages with lit windows, a church with a tall steeple, snow-laden pines and a frozen pond, thin curls of smoke above their chimneys, ribbons of aurora in warm gold, emerald green and deep rose arching over the back wall and across the vault, Santa's sleigh drawn by eight flying reindeer with a long tapering trail keystoned on the ceiling at the upper left, a colossal glowing gold hot-air balloon shaped like a great ribbed Christmas bauble with lit lanterns hung round its wicker basket and a long ribbon of light streaming down behind it, three smaller balloons climbing behind it at three different depths, a big soft ivory full moon over on the right, one big brilliant north star, a dense field of warm gold five-point stars of many sizes, long-tailed shooting stars, red-and-cream striped candy canes, huge faceted six-point ice crystals, and a heavy fall of large soft glowing six-point snowflakes and tiny points of light.

HOW THE PICTURE BEHAVES - THIS IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE CLIP. In every previous attempt the picture sat dead still like printed wallpaper and the clip was worthless. THE PICTURE IS A FILM PLAYING ON A CINEMA SCREEN: the screen is the plaster and the timber and holds perfectly still, while everything inside the picture is in constant motion for all four seconds. The start image is one paused frame of that film; at 0.0s it un-pauses. Matching @Image 1 applies to the great room, the furniture, the children and the colours, not to where any element of the picture sits.
THE PICTURE AS A WHOLE IS ANCHORED. It does not rotate, spin, swing, sweep sideways or slide across the room as one sheet. Its outer boundary stays where it is. The motion lives INSIDE it, element by element:
- THE CHIMNEY SMOKE - every cottage chimney in the village is smoking. Each thin curl climbs upward out of its chimney pot, leaning slightly to the right, rising about one cottage-roof height every second, widening and thinning as it climbs and fading out before it reaches the aurora, while a fresh curl forms at the pot behind it. The plumes are never a fixed painted shape.
- THE RISING SPARKS - a slow steady rise of glowing gold sparks lifts off the village chimneys and climbs the full height of the wall to join the star field, drifting slightly sideways as it goes, new sparks leaving the chimneys continuously so the column never empties.
- THE AURORA - each ribbon ripples ALONG ITS OWN LENGTH, a slow travelling wave running from one end of the ribbon to the other, about a third of the ribbon's length every second, the ribbon swelling brighter and thinner as the wave passes and its lower fringe combing and re-forming. Each ribbon's overall arc stays where it is on the plaster; the wave inside it travels. Every ribbon on the wall and on the ceiling is doing this at the same time.
- THE SLEIGH AND THE REINDEER - they are FLYING. The team travels steadily across the ceiling away from where it sits in the start image, covering about a fifth of the ceiling's width every second, so by 4.0s it has crossed most of the way. The reindeer's legs gallop, their heads nod, the sleigh rocks gently behind them, the long tapering trail streams out behind, and the whole team rises and dips a little as it goes. The team is never parked.
- THE BALLOONS - the colossal gold bauble-shaped hot-air balloon CLIMBS. It rises steadily up the back wall and onto the vault, about a sixth of the wall's height every second, swaying very gently from side to side as it climbs; the lit lanterns hung round its wicker basket swing on their hooks and the long ribbon of light streaming down behind it ripples and trails. The three smaller balloons climb behind it at their three different depths, each at its own slightly slower rate, so the group opens out as it rises.
- THE SNOWFLAKES AND THE POINTS OF LIGHT - each one drifts downward and slightly sideways about a quarter of the wall's height every second, the way snow falls past a window at night. Each turns slowly on its own centre as it drifts and breathes brighter and dimmer on its own timing. One that reaches the floor line fades out there while a fresh one fades in high near the rafters, so the density holds even.
- THE SMALL TRAVELLERS - the red-and-cream striped candy canes turn slowly end over end as they drift down; the huge faceted six-point ice crystals turn slowly in place; the long-tailed shooting stars streak across, their tails thinning out behind them, and fade, with fresh ones setting off elsewhere.
- THE STAR FIELD - the small gold stars hold their places and twinkle, each brightening and dimming on its own timing, never all together.
- THE MOON AND THE NORTH STAR - these two are the ONLY elements that hold their positions. They stay exactly where they are on the right for the whole clip and only brighten and dim very slightly. Nothing else in the picture is allowed to hold still.
Because the back wall and the whole ceiling are lit by the SAME projector, they are one picture and behave identically at the same instant. Whatever the flakes, the aurora and the stars on the wall are doing, the flakes, the aurora and the stars on the ceiling are doing at the same moment and at the same speed. There is never a still ceiling above a moving wall. Nothing is painted, printed or stencilled on the plaster or the timber. NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR: the warm oak floorboards, the greige rug, the grey sectional sofa, the round coffee table, the tree and the gifts carry no projected shapes at all.

TIMELINE:
0.0-1.0s the person filming takes one clear step forward; the frame moves in and settles. THE OTHER CHILD bounces on the sofa cushions with both arms up, laughing. THE SMALLER CHILD turns on the rug with his face tipped up.
1.0-2.0s the camera holds in the closer position. THE OTHER CHILD pushes up harder and drops back down onto the cushion, her knees bending and springing back. THE SMALLER CHILD keeps turning and tips his head further back.
2.0-4.0s the camera tilts up in one slow smooth move past the top of the tree until the vaulted ceiling fills the upper half of the frame, the aurora rippling along it, the balloon still climbing into it and the sleigh team still flying across it. Both children stay low in the frame and keep moving.

AUDIO: room tone, two children laughing and squealing, feet thumping on the sofa cushions, feet on a rug. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS: real-time motion at normal speed throughout - real children moving at real speed with real weight. Exactly two children, and their knitted jumpers read clearly. One continuous take with no cut. The camera makes one move per beat and no more. The picture's outer boundary holds still while every element inside it moves. Walls and ceiling always move together. THE OTHER CHILD stays on the sofa. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.

DO NOT INCLUDE: a frozen or still pattern; chimneys that are not smoking; an aurora that sits still; a sleigh and reindeer parked in one place; a balloon that does not climb; flakes that only twinkle without travelling; a still ceiling above moving walls; the whole picture rotating, spinning, sweeping or sliding as one sheet; slow motion; floating or weightless movement; any music; children standing still; a third child; an adult; the projector unit in shot; jellyfish, fish, coral or bubbles; blur; a cut; on-screen text; subtitles.

det.label: Image prompt · v9_c01_g8.png
det.text:
Extremely high quality candid vertical iPhone photo taken from a hallway looking into a family's living room on a winter evening: a young mother kneels on the bare floor with a huge tangled knot of old multicoloured Christmas string lights in front of her, her arm stretched out to push the plug into a wall socket, while her two small children stand behind her watching the Christmas tree.

Use the attached reference photograph for BOTH the staging AND the camera position - the mother kneeling in the near foreground, the knot of lights on the floor beside her, her arm reaching out to the low wall socket, the two small children standing behind her, the tall Christmas tree on the right and the plain white wall corner the camera is looking past. COPY ITS CAMERA POSITION AND ITS COMPOSITION EXACTLY. Copy nothing else from it: the room, the mother and the children are all described below and are all different people in a different house.

FRAMING AND ANGLE - COPY THE CAMERA FROM THE REFERENCE: the camera is handheld at about the chest height of a standing adult, tilted very slightly down, standing in the next room and looking in through a doorway, so a plain white wall corner with a white skirting board runs floor to ceiling down the RIGHT EDGE of the frame and takes up roughly the right eighth of the picture - we are looking past it into the living room. The living room floor fills the bottom half of the frame and runs away into depth. The mother kneels in the lower LEFT of the frame, seen from behind at three quarters, close to the camera and large in the picture: her head and shoulders sit around the middle of the frame and the bottom edge of the picture cuts her just below the knees. The knot of lights lies on the bare floor immediately to her right, between her and that white wall corner, around the centre of the lower third of the picture. The Christmas tree stands on the RIGHT of the frame just inside the white corner, tall enough that the top edge of the picture cuts off its top. The two children stand on the floor in the middle distance between the mother and the tree, small in the frame, their heads in the middle third of the picture. Nobody is looking at the camera and nobody is posing. This is NOT a side angle, NOT a low floor-level angle and NOT a symmetrical composition.

THE KNOT AND THE PLUG: on the bare floorboards immediately to the mother's right lies a big ugly knot of old-fashioned Christmas string lights - dark green flex wound and knotted into a messy nest about the width of two floorboards across, studded with fat vintage multicoloured bulbs in red, green, blue and yellow, with a white in-line plug body and loops of slack wire lifting out of the top of it. She holds the end of that flex in her outstretched right hand and the two-pin plug is an inch from a white electrical socket set low on the white wall corner at the right of the frame. It is not plugged in yet and every bulb in the knot is dark.

THE CONNECTION - THIS IS THE IMPORTANT PART: one single continuous run of that SAME dark green flex with the SAME fat multicoloured bulbs leaves the far side of the knot, travels away across the floorboards to the right, passes behind the children, reaches the foot of the Christmas tree and climbs up into its lower branches, where it is plainly the very same string that is wound round and round the whole tree above. Same wire colour, same bulb size, same bulb spacing, one unbroken line. The eye must be able to follow the wire from the plug in her hand, through the knot on the floor, across the floor and up onto the tree without a single break or gap. The heap on the floor is NOT a separate loose pile with nothing leading out of it, and the tree is NOT wired to anything else.

THE TREE IS NOT SWITCHED ON: because the plug is still in her hand, every bulb on the tree is dark and unlit. The tree is not glowing, no light comes off it, and it throws no coloured light onto the floor, the walls or the children. It is still fully decorated and still reads as a beautiful Christmas tree - the baubles catch the warm lamplight in the room - it is simply not lit yet.

THE ROOM: a cosy American farmhouse living room. Walls of cream-white painted shiplap boards with white skirting, wide pale grey-washed pine floorboards running away from the camera, a deep navy-blue slipcovered sofa along the left wall with a mustard wool blanket folded over its back, a cream and charcoal flat-weave rug on the floor in front of it, an oak side table behind the sofa carrying a black ceramic table lamp with a white linen shade that is switched on and glowing, and a white-painted window with black muntins on the back wall showing a dark blue winter evening and snow on the sill outside.

THE TREE: a big real fir, dense and dark green, dressed with silver, white and pale blue glass baubles, cream knitted snowflakes, a wide cream linen ribbon wound down it and a silver star on top, with a heavy cream cable-knit tree skirt gathered round its base and four presents wrapped in white paper and green ribbon sitting on it.

THE MOTHER: about 28, long wavy honey-blonde hair falling loose past her shoulders, an oversized forest-green chunky cable-knit sweater with the sleeves pushed up her forearms, charcoal grey joggers and thick oatmeal socks, no shoes. She kneels sitting back on her heels, her left hand flat on the floorboards taking her weight, her right arm stretched right out towards the socket with the plug pinched between her thumb and fingers, her head turned in profile watching the plug. She is concentrating, slightly fed up, not smiling.

THE CHILDREN: a boy of about seven standing on the rug behind his mother, straight light-brown hair, red-and-white striped pyjamas, barefoot, his mouth wide open in a huge exaggerated gasp of amazement and both hands up near his cheeks, staring at the tree. Beside him a girl of about four with blonde hair in two short pigtails, a cream flannel nightgown printed with tiny red hearts, crouched down on one knee with her right arm flung out pointing straight at the tree. Neither child blocks the mother, the knot of lights or the tree.

COLOUR: warm domestic evening white balance, the way an iPhone renders a lamp-lit living room - warm but not orange. The picture is NOT sepia, NOT amber-washed and NOT heavily graded. Skin reads natural, the white wall corner reads clean white, the floorboards read as real wood and the sweater reads as true forest green.

LIGHTING AND QUALITY: the room is lit by the warm table lamp plus soft ambient light - cosy and warm, but still bright enough that every face, every twist of wire in the knot and the whole tree are clearly readable, with no dark corners where detail disappears and no blown highlights. Shot on an iPhone 16 Pro and straight out of the camera roll - an ordinary everyday snapshot somebody took of their family, not a magazine photo and not a rendered image. Extremely high quality, tack sharp and in focus everywhere from the mother in the foreground to the tree behind her, crisp detail in every individual bulb and every twist of flex in the tangle, realistic skin, hair and knitwear texture. Absolutely nothing blurry: no motion blur, no soft focus, no background blur, no bokeh, no grain, no film look, no cinematic grade, no vignette. Normal wide-angle lens, vertical lines vertical and parallel, no fisheye distortion.

FRAMING: leave the upper LEFT of the image - roughly the top eighth of the frame on the wall side - as plain uncluttered wall, free of pictures, shelves, garland, hanging decorations and lettering, so a caption can sit there. Do not pull the camera back or shrink the mother to make that room.

No captions, no watermarks, no added lettering anywhere in the image, no writing on any clothing, no user-interface elements, no mute or speaker icons and no social-media overlays.

det.text:
Single continuous handheld iPhone shot, 5 seconds, vertical 9:16, hyperrealistic. No cuts, no zoom, no slow motion, no speed ramp. The camera itself IS the phone being held by a man standing in the hallway doorway, so we see ONLY what he sees. No phone, no screen, no hand, no fingers, no thumb, no arm, no sleeve, no device and no object ever appears in the foreground or along any edge of the frame.

Start frame: a blonde mother in a forest-green cable-knit sweater kneels on pale wooden floorboards in the lower left, her right arm stretched out to a white wall socket on the white corner at the right of the frame, holding the plug of a big tangled knot of unlit multicoloured Christmas string lights that lies on the floor beside her. One continuous run of that same string leads away across the floor and up into the decorated but unlit Christmas tree standing on the right. A boy in red-and-white striped pyjamas and a small girl in a cream nightgown stand behind her near the navy sofa.

ACTION TIMELINE:
0.0-0.8s - The mother pushes the plug the last few centimetres into the socket. Her hand moves slowly and steadily, her head still turned in profile watching it. Everything else in the room is calm and still. The tree is dark. The camera is locked where it stands in the start frame, only natural handheld sway.

AT 0.8s - ONE SINGLE INSTANT, AND EVERYTHING IN IT HAPPENS ON THE SAME FRAME. The two pins seat in the socket; every bulb on the knot and on the tree flashes on for a split second; and in that same instant a burst of orange flame erupts low in the Christmas tree where the string meets the branches and the tree catches fire. On that exact same frame the man holding the camera shouts "Oh, shoot" and the whole frame jolts as he flinches backwards. The fire is not delayed, it does not build up, it does not start small and grow for a second first - the tree is already burning on the same frame the plug goes in.

0.8-2.0s - The flames climb the tree fast and realistically, running up through the dry branches, orange and yellow, throwing real flickering firelight across the shiplap walls, the floorboards, the sofa and the three faces, with dark smoke rolling up off the top of the tree toward the ceiling. Ornaments glow and the branches blacken. The mother recoils hard away from the socket, twists round onto her hands and pushes herself up off the floor. The boy and the girl scream and turn toward the camera. The man with the camera takes ONLY TWO OR THREE SHORT STEPS BACKWARDS and then stops and stands his ground. That small retreat is finished by about 1.6s. He does not walk backwards down the hallway, he does not run, he does not retreat any further at any later point in the clip.

2.0-5.0s - The camera is now STANDING STILL in the hallway just behind the doorway, holding its position with only natural handheld sway, not moving backwards at all. The mother is on her feet and runs straight toward the camera with her arms out, scooping the two children ahead of her, all three sprinting toward the lens and growing rapidly larger in the frame, faces wide with panic, the boy's arms pumping, the little girl half carried. Because the camera is no longer backing away, they close the distance fast and come right up to the lens. End frame: the three of them very close and very large in the frame mid-run, almost filling it, the burning tree bright behind them through the doorway.

AUDIO: natural room sound only. One male voice, off camera behind the lens, shouting "Oh, shoot" exactly on the frame the tree catches fire - nothing else from him before it, nothing else after it. Then the crackle and roar of the fire, the mother shouting wordlessly, the two children screaming, bare feet running on wood. NO music, no score, no background song, no narration, no added sound effects beyond these.

REALISM - HARD RULES: the mother, the boy and the girl keep exactly the same faces, hair, clothes and body shapes as the start frame throughout. The room stays the same room - same cream shiplap walls, same navy sofa with the mustard blanket, same pale floorboards, same rug, same lamp, same window. The fire behaves like real fire on a real dry conifer: it spreads along branches, it does not float, it does not appear as a glowing overlay, it casts real moving light and real shadows on every surface, and it produces real dark smoke. Real phone-camera look with slight sensor noise and natural motion blur only from the handheld movement. No text overlays, no captions, no watermark, no on-screen graphics.

POSITIVE LOCKS: one continuous take from 0.0s to 5.0s with no cut anywhere. Everything plays at real-time speed. The camera never zooms. The ONLY camera movement in the entire clip is a short backwards flinch of two or three steps between 0.8s and 1.6s; before 0.8s the camera holds its start-frame position and after 1.6s the camera holds its new position and stays there until the end. BANNED: the camera walking or running backwards down the hallway, the camera retreating for more than three steps, the camera moving away from the family during their run, the family staying the same size in the frame as they run. Nobody stops moving once the fire starts.

Recreate @Image 1's camera, light quality and style in a completely different room, with a much bigger projection. @Image 1 owns the camera, the framing, the poses and the light. @Image 2 is a photograph of a REAL AMERICAN HOUSE and owns the architecture of the room and nothing else - its two sloping painted-drywall ceiling planes, its dark ridge beam, its dark rafter beams, its white board-and-batten wainscot, its stacked-stone fireplace chimney breast, its white-railed loft balcony, its white crown moulding and its proportions are to be copied as built; ignore its daylight, its lamps, its time of day and the fact that it is not decorated.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing of a whole tall room seen from a doorway, the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two children - a boy standing TURNED AROUND FACING THE CAMERA, front-on, his face fully visible and lit by the coloured light, looking towards the lens with a delighted open-mouthed smile, arms slightly out in wonder, and a girl beside him seen from behind, still looking up at the projected wall.

Both children are fully dressed for winter in warm rust-red and cream nordic knitted Christmas jumpers with a row of cream snowflakes across the yoke, matching charcoal knitted lounge trousers and thick oatmeal knitted socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas.

CHANGE 1 - THE ROOM. The room is the real house photographed in @Image 2, seen from the doorway. Build its architecture exactly as it is built there, as a real room a real American builder made, and it must read unmistakably as an ordinary AMERICAN suburban family room - a Zillow-listing house in Connecticut, NOT a European chalet, NOT an alpine lodge, NOT a barn and NOT a rustic cabin: a tall two-storey family room whose ceiling is one big CATHEDRAL VAULT - two large flat sloping ceiling planes rising from the tops of the side walls and meeting at a single high ridge that runs the whole length of the room away from the camera, both slopes SMOOTH WARM-WHITE PAINTED DRYWALL with no planking and no boards; one heavy dark-walnut-stained ridge beam runs the full length of the apex, and four evenly spaced dark-walnut-stained beams run up each slope from the top of the side wall to that ridge beam like rafters, every beam chunky and square-edged and standing well clear of the drywall behind it, with small round recessed can lights set into the slopes between them; the side walls are smooth warm-white painted drywall above a white-painted BOARD-AND-BATTEN wainscot that runs right round the room to about chest height, evenly spaced vertical white battens standing proud of the wall with a flat white cap rail along the top and a white baseboard below, and wide white crown moulding and white trim throughout; at the far end a floor-to-ceiling STACKED LEDGESTONE fireplace chimney breast rises the full height into the gable, with a thick chunky dark wood mantel across it and a wide black rectangular firebox below; high on the right-hand side a short second-floor loft balcony overlooks the room behind a white-painted railing of square white balusters; there are only two modest windows in the whole room, both set low on the left-hand wall, ordinary American double-hung windows with white grilles and wide white casing, and there is no glazed wall and no glazed gable anywhere. Wide light-oak plank floor, a very large light-grey fabric sectional sofa with a big matching ottoman filling the middle of the room, and a large jute rug under it. Copy the proportions, the two sloping drywall planes, the high ridge beam, the rafter beams, the board-and-batten wainscot, the stacked-stone fireplace and the white loft railing from @Image 2 exactly - this is a photograph of a room that exists, and the finished picture must still read as that room.

TWO THINGS CHANGE FROM @Image 2. First, it is night: the two low double-hung windows show a dark blue snow-covered night outside, there is no daylight anywhere in the room, every recessed can light and every lamp in the house is switched off and dark, and the projection is the only light. Second, the room is decorated for Christmas: a tall real Christmas tree standing beside the stacked-stone chimney breast with warm white lights and rust-red and antique gold ornaments and wrapped gifts beneath it, a thick evergreen garland with pine cones and rust-red velvet ribbon laid along the chunky wood mantel, cream knitted stockings hanging from that mantel, and a large evergreen wreath with a rust-red velvet bow hung on the stacked-stone chimney breast above the mantel. Nothing else about the room changes.

CHANGE 2 - THE PROJECTION, and this is the part that matters most. It is ONE enormous cinematic Christmas night scene - a single continuous picture, NOT scattered floating icons - and it is far bigger, denser and more beautiful than in @Image 1. It reads as one unbroken field across both painted drywall side walls and the white board-and-batten wainscot below them, across the stacked-stone chimney breast, across the white loft railing, and across both sloping drywall ceiling planes right up to the ridge, and over every face of the ridge beam and of every rafter beam crossing them, with no visible edge, no rectangle and no screen. NO SURFACE IN THE ROOM IS LEFT BARE. Every square inch of wall and ceiling the camera can see is inside the projection, and that explicitly includes THE TALL STACKED-STONE CHIMNEY BREAST ABOVE THE FIREPLACE: the picture crosses it from the mantel shelf all the way up to the ceiling ridge exactly as densely as it crosses everything else, so that stone carries lit forest, city, aurora ribbons, stars and drifting gifts across it and is NEVER a bare grey or brown column running up the middle of the frame. The same is true of the lower halves of both side walls, the white board-and-batten wainscot, the wall above and behind the white loft railing, the soffit under the loft floor, the strips of wall between and beside the windows, and the wall on the right - every one of them carries the picture at full density right down to where it meets the floor. If any wall or ceiling surface anywhere in the frame reads as plain paint, plain drywall or plain stone, the image is wrong. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a deep snow-laden pine forest running the whole width of the room along the very bottom of the projection, rank behind rank of little glowing firs in emerald green and warm gold with snow heaped on every branch, and rising straight out of that forest on the left a whole ornate fairy-tale Christmas city built of lit gold - tier upon tier of slender spires, ribbed onion domes, arched galleries and pinnacled towers stacked up the wall, every arched window lit warm gold, fine gold filigree running along every cornice and balustrade, thick snow lying on every ledge and roof and dome, the whole city glowing as though it were carved out of light; and winding out of the pines on the right a long lit steam train, a dark locomotive leading eight carriages whose windows all glow warm gold, a bright plume of steam and sparks trailing back over the carriage roofs and a glowing gold rail curving away behind it through the trees; ABOVE THE FOREST AND THE CITY, wide soft aurora ribbons in deep Christmas crimson and glowing ruby red, with warm gold, emerald green and rose magenta threaded between them and only a thin thread of teal, sweeping up the walls in long slow curves and carrying over onto both sloping ceiling planes, five or six broad overlapping bands layered over each other so there is very little bare surface left between them, each band shot through with a fine glittering grain so it reads as a river of stars rather than a painted stripe, where they lie flat ON the slopes and run up them with the direction of the slope instead of hanging as vertical curtains, visibly kinking and changing direction at the ridge beam where they cross from one slope onto the other, visibly stepping and breaking at every rafter beam they pass under, and visibly rippling across the raised white battens of the wainscot where they reach the lower wall, and several of these red and gold ribbons stream inward and feed into the mouth of the great spiral overhead; ACROSS BOTH CEILING SLOPES OVERHEAD, one colossal spiral whirlpool of light filling the whole vault with its centre sitting right on the ridge beam, so half of it lies on one slope and half on the other and every ring visibly bends where it crosses the ridge - seven concentric glowing rings of deep crimson, ruby red, warm gold and emerald green winding in on each other in a slow tightening spiral and drawing down to one brilliant white-gold core at the very centre, every ring built of countless tiny points of light so the whole thing reads as a whirlpool of stars rather than a painted disc; Santa's sleigh drawn by a team of eight flying reindeer sweeping straight out of the mouth of that spiral, seen side-on in glowing warm gold and large enough to read every antler, the harness and bells on each reindeer, the curved runners and Santa himself sitting up in the sleigh with his sack behind him, a long bright tapering trail of golden light streaming back behind the runners into the spiral, the whole team lying flat on one ceiling slope so it is keystoned and stretched by that slope's angle, foreshortening as it recedes along the room and broken into sections by the ridge beam and the rafter beams it passes under; a big pale blue full moon glowing high on one of the painted drywall side walls, cool silver-blue and softly cratered and the one cool-coloured thing in the whole picture, with the tiny black silhouette of a second sleigh and its reindeer team crossing right over the face of it; floating wrapped Christmas gifts drifting through the whole scene at five or six different depths and sizes, each a solid glowing box in gold, emerald or rose with a bright ribbon cross and a big soft bow on top, the nearest big enough to read the weave of the ribbon, all of them turning slowly end over end as they drift; a dense field of stars at many different sizes, hundreds of them, from tiny pinpricks to a few large bright ones with soft radiating rays, with four or five long-tailed shooting stars crossing at different angles with bright tapering trails; large soft glowing six-point snowflakes in cream and pale gold at several different sizes, the nearest big enough to read every arm, drifting across both ceiling slopes and both side walls; faint wisps of glowing crimson and gold cloud between the aurora bands; and over all of it a heavy fall of hundreds of tiny bright points of light drifting down the walls like real snow caught in a beam. It stays ONE continuous night-sky picture, richly packed and busy, not scattered separate icons. THE PALETTE IS LED BY RED. Deep Christmas crimson and glowing ruby red are the dominant colours of the entire picture, warm gold is second, then emerald green, cream white and rose magenta; soft teal survives only as a thin accent inside one or two of the aurora bands. The aurora ribbons are mostly crimson and ruby with gold and emerald threaded between them, the outer rings of the great spiral are deep red winding in to a gold core, the fairy-tale city glows red-gold, the train's carriage windows burn red-gold, and most of the floating gifts are crimson and gold. Everything is richly saturated, and the single pale blue moon is the only cool note anywhere in it. NO grey, no muddy brown, no violet and no harsh electric blue. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn. The great spiral is an AURORA WHIRLPOOL made of Christmas light with a sleigh flying out of its mouth, not a space nebula: it must NOT look like outer space, a galaxy, a wormhole, a tunnel or anything science-fiction, alien or dystopian - it is a storybook Christmas night sky with a lit gold Christmas city, a steam train, flying reindeer and falling gifts in it. Every element is a separate glowing shape sitting on the surface - nothing is painted, printed, stencilled or wallpapered, and nothing is a flat repeating texture. HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely. The white painted drywall, the white battens and the pale stone do NOT read as white anywhere inside the projection field - the light has swallowed their colour. The only things that survive through it are the surface's TEXTURE and its SHADOWS: the slight tooth of the drywall, the joints and edges, the mortar lines of the stone, the square corners of the beams and battens. That is the ten percent; the colour of the surface is not part of it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white. Contrast is extreme: the cores of the gold city, the train, the spiral and the stars are near-white hot, the mid-tones are deep saturated crimson and emerald, and the empty sky between them is almost black - never pale paint. AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on. Each of the two ceiling slopes is a separate plane at its own angle, and every shape lying on a slope is keystoned and skewed by THAT plane's perspective, so the same aurora band is stretched differently on the left slope than on the right. Every band, every ring of the spiral and every large shape that crosses the ridge visibly FOLDS at the ridge line, changing direction there with a clean kink, exactly like a picture projected across the inside of a tent. Where the light reaches the top of a side wall it breaks again at that corner and runs down the vertical plane at a different angle. The ridge beam and every rafter beam interrupt it: the face of each beam that points back toward the projector catches its own bright slice of the picture, offset and stepped from the piece on the drywall behind it, while the underside and the far side of every beam sit in hard unlit shadow, so the whole ceiling reads as a lit vault ribbed by dark beams and never as one flat painted mural. The white board-and-batten wainscot breaks it again, every raised batten catching its own bright vertical strip and throwing its own shadow so the picture ripples across the lower wall in a row of ribs. The stacked-stone chimney breast breaks it a third time, every stone catching the light on its own face and throwing its own small shadow, and the white loft railing breaks it a fourth, each square baluster catching a bright edge and casting a bar of shadow onto the wall behind it. The surface texture stays legible inside the light - the tooth of the drywall, the square edges of the beams and battens, the mortar joints of the stone - so it still reads as projected light on a real room and never as paint, wallpaper, a sticker or a printed panel. AND EVERY PIECE OF STANDING-PROUD TIMBER AND TRIM THROWS A REAL SHADOW: each chunky beam and each raised batten casts a hard-edged shadow of itself across the surface behind it, so a dark unlit band runs alongside every beam and every batten where the picture is blocked. Those cast shadows are the clearest proof that this is light crossing a real room and not a mural, and they must be plainly visible. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the top corners of the vault, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room. Three or four thin volumetric shafts of coloured light hang visibly in the air of the room so the beam itself is seen in the space, but they are narrow and crisply defined and they do NOT fog, veil or soften any part of the picture. EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP. Each spire and arched window of the gold city, each carriage window of the train, each antler and harness bell on each reindeer, each arm of each snowflake, each ribbon and bow on each floating gift and each ring of the great spiral has a hard, crisp, precisely drawn edge. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 3 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The light-oak floorboards, the jute rug, the light-grey sectional sofa, the big ottoman, the tree and the gifts carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no city, no train, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children's faces and their knitted jumpers catch that spill so both faces read clearly.

CHANGE 4 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no side table, no stool, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain floor and the edge of the jute rug.
