ASSET ROLES: @Image 1 is frame 0.0s and controls a tall double-height New England Christmas great room with a simple steep CATHEDRAL CEILING: two broad smooth cream-plaster roof planes meeting in one straight high central ridge, crossed by three dark stained-oak horizontal collar beams at even intervals, no curved cathedral ceiling and no coffer grid. The back wall is a tall triangular gable with a central chimney breast of small warm-grey fieldstones and a thick oak mantel; three tall rectangular white-framed windows stand on the left and a square opening into a dining room is on the right. Natural honey-oak floorboards, a large cream boucle sectional sofa, a low rectangular upholstered ottoman and a muted cranberry wool rug. Preserve the exact furniture placement, child identities, clothing, room colours and framing in that supplied image.

SUBJECTS:
THE SMALLER CHILD - a boy of about five with light skin, freckles and tousled auburn hair, on the rug in front of the sofa, back to camera and slightly to the side, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling with his arms out in wonder, turning slowly on the spot.
THE OTHER CHILD - a girl of about eight with warm tan skin and straight dark-brown hair in two loose braids. Preserve her airborne opening pose, then complete that jump with a small natural inward landing on the broad flat seat cushion INSIDE the sofa, beyond the near backrest. Both feet land fully supported near the cushion centre. She continues small vertical bounces over this same broad cushion centre with natural knee flexion, balanced arms and visible cushion compression. She never lands or balances on the narrow top of the backrest, armrest, cushion seam or outer edge. Keep normal anatomy and consistent limb proportions; no twisting legs, floating feet or furniture intersection.
Both in warm forest-green and cream knitted Christmas jumpers with red holly berries and white reindeer, cream knitted lounge trousers and thick red socks. Both stay small in frame, in scale with the huge room. Exactly two children. No third child, no adult, no pet.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running in the room, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the back wall and the whole cathedral ceiling. Everything glowing on the plaster, wall material and ceiling details is that one cone landing.
THE PICTURE - the animated scene is the exact Christmas panorama visible in the start image. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, one continuous SNOWY CHRISTMAS VILLAGE ON CHRISTMAS EVE: glowing red-and-cream wooden houses, a tall candlelit village church, little shops dressed in holly and scarlet bows, garland-lined cobbled lanes, children in winter coats carrying wrapped presents and a tiny choir with songbooks beneath a gold-lit Christmas tree. A horse-drawn red gift wagon loaded with ribboned parcels passes the village square. The whole lower panorama is packed with festive detail, snowy firs, frosted shop windows, candy canes and candle lanterns. High on the walls, enormous ornate gold Christmas bells and evergreen wreaths tied with crimson velvet bows. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight gold-lit reindeer follow a graceful arc around one brilliant eight-point Christmas star; long woven trails of holly, red ribbon, gilded baubles and tiny ivory snowflakes spread across both roof planes. The dominant colours are deep Christmas crimson and ruby red, rich gold, evergreen green and cream-white detail against deep midnight sky. No Ferris wheel, no carousel, no nebula, no abstract space vortex. This is one coherent Christmas story illustrated as projected light, not physical props. Every projected shape and flake lies on the walls or ceiling only.

HOW THE PICTURE BEHAVES - THIS IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE CLIP. In every previous attempt the picture sat dead still like printed wallpaper and the clip was worthless. THE PICTURE IS A FILM PLAYING ON A CINEMA SCREEN: the screen is the plaster, wall material and ceiling details and holds perfectly still, while everything inside the picture is in constant motion for all four seconds. The start image shows the film already fully projected across the walls AND the entire ceiling. From the first frame continue the moving artwork at the same full coverage and brightness. Start motion within the existing picture, never the appearance of the picture itself. Matching @Image 1 applies to the great room, the furniture, the children and the colours, not to where any element of the picture sits.
THE PICTURE AS A WHOLE IS ANCHORED. It does not rotate, spin, swing, sweep sideways or slide across the room as one sheet. Its outer boundary stays where it is. The motion lives INSIDE it, element by element:
- THE CHIMNEY SMOKE - every single chimney in the village is smoking, not one of them without its plume. Each thin curl climbs upward out of its chimney pot, leaning slightly to the right, rising about one roof height every second, widening and thinning as it climbs and fading out before it reaches the ribbons, while a fresh curl forms at the pot behind it. The plumes are never a fixed painted shape.
- THE RISING SPARKS - a slow steady rise of glowing gold sparks lifts off the village chimneys and climbs the full height of the wall to join the star field, drifting slightly sideways as it goes, new sparks leaving the chimneys continuously so the column never empties.
- THE RIBBONS - each crimson, ruby, gold and emerald ribbon radiates outward from the great star and ripples ALONG ITS OWN LENGTH, a slow travelling wave running down the band away from the star, about a third of the ribbon's length every second, the ribbon swelling brighter and thinner as the wave passes and its lower fringe combing and re-forming. Each ribbon's overall fan stays where it is on the plaster; the wave inside it travels. Every ribbon on the wall and on the ceiling is doing this at the same time.
- THE SLEIGH AND THE REINDEER - they are FLYING. The team travels steadily across the ceiling on a long sweeping curve away from where it sits in the start image, arcing in toward the great star, covering about a fifth of the ceiling's width every second, so by 4.0s it has crossed most of the way. The reindeer's legs gallop, their heads nod, the sleigh rocks gently behind them, the long tapering trail streams out behind, and the whole team rises and dips a little as it goes. The team is never parked.
- THE GIFT WAGON AND THE VILLAGERS. The red gift wagon travels along the lower wall; its wheels turn and its horse walks at a steady pace, about one wagon length every second. The projected village children walk through the lanes carrying parcels, while the tiny choir gestures with songbooks. All are flat moving drawings on the wall. All keep moving from the first frame to the last.
- THE GOLD LIGHT WAVES. Successive bright gold waves TRAVEL OUTWARD along the existing red-and-gold ribbon and evergreen-garland paths on the ceiling, each bright crest travelling about a third of its ribbon's length every second, fading behind as the next bright crest follows, so the existing ribbons sparkle and flow continuously. No new rings or new objects appear; the moving light stays within the shapes that already exist in the image.
- THE SNOWFLAKES AND THE POINTS OF LIGHT - each one drifts downward and slightly sideways about a quarter of the wall's height every second, the way snow falls past a window at night. Each turns slowly on its own centre as it drifts and breathes brighter and dimmer on its own timing. One that reaches the floor line fades out there while a fresh one fades in high near the plaster ceiling details, so the density holds even.
- THE SMALL TRAVELLERS - the red-and-white striped candy canes and the glowing baubles turn slowly end over end as they drift; the tiny village children keep passing gifts beside the village and the big gold bells swing gently on their crimson bow with the clappers moving inside them; the long-tailed shooting stars streak across, their tails thinning out behind them, and fade, with fresh ones setting off elsewhere.
- THE STAR FIELD - the small gold stars hold their places and twinkle, each brightening and dimming on its own timing, never all together.
- THE GREAT CHRISTMAS STAR - the gold eight-pointed star is the ONLY element that holds its centre position. It stays exactly where it is on the ceiling for the whole clip and only brightens and dims very slightly. Nothing else in the picture is allowed to hold still.
Because the back wall and the whole ceiling are lit by the SAME projector, they are one picture and behave identically at the same instant. Whatever the flakes, the ribbons and the stars on the wall are doing, the flakes, the ribbons and the stars on the ceiling are doing at the same moment and at the same speed. There is never a still ceiling above a moving wall. Nothing is painted, printed or stencilled on the plaster, wall material and ceiling details. NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR: the pale oak floorboards, the muted cranberry wool rug, the cream boucle sectional sofa, the long ottoman, the tree and the gifts carry no projected shapes at all.

TIMELINE:
0.0-1.0s the person filming takes one clear step forward; the frame moves in and settles. THE OTHER CHILD completes the opening jump with an inward landing onto the centre of the broad seat cushion, both feet fully supported, knees absorbing the landing, laughing. THE SMALLER CHILD turns on the rug with his face tipped up.
1.0-2.0s the camera holds in the closer position. THE OTHER CHILD makes a small balanced vertical bounce directly above that same broad seat-cushion centre and lands there on both feet, her knees bending naturally and the cushion compressing. THE SMALLER CHILD keeps turning and tips his head further back.
2.0-4.0s the camera tilts up in one slow smooth move past the top of the tree until the cathedral ceiling fills the upper half of the frame, the ribbons rippling along it, the travelling gold light waves still spreading outward across it from the great star and the sleigh team still flying in toward that star. Both children stay low in the frame and keep moving.

AUDIO: room tone, two children laughing and squealing, feet thumping on the sofa cushions, feet on a rug. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS: real-time motion at normal speed throughout - real children moving at real speed with real weight. Exactly two children, and their knitted jumpers read clearly. One continuous take with no cut. The camera makes one move per beat and no more. The picture's outer boundary holds still while every element inside it moves. Walls and ceiling always move together. THE OTHER CHILD stays on the sofa. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.

DO NOT INCLUDE: blank or partly blank walls or ceiling at the start; a projection appearing, switching on, fading in, spreading, growing or revealing itself during the shot; an opening before-and-after transformation; a frozen or still pattern; chimneys that are not smoking; an ribbons that sits still; a sleigh and reindeer parked in one place; a gift wagon that does not travel or villagers that do not move; travelling gold light waves that do not spread outward; flakes that only twinkle without travelling; a still ceiling above moving walls; an un-animated area of the cathedral ceiling or an un-animated ceiling detail in any frame; the whole picture rotating, spinning, sweeping or sliding as one sheet; slow motion; floating or weightless movement; any music; children standing still; a third child; an adult; the projector unit in shot; jellyfish, fish, coral or bubbles; blur; a cut; on-screen text; subtitles.

CONTINUOUS MOTION CHECK - from the first visible frame through the very last frame, the wall AND ceiling each contain clearly travelling projected elements at the same time: the sleigh changes position across the ceiling, its reindeer gallop; the gift wagon advances along the wall; villagers move and pass gifts; bells swing; ribbons carry travelling light waves; snowflakes translate across the surfaces. Twinkle alone and camera movement alone do not count. Maintain that same lively real-time motion with no opening freeze, no settling into a still image and no final freeze. All light bends with the real wall and ceiling geometry and stays on those surfaces.

SURFACE MAPPING - The two sloping ceiling planes remain plainly visible. Projected garlands, the sleigh trail and snowflakes change perspective at the straight roof ridge, folding across it and foreshortening differently on the left and right roof slopes. Each dark oak collar beam catches light on its near face and casts a narrow real shadow on the plaster beyond; projected elements break and resume with a visible offset across the beam. Imagery bends again at each wall-to-roof junction and both corners of the projecting fieldstone chimney; tiny stone faces and recessed mortar retain their texture under the luminous image. All physical walls, ceiling planes, beams, seams and trim remain stationary.

The SECOND attached image is only a photographic-look reference for clear natural iPhone detail, realistic materials and colour; do not copy its people, room or composition. The new people and room are specified below. Preserve the FIRST image's composition.

Extremely high quality candid vertical iPhone photo taken from the floor of a double-height Christmas living room, looking up and across at a woman standing on the mezzanine landing, evening. We see her from below and slightly to the side, her raised arms and the high ceiling in front of her.

FRAMING AND ANGLE: the camera stands on the living-room floor MUCH closer in to the stairs than a wide establishing shot, tilted up, so the woman and the inflatable she is taping fill most of the picture and the room reads as context around them rather than as the subject. The mezzanine landing crosses the frame with its black metal railing along it, and the woman stands on that landing behind the railing DEAD CENTRE on the vertical axis of the frame, framed from roughly the waist up and very large in the picture - she is the biggest thing in the photograph and the taped inflatable is directly above and ahead of her, also near the centre, so her reaching arm and the inflatable together sit in the middle of the frame. A short stretch of the open white staircase still enters the lower right corner, and the living-room floor is still clearly visible below her in the lower part of the picture, so the drop from the landing to the floor reads plainly. She is NOT on a ladder - there is no ladder anywhere in the picture.

THE KEY ELEMENT: a large inflatable Santa Claus decoration is TAPED FLAT TO THE HIGH WHITE CEILING above the double-height space, lying on its back against the plaster and facing down into the room, held by a mess of criss-crossed silver duct tape strips over its legs, arms and hat. It is clearly fixed to the ceiling. It hangs out over the open double-height void rather than over the landing. One corner has started to peel, with a long strip of tape hanging down.

HER POSE - THIS IS THE POINT OF THE PICTURE: she is leaning far out over the landing railing to reach it. Her hips are pressed against the top rail, her weight is tipped forward past it and out over the open void, her feet still on the landing behind her with her heels lifting, one hand gripping the rail and the other stretched up and out pressing a fresh strip of silver duct tape onto Santa's shoulder, a roll of duct tape in her gripping hand. She is visibly overreaching and off balance, the rail the only thing holding her, empty air and the floor below her.

THE ROOM: a double-height American transitional living room - pale dove-grey painted walls with white picture-frame moulding, a wall of tall black-framed windows at the right with a dark winter garden behind them, a white open-tread staircase with slim black metal spindles, a mezzanine landing with a matching black rail and a green garland with red bows wound along it, a pale limestone fireplace on the ground floor, a tall green Christmas tree with warm white lights and red and gold baubles standing in the double-height space, honey-oak wide-plank floor, a camel linen sofa and a muted blue and cream rug.

A UNITED STATES FLAG: a real fabric United States flag hangs flat against the pale dove-grey wall in the background under the landing, clearly readable stars and stripes, hanging straight and still, about the size of a large poster. It does not cover the Christmas tree or the fireplace and it does not reach up into the empty band of ceiling at the top of the frame.

HER CLOTHES: matching American-flag Christmas pyjamas - a pyjama top with bold red and white horizontal stripes and a navy blue yoke across the shoulders covered in small white stars, and matching red and white striped pyjama bottoms, soft brushed cotton, slightly loose the way real pyjamas fit - with thick grey wool socks. She is early 30s with copper-red hair in a loose low bun, fair freckled skin and a softly rounded face.

There is no projected light anywhere - the ceiling, the walls and the staircase are plain painted plaster and plain timber, completely clean, no projected patterns, no snowflakes, no stars, no coloured light spilling on any surface. The room is lit only by the Christmas tree, the fireplace and ordinary warm lamps.

COLOUR - READ THIS CAREFULLY: neutral white balance, the way an iPhone auto-corrects a warm room. The picture is NOT orange, NOT amber, NOT sepia, NOT golden-hour, and there is no warm colour cast laid over the whole frame. The ceiling reads as clean white paint and the walls as pale dove-grey paint, the window frames and the rail read as true black, the oak floor reads as natural wood, the flag keeps true red, white and navy. The Christmas tree lights, the fireplace and the lamps are warm points of light sitting inside a neutrally balanced room - they do not tint the rest of the picture.

LIGHTING AND QUALITY: bright, clean and evenly lit - plenty of light on the high ceiling, on the landing and on her, no dark corners, no heavy shadows. Shot on an iPhone and straight out of the camera roll: an ordinary everyday snapshot, not a magazine photo and not a rendered image. Modern phone-camera look - wide dynamic range, lifted shadows, clean highlights, accurate colour. Extremely high quality, tack sharp and in focus everywhere, crisp detail in the duct tape, the inflatable vinyl sheen and the weave of her pyjamas, realistic skin and fabric texture. Absolutely nothing blurry: no motion blur, no soft focus, no background blur, no grain, no film look, no cinematic grade, no vignette, no bloom. Normal wide-angle lens, vertical lines vertical and parallel, no fisheye distortion.

FRAMING: leave a generous clean band of plain empty ceiling across the very top of the image - roughly the top fifth of the frame - completely empty and free of Santa, of tape, of beams, of garland and of any other object, so a caption can sit there. Make that room by tilting the camera up slightly, NOT by pulling the camera back and NOT by shrinking the woman - she stays close and large and centred exactly as described above.

No captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

det.text:
Single continuous handheld iPhone shot, 5 seconds, vertical 9:16, filmed by someone standing on the living room floor below and holding the phone up — real held-phone look with natural handheld sway, no cuts, no zoom, no lens push-in, framing locked exactly as in the start frame for the whole clip.

Start frame: a woman in American-flag pajamas stands on the upstairs balcony, leaning her hips against the dark wooden top rail, both arms stretched up over her head, pressing strips of silver duct tape onto the white ceiling to hold up a big inflatable Santa. Below her: the two-storey living room with the lit fireplace, the American flag on the wall, the decorated Christmas tree and the white sofa.

ACTION TIMELINE:
0.0–1.0s — Up on her toes, she smooths one more strip of silver tape onto the ceiling with her palm, then gives the inflatable Santa a quick test tug to check it is holding, leaning her whole weight forward into the wooden top rail.
1.0–1.5s — The section of the dark wooden top rail she is leaning on splits with a loud crack and swings away from her, and she pitches forward over the balcony edge, eyes wide, both hands clamping onto the inflatable Santa.
1.5–2.5s — She drops down into the living room, the inflatable Santa peeling straight off the ceiling and coming with her — the silver tape strips tearing free and trailing, the green garland and a red bow sliding off the broken rail behind her.
2.5–3.4s — She misses the sofa completely and lands flat on her back on the wooden living room floor in front of it, hitting the floor and settling straight down with no bounce, and the big inflatable Santa flops down on top of her, covering her from the waist up.
3.4–5.0s — She shoves the inflatable Santa's head sideways off her face, hair everywhere, looks straight up at the camera and bursts out laughing, still flat on her back on the floor with the Santa across her lap. End frame: her laughing on the floor under the inflatable, the empty broken balcony rail above her.

AUDIO: her real voice, lip-synced, matching her appearance — a short surprised yelp as the rail gives way, then breathless laughing at the end; the sharp crack of splitting wood; duct tape ripping off the ceiling; the squeaky rubbery scuff of the big inflatable; the heavy flat thud of her body landing on the wooden floor; the fireplace crackling quietly under everything. (no BGM). No subtitles.

REALISM — HARD RULES: she keeps exactly the same face, hair and American-flag pajamas as the start frame the whole clip. The living room stays pixel-faithful to the start frame — same fireplace, same flag, same Christmas tree, same sofa, same windows, same warm lamp light. The inflatable Santa stays the same size, colours and printed face the whole clip and never deforms into a different character. Real weight and gravity on the fall — she drops straight down, she is never thrown or launched sideways. She lands on the wooden floor, NOT on the sofa - she never touches the sofa at any point in the clip. Real phone-camera look, slight sensor noise, mild motion blur on the fall, no cinematic bokeh, no slow motion, no text overlays, no watermark.

POSITIVE LOCKS: everything plays at real-time speed. One continuous take from 0.0s to 5.0s. The camera never moves from where it is in the start frame.

Whatever the flakes, the ribbons and the stars on the wall are doing, the flakes, the ribbons and the stars on the ceiling are doing at the same moment and at the same speed. There is never a still ceiling above a moving wall. Nothing is painted, printed or stencilled on the plaster, wall material and ceiling details. NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR: the pale oak floorboards, the dark-green woven wool rug, the curved ivory linen sectional sofa, the long ottoman, the tree and the gifts carry no projected shapes at all.

TIMELINE:
0.0-1.0s the person filming takes one clear step forward; the frame moves in and settles. THE OTHER CHILD bounces on the sofa cushions with both arms up, laughing. THE SMALLER CHILD turns on the rug with his face tipped up.
1.0-2.0s the camera holds in the closer position. THE OTHER CHILD pushes up harder and drops back down onto the cushion, her knees bending and springing back. THE SMALLER CHILD keeps turning and tips his head further back.
2.0-4.0s the camera tilts up in one slow smooth move past the top of the tree until the eight-facet pyramidal ceiling fills the upper half of the frame, the ribbons rippling along it, the travelling gold light waves still spreading outward across it from the great star and the sleigh team still flying in toward that star. Both children stay low in the frame and keep moving.

AUDIO: room tone, two children laughing and squealing, feet thumping on the sofa cushions, feet on a rug. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS: real-time motion at normal speed throughout - real children moving at real speed with real weight. Exactly two children, and their knitted jumpers read clearly. One continuous take with no cut. The camera makes one move per beat and no more. The picture's outer boundary holds still while every element inside it moves. Walls and ceiling always move together. THE OTHER CHILD stays on the sofa. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.

DO NOT INCLUDE: blank or partly blank walls or ceiling at the start; a projection appearing, switching on, fading in, spreading, growing or revealing itself during the shot; an opening before-and-after transformation; a frozen or still pattern; chimneys that are not smoking; an ribbons that sits still; a sleigh and reindeer parked in one place; a nutcracker parade that does not travel or elves that do not move; travelling gold light waves that do not spread outward; flakes that only twinkle without travelling; a still ceiling above moving walls; an un-animated area of the eight-facet pyramidal ceiling or an un-animated ceiling detail in any frame; the whole picture rotating, spinning, sweeping or sliding as one sheet; slow motion; floating or weightless movement; any music; children standing still; a third child; an adult; the projector unit in shot; jellyfish, fish, coral or bubbles; blur; a cut; on-screen text; subtitles.

CONTINUOUS MOTION CHECK - from the first visible frame through the very last frame, the wall AND ceiling each contain clearly travelling projected elements at the same time: the sleigh changes position across the ceiling, its reindeer gallop; the nutcracker parade advances along the wall; elves move and pass gifts; bells swing; ribbons carry travelling light waves; snowflakes translate across the surfaces. Twinkle alone and camera movement alone do not count. Maintain that same lively real-time motion with no opening freeze, no settling into a still image and no final freeze. All light bends with the real wall and ceiling geometry and stays on those surfaces.

SURFACE MAPPING - All eight triangular ceiling facets remain unmistakably separate real plaster planes. The red ribbons, garlands, sleigh trail and snowflakes visibly kink at every straight diagonal seam and narrow toward the central apex; every facet foreshortens the image at its own angle. Projected village buildings bend across each of the eight vertical room corners. The projecting chimney breast interrupts the village with clear bends at its two outside corners, and the window jambs and doorway lintel clip and offset the light. Raised trim throws narrow hard-edged shadows, never a seamless flat poster over the geometry. All physical walls, ceiling planes, beams, seams and trim remain stationary.

HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ THIS FIRST: the pictures on the walls and the coved ceiling are A MOVIE THAT IS PLAYING, not a pattern painted on the plaster. @Video 1 supplies the room design, children's identities and moving projection artwork only. It is a visual room reference, not a timeline or camera reference. No frame of it is a target frame for this clip. Smoke pours from every chimney, the ribbons radiates, the sleigh flies, the deer procession travels and the elves work, the travelling gold light waves spread, the snow falls - continuously, in every single frame. TASK: image-to-video, one continuous handheld phone POV take, vertical 9:16. Frame 0.0s is the start image: a natural dark-walnut six-panel solid wood door with two small square upper panels and four taller panels beneath, a satin wax finish and clearly visible walnut grain fully closed with a wreath, a hand on the brass knob. @Video 1 is a room-content reference for the layout, coved ceiling, furniture, the children's identities and clothes, colours, and moving projection artwork. Use the camera and child actions specified below, not the reference video's camera or its specific child actions. Only the closed-door start image defines frame 0.0s. No end frame is supplied.

PROJECTED FILM ACTION - THE MAIN SUBJECT IS THE MOVING CHRISTMAS ARTWORK. Animate the existing illustrated objects themselves, not just the camera, children, brightness or glitter. At every moment MOST visible illustrated subjects are visibly changing position or shape independently. Keep the physical room and the projection's overall footprint fixed.
SLEIGH AND REINDEER: the existing sleigh team travels along the plaster ceiling at roughly one fifth of the visible ceiling width per second, crossing architectural seams and passing the fixed central star. Every reindeer continuously cycles its legs in a running gallop; heads bob, harnesses flex and the sleigh rocks behind them. CHIMNEYS: each visible illustrated house chimney continuously emits a clearly visible cream-grey animated smoke plume, contained INSIDE the flat wall illustration. VILLAGE: the existing illustrated figures walk along the wall, take full alternating steps and swing arms. Gift carriers lift and pass the existing parcels. Existing animal drawings walk with articulating legs, toy processions advance and wheels turn where present. Existing house-window light flickers independently. RIBBONS, GARLANDS AND BELLS: successive waves visibly deform each existing ribbon along its length while bright gold crests travel from the central star toward the walls, covering half a ribbon length per second. Existing bell drawings swing left-right-left roughly once per second with independently swinging clappers. Existing ornament drawings rotate within the projected picture. Do not leave the wall decorations frozen while only the ceiling sleigh moves.
SNOW AND STARS: existing snowflake drawings translate along the ceiling planes and down the walls continuously, at different speeds. Ceiling snow stays flush to ceiling plaster and follows its slope, never drops into the air. Stars twinkle independently while existing shooting-star streaks traverse the surface. All these actions run simultaneously from the first visible projected frame until the final frame, at normal playback speed, without a fade-in, opening pause, final freeze or settling back into the reference image. The supplied visual references fix architecture, identities and artwork appearance ONLY; replace their static or weak artwork motion with the explicit motion above. The original full projection is already on at frame zero or behind the closed door. All animated pixels bend at actual wall and ceiling seams, remain flat on those surfaces and are occluded by real foreground objects.

ONE PROJECTOR, ONE PICTURE: whatever the wall is doing, the ceiling is doing at the same instant and the same speed. The picture's outer boundary is anchored - it never rotates, spins or slides across the room as one sheet; only the things inside it travel. It is flat light lying on the actual room surfaces. The broad flat central ceiling and all four smooth coved transitions remain visible. The sleigh trail and garlands run across the flat panel then curve and progressively stretch around the rounded coves before continuing vertically down the walls; no invented ridge or angular fold interrupts the coves. At the chimney breast the picture breaks sharply around the two projecting vertical corners, carrying across every brick face with crisp mortar-line texture and tiny mortar shadows. The arched doorway and window reveals interrupt the light at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. Nothing ever leaves a surface, and nothing is projected on the floor, rug, sofa, table, tree or gifts.

THE CEILING IS FULL. The ceiling carries as much moving picture as the walls do, everywhere it appears in frame and above all in the closing seconds: the great star, the travelling gold light waves, the rippling red-and-gold ribbons, the flying sleigh, pouring snow and twinkling stars run across the whole coved ceiling and over every ceiling seam, right into all four corners. No bare un-animated patch of plaster and no bare ceiling detail anywhere in the closing framing.

BEATS
0.0-0.6s - The gentle upward tilt and gentle forward drift have ALREADY STARTED on the first frame and continue at constant speed while the hand turns the knob and pushes the door away from camera in one quick decisive shove. The room behind it is already running AND BOTH CHILDREN ARE ALREADY IN MOTION - the widening gap only uncovers more of a movie that was already playing and two kids who were already running before the door opened. Nothing ignites or spreads as the door opens, and the door edge and frame stay plain painted wood - no glowing strip, no coloured fringe, no bright seam in the gap.
0.6s to the end - CONTINUE THE SAME SIMULTANEOUS FORWARD-AND-UPWARD MOVE ALREADY IN PROGRESS. Clearing the door is not a camera cue. The view must not travel straight ahead first and only later rise to the ceiling. The camera crosses the single thin doorway threshold directly into the living room, already beside its sectional and cream rug without passing through any intervening space, while its aim keeps rising at the same small constant angular rate that began at 0.0s; room features slide downward through the frame continuously as perspective gently advances. No hold on the children, no stop at the sofa, no separate ceiling reveal. Do not speed up the tilt in the last two seconds to finish a composition. The shot simply ends during the same ongoing gentle movement, with both back wall and ceiling still visible. All through it the smoke pours from every chimney, the ribbons ripples, the sleigh flies on across the ceiling, the deer procession and the elves keep moving, the travelling gold light waves keep spreading and the snow keeps falling.
Inside that single move, the children are playing ONE CONTINUOUS GAME OF CHASE on the open floor. They are already mid-stride before the door reveals them. The girl with East Asian features, light warm skin and long straight dark hair  runs a broad curving path across the rug and alongside the sofa; the boy with East Asian features, light warm skin and straight dark hair in a neat side part follows two steps behind, both laughing, taking quick alternating footfalls with swinging arms. They continue their running loop naturally around the available floor space, curving away from furniture and each other. Their positions change in every successive instant, including the middle of the shot. They do not arrive at a destination, stop beside each other, face the camera, line up, switch activities or climb onto the sofa. This is already-running, still-running, keep-running: the same continuous playful action before the door opens, through the reveal and through the last frame in which they are visible. They may glance up while their feet keep stepping, but their momentum never stops. Real speed, grounded feet and natural weight; no sliding, teleporting or running in place.

CAMERA - eye height, normal wide-angle phone lens, subtle natural handheld sway. One blended forward-and-upward move, with constant gentle upward angular speed across all five seconds. No delayed tilt, no pitch jump, no sudden reframe, no acceleration or speed ramp, no stop, no second move, no cut, no zoom, no orbit, no fisheye, no lens warping. EXACTLY TWO CHILDREN, no adults, no third child, no pets. Hold the sharpness and exposure of the start image - the panel edges of the door, the brass knob, the forearm and sleeve exactly as shown in the starting image, with no jewellery. Crisp phone footage, in focus first frame to last.

AUDIO - dry documentary sound only: the handle, the door swinging, continuous alternating running footfalls, children laughing, quiet room tone. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS - real-time motion at normal speed. One continuous take. One single smooth camera move with forward translation and upward tilt happening simultaneously from the first frame, at unchanged gentle speed throughout. The projected picture is visibly in motion in every single frame, at the start, in the middle and in the last second. The whole coved ceiling is covered in moving picture at the end. BOTH CHILDREN ARE MOVING IN EVERY FRAME THEY APPEAR IN, from the first frame the door uncovers them to the last frame of the clip: both children keep running their playful curving loop; the camera may tilt them out of view but never catches them settled into a pose. Their movement is natural, unchoreographed, real-speed kid movement. Sharp focus to the final frame.

BANNED - a still or frozen picture; a projection that appears to move only because the camera moves; light that moves for a moment then stops; chimneys without smoke; an ribbons that sits still; a parked sleigh; a deer procession that does not travel or elves that do not move; travelling gold light waves that do not spread outward; flakes that twinkle but never travel; a still ceiling above a moving wall; an empty or un-animated area of ceiling or an un-animated patch of the vault in any frame; the whole picture rotating or sliding as one sheet; a pattern that looks printed, painted or like wallpaper; a glow or bright seam along the door edge or gap; light that grows or fills the room as the door opens; particles falling through the open air of the room; volumetric snow; snow in front of the children, the sofa, the stair or the real tree; a camera that moves, stops and then moves again; two separate camera moves; a forward-only push followed by a late upward tilt; holding a level angle until entering the room; a sudden ceiling swing; accelerating the tilt near the end; copying @Video 1's camera timing; either child climbing or jumping onto the sofa; either child standing still, waiting, hesitating, posed or rooted to one spot at any point; a child who only turns her head while her feet stay planted; a child who begins the clip motionless and starts moving later; a child who stops moving before the last frame; the projector unit visible; slow motion; blur; any music; a cut; an adult; subtitles; on-screen text.

CONTINUOUS MOTION CHECK - from the first visible frame through the very last frame, the wall AND ceiling each contain clearly travelling projected elements at the same time: the sleigh changes position across the ceiling, its reindeer gallop; the deer procession advances along the wall; elves move and pass gifts; bells swing; ribbons carry travelling light waves; snowflakes translate across the surfaces. Twinkle alone and camera movement alone do not count. Maintain that same lively real-time motion with no opening freeze, no settling into a still image and no final freeze. All light bends with the real wall and ceiling geometry and stays on those surfaces.

REFERENCE-ONLY LOCK - @Video 1 provides room, identity and projection appearance only. No static room image is attached. Preserve the closed-door starting frame and the established single walking-and-tilting camera move. The children are continuously running a playful chase; their actions are independent of all poses and activity changes in the reference video. Moving drawings follow the surface perspective and bend or clip at actual corners and ceiling details. They have no thickness, volume, free-space parallax or physical cast shadow. The real fireplace opening and mantel remain real stationary architecture. No character, sleigh, ribbon, spark, snowflake, smoke curl or ornament floats between the camera and a wall, emerges from the fireplace, hovers above the mantel, or enters the usable room. Apparent depth belongs only to the drawn illustration on the wall.

ROOM AND IDENTITY - a spacious double-height Arts-and-Crafts Christmas great room with a high COVED CEILING: a broad perfectly flat rectangular central ceiling panel, connected to all four vertical walls by deep smoothly curved plaster coves, with no ridge, no beam, no barrel tunnel and no coffer grid. A floor-to-ceiling brick chimney breast in small red-brown bricks stands on the back wall with a dark cherry mantel; a wide three-part rectangular window occupies the left wall and a rounded archway opens laterally on the living room's right side wall, outside the entrance route; the starting walnut door itself opens directly into this room through one normal wall-thickness threshold. PROJECTED SCENE CONTENT - LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a magical WOODLAND CHRISTMAS GIFT NIGHT: a snowy forest of enormous decorated fir trees, every branch hung with crimson baubles, gold candle lights and tiny ribboned gifts; nestled between the trees, warmly lit log cottages decorated with holly wreaths and red bows; friendly illustrated deer with gold bells and rabbits beside little stacks of wrapped Christmas presents. A red sleigh filled with colourful ribboned parcels waits outside Santa's warm log-cabin gift depot, with red-coated elves carrying teddy bears and wooden rocking horses toward it. Two monumental gold Christmas lanterns flank a towering fully decorated tree; every ornament has a crisp rim and every gift ribbon a visible knot. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa and eight reindeer sweep past a gold Christmas star, with curling red-and-gold ribbon trails interwoven with holly leaves, candy canes, delicate cream snowflakes and tiny star lights. This is unmistakably Christmas Eve, red and gold dominant with deep fir-green accents, warm windows and a dark midnight background. det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, framing, scale and poses. Wholesome family Christmas scene. @Image 1 owns composition geometry only. @Image 2 owns the dense saturated photographic projection look; change the architecture and children to the descriptions below. Both reference images are generated stills, not photographs of a documented real house.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same framing that shows the wall behind the bed and the ceiling above it both in shot, and the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself.

CHANGE 1 - THE CHILD. A different child from @Image 1: a boy of about five with East Asian features, light warm skin and straight dark hair in a neat side part, fully dressed for winter in a warm red and ivory knitted Christmas jumper with gold bells and green fir-tree patterns, navy knitted lounge trousers and cream wool socks. He is standing up on top of the bed, knees bent and both arms raised out to his sides, caught mid-bounce, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling, laughing. Clearly standing on top of the bed, not sitting on its edge.

CHANGE 2 - THE ROOM. Build a structurally believable room: a snug bedroom under a steep PITCHED CEILING with two smooth plaster slopes meeting at a straight central ridge, crossed by three slender white-painted horizontal tie beams with crisp square edges; the back wall is a simple triangular gable with two small side windows. A warm cherry wooden bed with a tall arched headboard is centred on that wall, red-and-cream checked bedding, cherry bedside chests, medium-brown timber floorboards and a cream wool rug. The bed stays in the same place in the frame, leaving the room's ceiling geometry clearly visible.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. The bed has a cream wool duvet with red tartan throw, pillows and a knitted stocking. A small real Christmas tree with gold lights and red ornaments stands by the window.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every roof plane and seam, wall above the headboard, window jambs and lintels. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a magical WOODLAND CHRISTMAS GIFT NIGHT: a snowy forest of enormous decorated fir trees, every branch hung with crimson baubles, gold candle lights and tiny ribboned gifts; nestled between the trees, warmly lit log cottages decorated with holly wreaths and red bows; friendly illustrated deer with gold bells and rabbits beside little stacks of wrapped Christmas presents. A red sleigh filled with colourful ribboned parcels waits outside Santa's warm log-cabin gift depot, with red-coated elves carrying teddy bears and wooden rocking horses toward it. Two monumental gold Christmas lanterns flank a towering fully decorated tree; every ornament has a crisp rim and every gift ribbon a visible knot. Along the upper walls, paired gold bells, holly clusters and richly woven evergreen swags. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa and eight reindeer sweep past a gold Christmas star, with curling red-and-gold ribbon trails interwoven with holly leaves, candy canes, delicate cream snowflakes and tiny star lights. This is unmistakably Christmas Eve, red and gold dominant with deep fir-green accents, warm windows and a dark midnight background. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The two roof slopes, straight central ridge and three white-painted tie beams remain clearly legible. The sleigh and garlands fold at the ridge and stretch down both roof planes. Each tie beam catches its own slice of the projected picture on the face toward the source, with a clear offset to the plaster beyond and a narrow hard shadow behind it. At the triangular gable and window casings the picture breaks again along the actual wall-to-ceiling and trim edges. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The timber floorboards, the large flat-weave rug, the bed and its covers, the bench at its foot and the little Christmas tree carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. The boy's face and his knitted jumper catch that spill so his face reads clearly.

CHANGE 5 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no stool, no side table, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain wall and floor.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the knit stitches of the jumpers, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the plaster, the crisp architectural edges of the ceiling and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, a child at home with his family at Christmas.

GLOBAL STYLE: crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed. Sharp and in focus from the first frame to the last, at least as sharp as the start image. No blur, no haze, no soft focus, no washed-out exposure, no colour shift.

ASSET ROLES: @Image 1 is frame 0.0s and controls a snug bedroom under a steep PITCHED CEILING with two smooth plaster slopes meeting at a straight central ridge, crossed by three slender white-painted horizontal tie beams with crisp square edges; the back wall is a simple triangular gable with two small side windows. Preserve the exact furniture placement, child identities, clothing, room colours and framing in that supplied image.

SUBJECTS:
THE BOY - exactly one child, a boy of about five with East Asian features, light warm skin and straight dark hair in a neat side part, wearing warm red and ivory knitted Christmas jumpers with gold bells and green fir-tree patterns, navy knitted lounge trousers and cream wool socks, standing on the bed with his arms thrown wide. No second child, no adult, no pet.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running on the bedroom floor, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the cream plaster wall and the whole pitched ceiling with tie beams. Everything glowing on the plaster is that one cone landing.
THE PICTURE - the animated scene is the exact Christmas panorama visible in the start image. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a magical WOODLAND CHRISTMAS GIFT NIGHT: a snowy forest of enormous decorated fir trees, every branch hung with crimson baubles, gold candle lights and tiny ribboned gifts; nestled between the trees, warmly lit log cottages decorated with holly wreaths and red bows; friendly illustrated deer with gold bells and rabbits beside little stacks of wrapped Christmas presents. A red sleigh filled with colourful ribboned parcels waits outside Santa's warm log-cabin gift depot, with red-coated elves carrying teddy bears and wooden rocking horses toward it. Two monumental gold Christmas lanterns flank a towering fully decorated tree; every ornament has a crisp rim and every gift ribbon a visible knot. Along the upper walls, paired gold bells, holly clusters and richly woven evergreen swags. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa and eight reindeer sweep past a gold Christmas star, with curling red-and-gold ribbon trails interwoven with holly leaves, candy canes, delicate cream snowflakes and tiny star lights. This is unmistakably Christmas Eve, red and gold dominant with deep fir-green accents, warm windows and a dark midnight background. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room.

HOW THE PICTURE BEHAVES - THIS IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE CLIP. In every previous attempt the picture sat dead still like printed wallpaper and the clip was worthless. THE PICTURE IS A FILM PLAYING ON A CINEMA SCREEN: the screen is the plaster and holds perfectly still, while everything inside the picture is in constant motion for all five seconds. The supplied starting frame already has the complete projection at full brightness. Continue motion inside that existing picture immediately; no fade-in or gradual appearance. Matching @Image 1 applies to the bedroom, the bed, THE BOY and the colours, not to where any element of the picture sits.
THE PICTURE AS A WHOLE IS ANCHORED. It does not rotate, spin, swing, sweep sideways or slide across the room as one sheet. Its outer boundary stays where it is. The motion lives INSIDE it, element by element:
- THE CHIMNEY SMOKE DRAWINGS - animated flat smoke curls rise within the projected cottage drawings on the wall, leaning right and changing shape while new drawn curls form below. These are pixels on plaster, not real smoke or haze in the room.
- THE RISING SPARK DRAWINGS - flat gold pixels climb along the wall from the illustrated village chimneys toward the painted star field at roughly one roof height each half-second. They are part of the projected wall movie, with no real sparks, airborne trails or particles between the camera and the wall.
- THE RIBBONS - each crimson, ruby, gold and emerald ribbon radiates outward from the great star and ripples ALONG ITS OWN LENGTH, a slow travelling wave running down the band away from the star, about half of the ribbon's length every second, the ribbon swelling brighter and thinner as the wave passes and its lower fringe combing and re-forming. Each ribbon's overall fan stays where it is on the plaster; the wave inside it travels. Every ribbon on the ceiling is doing this at the same time.
- THE SLEIGH AND THE REINDEER - they are FLYING. The team travels steadily across the ceiling on a long sweeping curve away from where it sits in the start image, arcing in toward the great star, covering about a quarter of the ceiling's width every second, so by 5.0s it has crossed most of the way. The reindeer's legs gallop, their heads nod, the sleigh rocks gently behind them, the long tapering trail streams out behind, and the whole team rises and dips a little as it goes.
- THE WOODLAND DEER AND THE ELVES. The illustrated deer travel steadily among the projected fir trees along the lower wall, legs walking and heads nodding, moving about two body lengths every second. Existing rabbits make small grounded hops within the wall drawing; elves bend, lift existing wrapped gifts and pass them toward the red sleigh at the log-cabin depot. All keep moving from the first frame to the last.
- THE GOLD LIGHT WAVES. Successive bright gold waves TRAVEL OUTWARD along the existing red-and-gold ribbon and evergreen-garland paths on the ceiling, each bright crest travelling about half of its ribbon's length every second, fading behind as the next bright crest follows, so the existing ribbons sparkle and flow continuously. No new rings or new objects appear; the moving light stays within the shapes that already exist in the image.

Flat bauble and candy-cane drawings translate and turn along the wall and ceiling planes; they have no depth in the real room. Big gold bell drawings swing visibly side to side within the same projected surface, their clapper drawings moving inside them. All obey surface perspective and architectural occlusion.

On the ceiling they glide tangentially ALONG each roof plane toward the ridge or wall seam, following its perspective; they never fall away from the ceiling into the room. On the walls they translate downward along the wall at about one quarter wall-height per second. At a wall-ceiling corner their path bends onto the adjoining surface and remains flush with it; behind the real boy, bed, headboard and beams they are occluded and disappear, never drawn over those objects. THE BOY lands on both feet and drives straight into a second, higher jump, knees tucking, then a third; he never stops moving and the body motion carries straight across the seam between the two camera moves.

det.label: Image prompt · v14_c07_g1.png
det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, framing, scale and poses. Wholesome family Christmas scene. @Image 1 owns composition geometry only. @Image 2 owns the dense saturated photographic projection look and the identity of the new room and children; it is the same house viewed from farther inside. Both reference images are generated stills, not photographs of a documented real house.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing that shows a whole enormous double-height room with its full ceiling in shot, the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two poses - a girl JUMPING ON THE SOFA, caught mid-air above the cushions, knees bent, arms flung up, hair lifted, the cushion compressed under where she pushed off; and a boy standing on the rug in front of the sofa, seen from behind and slightly to the side, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling with his arms out in wonder. Both are small in frame, in scale with the huge room - keeping them small preserves the sense of how big the space is.

CHANGE 1 - THE CHILDREN. The same new children as @Image 2: a girl of about eight with East Asian features, light warm skin and long straight dark hair with a red velvet hairband; a boy of about five with East Asian features, light warm skin and straight dark hair in a neat side part. Both fully dressed in warm red and ivory knitted Christmas jumpers with gold bells and green fir-tree patterns, navy knitted lounge trousers and cream wool socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene.

CHANGE 2 - THE ROOM. Build a structurally believable room: a spacious double-height Arts-and-Crafts Christmas great room with a high COVED CEILING: a broad perfectly flat rectangular central ceiling panel, connected to all four vertical walls by deep smoothly curved plaster coves, with no ridge, no beam, no barrel tunnel and no coffer grid. A floor-to-ceiling brick chimney breast in small red-brown bricks stands on the back wall with a dark cherry mantel; a wide three-part rectangular window occupies the left wall and a rounded archway opens on the right. Medium-brown cherry floorboards, a large oatmeal linen sectional sofa, a rectangular upholstered ottoman and a cream wool rug. The same room and decor as @Image 2, seen from the middle of the great room with the whole ceiling in shot.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. A real Christmas tree with warm gold lights, red baubles, gold ribbon and wrapped gifts stands beside the fireplace. Evergreen garland with holly berries covers the mantel, with three red-and-cream knitted stockings below. The projection is the main illumination.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every architectural plane and seam, every beam or cove, and the entire chimney breast all the way to the ceiling. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a magical WOODLAND CHRISTMAS GIFT NIGHT: a snowy forest of enormous decorated fir trees, every branch hung with crimson baubles, gold candle lights and tiny ribboned gifts; nestled between the trees, warmly lit log cottages decorated with holly wreaths and red bows; friendly illustrated deer with gold bells and rabbits beside little stacks of wrapped Christmas presents. A red sleigh filled with colourful ribboned parcels waits outside Santa's warm log-cabin gift depot, with red-coated elves carrying teddy bears and wooden rocking horses toward it. Two monumental gold Christmas lanterns flank a towering fully decorated tree; every ornament has a crisp rim and every gift ribbon a visible knot. Along the upper walls, paired gold bells, holly clusters and richly woven evergreen swags. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa and eight reindeer sweep past a gold Christmas star, with curling red-and-gold ribbon trails interwoven with holly leaves, candy canes, delicate cream snowflakes and tiny star lights. This is unmistakably Christmas Eve, red and gold dominant with deep fir-green accents, warm windows and a dark midnight background. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The broad flat central ceiling and all four smooth coved transitions remain visible. The sleigh trail and garlands run across the flat panel then curve and progressively stretch around the rounded coves before continuing vertically down the walls; no invented ridge or angular fold interrupts the coves. At the chimney breast the picture breaks sharply around the two projecting vertical corners, carrying across every brick face with crisp mortar-line texture and tiny mortar shadows. The arched doorway and window reveals interrupt the light at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The timber floorboards, the cream wool rug, the oatmeal linen sectional sofa, the long upholstered ottoman and the tree carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children catch that spill so their knitted jumpers read clearly.

CHANGE 5 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no round side table, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain rug and floor.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the knit stitches of the jumpers, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the drywall, the surface texture of the red-brown brick and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

BEATS
0.0-0.6s - The gentle upward tilt and gentle forward drift have ALREADY STARTED on the first frame and continue at constant speed while the hand turns the knob and pushes the door away from camera in one quick decisive shove. The room behind it is already running AND BOTH CHILDREN ARE ALREADY IN MOTION - the widening gap only uncovers more of a movie that was already playing and two kids who were already running before the door opened. Nothing ignites or spreads as the door opens, and the door edge and frame stay plain painted wood - no glowing strip, no coloured fringe, no bright seam in the gap.
0.6s to the end - CONTINUE THE SAME SIMULTANEOUS FORWARD-AND-UPWARD MOVE ALREADY IN PROGRESS. Clearing the door is not a camera cue. The view must not travel straight ahead first and only later rise to the ceiling. The camera crosses the single thin doorway threshold directly into the living room, already beside its sectional and rug shown in the reference without passing through any intervening space, while its aim keeps rising at the same small constant angular rate that began at 0.0s; room features slide downward through the frame continuously as perspective gently advances. No hold on the children, no stop at the sofa, no separate ceiling reveal. Do not speed up the tilt in the last two seconds to finish a composition. The shot simply ends during the same ongoing gentle movement, with both back wall and ceiling still visible. All through it the smoke pours from every chimney, the ribbons ripples, the sleigh flies on across the ceiling, the existing illustrated villagers and toy/train procession and the elves keep moving, the travelling gold light waves keep spreading and the snow keeps falling.
Inside that single move, the children are playing ONE CONTINUOUS GAME OF CHASE on the open floor. They are already mid-stride before the door reveals them. The girl with East Asian features, light warm skin and long straight dark hair  runs a broad curving path across the rug and alongside the sofa; the boy with fair freckled skin and short tousled copper-red hair follows two steps behind, both laughing, taking quick alternating footfalls with swinging arms. They continue their running loop naturally around the available floor space, curving away from furniture and each other. Their positions change in every successive instant, including the middle of the shot. They do not arrive at a destination, stop beside each other, face the camera, line up, switch activities or climb onto the sofa. This is already-running, still-running, keep-running: the same continuous playful action before the door opens, through the reveal and through the last frame in which they are visible. They may glance up while their feet keep stepping, but their momentum never stops. Real speed, grounded feet and natural weight; no sliding, teleporting or running in place.

CAMERA - eye height, normal wide-angle phone lens, subtle natural handheld sway. One blended forward-and-upward move, with constant gentle upward angular speed across all five seconds. No delayed tilt, no pitch jump, no sudden reframe, no acceleration or speed ramp, no stop, no second move, no cut, no zoom, no orbit, no fisheye, no lens warping. The camera is the person's eyes; no phone, screen or device in frame after 0.6s.

EXACTLY TWO CHILDREN, no adults, no third child, no pets. Hold the sharpness and exposure of the start image - the panel edges of the door, the brass knob, the forearm and sleeve exactly as shown in the starting image, with no jewellery. Crisp phone footage, in focus first frame to last.

AUDIO - dry documentary sound only: the handle, the door swinging, continuous alternating running footfalls, children laughing, quiet room tone. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS - real-time motion at normal speed. One continuous take. One single smooth camera move with forward translation and upward tilt happening simultaneously from the first frame, at unchanged gentle speed throughout. The projected picture is visibly in motion in every single frame, at the start, in the middle and in the last second. The whole coffered ceiling is covered in moving picture at the end. BOTH CHILDREN ARE MOVING IN EVERY FRAME THEY APPEAR IN, from the first frame the door uncovers them to the last frame of the clip: both children keep running their playful curving loop; the camera may tilt them out of view but never catches them settled into a pose. Their movement is natural, unchoreographed, real-speed kid movement. Sharp focus to the final frame.

BANNED - a still or frozen picture; a projection that appears to move only because the camera moves; light that moves for a moment then stops; chimneys without smoke; a ribbon that sits still; a parked sleigh; a existing illustrated villagers and toy/train procession that does not travel or elves that do not move; travelling gold light waves that do not spread outward; flakes that twinkle but never travel; a still ceiling above a moving wall; an empty or un-animated area of ceiling or an un-animated patch of the vault in any frame; the whole picture rotating or sliding as one sheet; a pattern that looks printed, painted or like wallpaper; a glow or bright seam along the door edge or gap; light that grows or fills the room as the door opens; particles falling through the open air of the room; volumetric snow; snow in front of the children, the sofa, the stair or the real tree; a camera that moves, stops and then moves again; two separate camera moves; a forward-only push followed by a late upward tilt; holding a level angle until entering the room; a sudden ceiling swing; accelerating the tilt near the end; copying @Video 1's camera timing; either child climbing or jumping onto the sofa; either child standing still, waiting, hesitating, posed or rooted to one spot at any point; a child who only turns her head while her feet stay planted; a child who begins the clip motionless and starts moving later; a child who stops moving before the last frame; the projector unit visible; slow motion; blur; any music; a cut; an adult; subtitles; on-screen text.

CONTINUOUS MOTION CHECK - from the first visible frame through the very last frame, the wall AND ceiling each contain clearly travelling projected elements at the same time: the sleigh changes position across the ceiling, its reindeer gallop; the existing illustrated villagers and toy/train procession advances along the wall; elves move and pass gifts; bells swing; ribbons carry travelling light waves; snowflakes translate across the surfaces. Twinkle alone and camera movement alone do not count. Maintain that same lively real-time motion with no opening freeze, no settling into a still image and no final freeze. All light bends with the real wall and ceiling geometry and stays on those surfaces.

REFERENCE-ONLY LOCK - @Video 1 provides room, identity and projection appearance only. No static room image is attached. Preserve the closed-door starting frame and the established single walking-and-tilting camera move. The children are continuously running a playful chase; their actions are independent of all poses and activity changes in the reference video. Never copy the reference video's opening composition, sofa bouncing, camera movement, cuts or timing. The new clip is exactly 5 seconds and has no end frame.

SURFACE-ONLY LOCK - every animated Christmas shape, including every shape above the real fireplace, is flat projected light attached to the existing plaster, chimney surface and ceiling. Moving drawings follow the surface perspective and bend or clip at actual corners and ceiling details. They have no thickness, volume, free-space parallax or physical cast shadow. The real fireplace opening and mantel remain real stationary architecture. No character, sleigh, ribbon, spark, snowflake, smoke curl or ornament floats between the camera and a wall, emerges from the fireplace, hovers above the mantel, or enters the usable room. Apparent depth belongs only to the drawn illustration on the wall.

ROOM AND IDENTITY - a spacious double-height French-country Christmas great room with a high COFFERED CEILING: a flat rectangular ceiling divided into six large deep square recesses by broad straight plaster beams. A tall pale limestone chimney breast stands on the back wall with a carved oak mantel; two tall arched windows occupy the left wall and a rectangular oak-trimmed opening sits on the right. Honey-oak floorboards, a large cream linen sectional sofa, a rectangular cream upholstered ottoman and a burgundy wool rug. The side opening on the right wall remains lateral to the route, never an extra threshold ahead. a girl of about eight with fair freckled skin and wavy auburn hair in two low braids; a boy of about six with fair freckled skin and short tousled copper-red hair. Both fully dressed in burgundy-and-cream brushed-cotton Christmas pyjama sets patterned with small gold nutcrackers and fir trees, with matching loose pyjama trousers and cream wool socks. Preserve these identities and architecture from @Video 1.

PROJECTED SCENE CONTENT - LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a magical NUTCRACKER CHRISTMAS TOY TOWN: snow-covered European toy shops with ruby-red doors, glowing golden windows, holly wreaths and tiny ribboned gifts; tall friendly red-and-gold wooden nutcrackers flank a grand illuminated Christmas tree, and cheerful elves carry drums, teddy bears and rocking horses between open workshops. A tiny red toy train carries stacks of wrapped gifts through the snowy village. Along the upper walls, sumptuous red velvet ribbon swags, gold bells and emerald fir garlands join the village into one uninterrupted festive panorama. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red-and-gold sleigh and eight reindeer cross a large fine-pointed gold Christmas star, with sweeping scarlet ribbons, delicate snowflakes, small hanging baubles and countless crisp golden star points. This is unmistakably Christmas Eve, rich ruby red and antique gold dominant with deep emerald accents and a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. 

CURRENT BRIEF — STRONG CONTINUOUS MOTION: The existing toy train rolls steadily through the projected village with its wheels turning; toy-shop elves walk and pass gifts; nutcrackers move their arms and nod. Preserve the artwork already visible. Every illustrated chimney emits fresh curling smoke continuously, moving at least one chimney height per second; the sleigh crosses a substantial part of the ceiling with galloping reindeer. Existing ribbon light fields carry clearly travelling aurora-like waves along their length, with brightness crests moving rather than blinking in place. Do not add a new aurora object where none exists; animate the existing sky and ribbon shapes. The house structures and central star stay anchored while characters, vehicles, smoke and light waves travel independently. The only physical motion in the room is the specified children and camera; all Christmas artwork and illustrated smoke remain flat light on real wall/ceiling surfaces. No floating 3D objects. No frozen opening or ending. Use the exact architecture and artwork in this shot's references; animate only illustrated characters actually present, never invent source-template deer or rabbits. Natural room audio only, no music.
