det.text: START FRAME — v17_c05_g1.png

det.label: Image prompt · v17_c05_g1.png
det.text:
Recreate @Image 1 with two changes.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo, the same dim hallway, the same antique brass round doorknob in the same place, the same small pine wreath with the red velvet bow hung on the door, the same oak floorboards, the same woman's forearm entering from the lower right with the cranberry-red fine-knit wool sleeve and no jewellery, with warm medium-tan skin, slender adult woman's fingers and short natural nails, her hand closed around the knob, the same camera position and camera height, the same warm low-key evening light.

CHANGE 1 - THE DOOR. It is now a deep navy-blue painted six-panel solid wood door with two small square upper panels and four tall rectangular panels, a satin finish and crisp white-painted surrounding trim, an antique brass round knob and matching brass escutcheon, set in a cream painted frame. Same size, same position in frame, same flat-on angle as @Image 1.

CHANGE 2 - the door is FULLY CLOSED and flush in its frame. There is NO gap at the edge of the door and absolutely NO light spilling out - no rainbow strip, no coloured glow, no bright line, no glare anywhere along the door edge, the jamb, the threshold or the floor. The seam between door and frame is a plain dark shadow line only. Nothing behind the door is visible or lit.

THE WREATH - it hangs on the FACE of the door, centred on the upper half of the door and comfortably inside the frame with clear painted door visible all the way around it. It must NOT be cut off by the right edge of the picture and must NOT drift onto the door frame or the wall. The whole circle of the wreath and the whole red velvet bow are visible.

EXPOSURE - brighter and warmer than @Image 1, which came out too dark. The hallway is dim but comfortably readable: the navy-blue paint reads clearly as deep blue, the brass knob catches a warm highlight, the oak floorboards and the forearm are clearly lit, and the shadows stay deep but still hold detail. Do not crush the blacks and do not let any part of the frame go to a flat dark mass.

SHARPNESS - this frame must be tack sharp edge to edge: every moulding edge and panel corner in the door, the machined edge and the patina of the brass knob, the individual needles of the pine wreath and the woven nap of the red velvet bow, the skin texture and fine hairs on the forearm, the grain of the floorboards. Extremely high quality, perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic. BANNED: blur, soft focus, haze, mushy low-detail surfaces, waxy skin, a dreamy or filtered look, motion blur, noise, upscaling artefacts.

Natural handheld UGC look, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, photorealistic, zero motion blur, no CGI look.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

REFERENCE ROLES: @Image 1 owns the exact layout, product geometry, hand positions and camera. @Image 2 owns the established photographic look and product fidelity only; use the new hands, materials and background specified above. All parts of this photograph, including the background, are in crisp natural iPhone deep focus, no portrait mode, no bokeh, no blur.
FRAME 2 — ROOM REFERENCE — v17_c05_r1.png

det.label: Image prompt · v17_c05_r1.png
det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, framing, scale and poses. Wholesome family Christmas scene. @Image 1 owns composition geometry only. @Image 2 owns the dense saturated photographic projection look; change the architecture and children to the descriptions below. Both reference images are generated stills, not photographs of a documented real house.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing of a whole tall room seen from a doorway, the same magical low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two children - a boy standing TURNED AROUND FACING THE CAMERA, front-on, his face fully visible and lit by the coloured light, looking towards the lens with a delighted open-mouthed smile, arms slightly out in wonder, and a girl beside him seen from behind, still looking up at the projected wall.

The boy is of about six with warm medium-tan skin and straight dark-brown hair in a short side-swept cut; the girl is of about eight with warm medium-tan skin and long dark-brown hair in a high ponytail tied with a red bow. Both children are fully dressed for winter in ivory brushed-cotton Christmas pyjama sets patterned with small red Christmas trains, green holly leaves and gold stars, with matching loose pyjama trousers and cranberry wool socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene.

CHANGE 1 - THE ROOM. Build a structurally believable room: a spacious double-height coastal Georgian Christmas great room with a high TRAY CEILING: a broad flat rectangular raised centre, four gently sloping border planes and a wide flat perimeter ledge with crisp stepped moulding. A tall white-painted fluted chimney breast stands on the back wall with a white marble mantel; three tall sash windows occupy the left wall and a wide rectangular white-trimmed opening sits on the right. Pale ash floorboards, a large dove-grey linen sectional sofa, a rectangular dove-grey upholstered ottoman and a soft blue wool rug. Seen from the doorway; the new a deep navy-blue painted six-panel solid wood door with two small square upper panels and four tall rectangular panels, a satin finish and crisp white-painted surrounding trim is open out of frame.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. A real Christmas tree with warm gold lights, red baubles, gold ribbon and wrapped gifts stands beside the fireplace. Evergreen garland with holly berries covers the mantel, with three red-and-cream knitted stockings below. The projection is the main illumination.

CHANGE 2 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every architectural plane and seam, every beam or cove, and the entire chimney breast all the way to the ceiling. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a magical NORTH POLE CHRISTMAS EXPRESS: a magnificent red-and-gold Christmas steam train with brass wheels and carriages full of ribboned gifts travels through a snowy North Pole station, surrounded by glowing red-roofed toy workshops, holly wreaths, golden lanterns and tall decorated fir trees. Friendly elves wave beside stacks of presents while Santa greets them on a warmly lit station platform. Along the upper walls, linked gold bells, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands connect the station roofs into a continuous Christmas panorama. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer sweep around a brilliant fine-pointed golden Christmas star, their long curling red-and-gold ribbon trail woven among crisp snowflakes and tiny golden lights. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold and cranberry red dominant with evergreen accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The raised flat tray centre, four sloping borders, stepped mouldings and flat lower perimeter remain clearly three-dimensional. The sleigh and garlands fold at each change of plane and stretch down the sloped borders before continuing onto the walls. The tall fluted chimney receives a continuous picture with tiny shadow breaks in its grooves and clear folds at its two projecting corners. Sash window reveals and doorway trim interrupt the light at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 3 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The timber floorboards, the soft blue wool rug, the dove-grey linen sectional sofa, the long upholstered ottoman, the tree and the gifts carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children's faces and their cotton pyjamas catch that spill so both faces read clearly.

CHANGE 4 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no side table, no stool, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain floor and the edge of the rug.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the fine cotton weave of the pyjamas, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the drywall, the surface texture of the white-painted fluted plaster and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.
CLIP IN THE CUT — v17_c05_g4.mp4

det.label: Clip prompt · v17_c05_g4.mp4
det.text:
CAMERA CONTINUITY - PRIMARY CORRECTION: the entire five seconds are ONE slow, uninterrupted forward-and-upward glide. Forward travel and upward aim are mechanically coupled as one motion, already underway together in frame zero. Keep the same gentle pace and the same forward-to-upward ratio for every frame, including while the door opens and while crossing its sill. Travel only about 0.8 metres forward over the entire shot, with an even upward tilt of about 18 degrees over those same five seconds. The wreath, door-panel edges and later the back-wall details drift smoothly downward in the frame from the beginning while perspective advances very gently. There is no forward-only phase and no later tilt-only phase. Never complete an entrance and then begin looking up. Do not accelerate the beginning, hurry through the door, ease in, ease out, steepen the tilt, speed-ramp or catch up to an end composition. The final frame can remain near the threshold with the back wall, furniture and ceiling visible; covering more distance or revealing the whole ceiling is not a goal. The door opens naturally during the same slow glide; its opening is not a camera cue. Preserve the same doorframe and room features across adjacent frames as the camera physically crosses the single sill. No cut, concealed edit, dissolve, match cut, scene replacement, teleport, jump or sudden perspective change. Maintain this single gentle motion unchanged until the clip ends.

CHILD MOVEMENT - PRIMARY CORRECTION: the two children are already playing chase behind the closed door, and their chase has no ending inside this clip. Their poses and floor positions in @Image 2 must NEVER be reproduced, approached as a target, or used as an end frame. @Image 2 gives their appearance only. Keep them separated by about two running strides along the route, at different depths and with side or three-quarter-back views. One leads and the other follows; they never stand side by side facing the lens. Their bodies continuously travel across the floor with alternating footfalls and swinging arms, from first visibility through the actual last frame. They do not slow down, converge, align, regroup, stop, look at the camera, pose or return to the reference positions. The last 1.5 seconds contain as much continuing running action as the middle: the girl rounds the rug's right-hand edge, the boy is still two strides behind crossing the rug, and both are mid-stride when the recording ends. The action continues beyond the cut-off time. This child-action correction must not alter the camera movement specified above.

DIRECT ROOM ENTRY - PRIMARY GEOMETRY CORRECTION: the closed door in @Image 1 is fitted directly into the living room's entrance wall. Its far face opens immediately into the furnished Christmas living room in @Image 2. There is ONE door and ONE thin normal wall-thickness threshold, about 15 cm deep. The very first gap reveals the living room itself, its already-moving children and active projections, close behind this door. As the camera crosses that single threshold it is already INSIDE the living room beside the near end of the sectional and rug shown in the reference. The living room floor begins at the far edge of the same sill; its side walls and high tray ceiling meet this entrance wall directly. No intervening hall, foyer, vestibule, tunnel, passage, empty approach space, second doorway or arch to walk under. Do not frame the living room at the far end of another space. The side opening visible on the reference room's RIGHT SIDE WALL is a lateral room feature only, away from the camera's route; never place it in front of the camera or between this door and the living room. Preserve the exact supplied closed-door first frame. After opening that same door, the existing continuous forward movement enters the living room directly.

PRIMARY REQUIREMENT: this is a continuously ANIMATED Christmas movie projected on real walls and ceiling. The sleigh travels, reindeer gallop and smoke actively billows from every illustrated house chimney. Most other existing illustrated subjects move too. A static decorative image behind moving children is a failed result. Apply the detailed PROJECTED FILM ACTION below at every instant; retain the existing camera and child choreography.

HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ THIS FIRST: the pictures on the walls and the tray ceiling are A MOVIE THAT IS PLAYING, not a pattern painted on the plaster. @Image 2 supplies the room design, children's identities and projection artwork appearance only. It is a visual room reference, not a timeline or camera reference. Its composition is not a target frame for this clip. Behind the closed door the projected movie is already playing, and it keeps running through the last frame. Smoke pours from every chimney, the ribbons radiates, the sleigh flies, the existing illustrated villagers and toy/train procession travels and the elves work, the travelling gold light waves spread, the snow falls - continuously, in every single frame. If the shapes on the walls and ceiling hold still, the clip has failed.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home at Christmas.

TASK: image-to-video, one continuous handheld phone POV take, vertical 9:16. Frame 0.0s is the start image: a deep navy-blue painted six-panel solid wood door with two small square upper panels and four tall rectangular panels, a satin finish and crisp white-painted surrounding trim fully closed with a wreath, a hand on the brass knob. @Image 2 is a room-content reference for the layout, tray ceiling, furniture, the children's identities and clothes, colours, and projection artwork appearance. Use only the single continuous camera move and child actions specified in this prompt; the room still supplies appearance only. Only the closed-door start image defines frame 0.0s. No end frame is supplied.

PROJECTED FILM ACTION - THE MAIN SUBJECT IS THE MOVING CHRISTMAS ARTWORK. Animate the existing illustrated objects themselves, not just the camera, children, brightness or glitter. At every moment MOST visible illustrated subjects are visibly changing position or shape independently. Keep the physical room and the projection's overall footprint fixed.
SLEIGH AND REINDEER: the existing sleigh team travels along the plaster ceiling at roughly one fifth of the visible ceiling width per second, crossing architectural seams and passing the fixed central star. Every reindeer continuously cycles its legs in a running gallop; heads bob, harnesses flex and the sleigh rocks behind them. The team must move relative to the stationary beams, star and ceiling corners in every half-second interval. Do not rotate the ceiling picture as a single disc.
CHIMNEYS: each visible illustrated house chimney continuously emits a clearly visible cream-grey animated smoke plume, contained INSIDE the flat wall illustration. New curls emerge every 0.25 second, rise one roof-height per second, expand and deform, then dissolve as more curls follow. Several different plumes must be visibly evolving at once; none may remain a frozen drawn squiggle. These are moving pixels on the wall, never real smoke entering the room.
VILLAGE: the existing illustrated figures walk along the wall, take full alternating steps and swing arms. Gift carriers lift and pass the existing parcels. Existing animal drawings walk with articulating legs, toy processions advance and wheels turn where present. Existing house-window light flickers independently. Buildings stay fixed so the moving figures and chimney smoke read clearly.
RIBBONS, GARLANDS AND BELLS: successive waves visibly deform each existing ribbon along its length while bright gold crests travel from the central star toward the walls, covering half a ribbon length per second. Existing bell drawings swing left-right-left roughly once per second with independently swinging clappers. Existing ornament drawings rotate within the projected picture. Do not leave the wall decorations frozen while only the ceiling sleigh moves.
SNOW AND STARS: existing snowflake drawings translate along the ceiling planes and down the walls continuously, at different speeds. Ceiling snow stays flush to ceiling plaster and follows its slope, never drops into the air. Stars twinkle independently while existing shooting-star streaks traverse the surface. Nothing moves over the boy or children, furniture, floor or in the open room.
All these actions run simultaneously from the first visible projected frame until the final frame, at normal playback speed, without a fade-in, opening pause, final freeze or settling back into the reference image. The supplied visual references fix architecture, identities and artwork appearance ONLY; replace their static or weak artwork motion with the explicit motion above. The original full projection is already on at frame zero or behind the closed door. All animated pixels bend at actual wall and ceiling seams, remain flat on those surfaces and are occluded by real foreground objects.

ONE PROJECTOR, ONE PICTURE: whatever the wall is doing, the ceiling is doing at the same instant and the same speed. The picture's outer boundary is anchored - it never rotates, spins or slides across the room as one sheet; only the things inside it travel. It is flat light lying on the actual room surfaces. The broad flat central ceiling and all four smooth ceiling transitions remain visible. The sleigh trail and garlands run across the flat panel then curve and progressively stretch around the rounded coves before continuing vertically down the walls; no invented ridge or angular fold interrupts the coves. At the chimney breast the picture breaks sharply around the two projecting vertical corners, carrying across every brick face with crisp mortar-line texture and tiny mortar shadows. The arched doorway and window reveals interrupt the light at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. Nothing ever leaves a surface, and nothing is projected on the floor, rug, sofa, table, tree or gifts.

THE CEILING IS FULL. The ceiling carries as much moving picture as the walls do, everywhere it appears in frame and above all in the closing seconds: the great star, the travelling gold light waves, the rippling red-and-gold ribbons, the flying sleigh, pouring snow and twinkling stars run across the whole tray ceiling and over every ceiling seam, right into all four corners. No bare un-animated patch of plaster and no bare ceiling detail anywhere in the closing framing.

CONTINUOUS ACTION, NOT CAMERA PHASES
0.0-5.0s - ONE identical slow forward-and-upward glide continues for the full duration, already underway at frame zero. The view rises gently while moving forward at the same steady ratio throughout. During approximately the first 1.5 seconds the hand turns the knob and opens the door with a smooth, ordinary unhurried push, never a quick shove or a fast reveal. The camera does not wait for the door, rush through it, pause for the room, change speed at the sill, or start a new movement afterward. The closed-door frame and the revealed room belong to the same continuous physical shot. The room behind it is already running AND BOTH CHILDREN ARE ALREADY IN MOTION - the widening gap only uncovers more of a movie that was already playing and two kids who were already running before the door opened. Nothing ignites or spreads as the door opens, and the door edge and frame stay plain painted wood - no glowing strip, no coloured fringe, no bright seam in the gap. Cross only the single thin threshold directly into the living room; no intervening space. There is no stop at the sofa or separate ceiling reveal. The shot ends during that same gentle glide, with back wall, furniture and ceiling still visible. All through it the smoke pours from every chimney, the ribbons ripples, the sleigh flies on across the ceiling, the existing illustrated villagers and toy/train procession and the elves keep moving, the travelling gold light waves keep spreading and the snow keeps falling.
Inside that single move, the children are playing ONE CONTINUOUS GAME OF CHASE on the open floor. They are already mid-stride before the door reveals them. The girl with East Asian features, light warm skin and long straight dark hair  runs a broad curving path across the rug and alongside the sofa; the boy with warm medium-tan skin and straight dark-brown hair in a short side-swept cut follows two steps behind, both laughing, taking quick alternating footfalls with swinging arms. They continue the same open-ended curving chase naturally around the available floor space, curving away from furniture and each other; this is not a loop that returns them to a reference pose. During the final 1.5 seconds the girl continues around the right-hand edge of the rug while the boy follows two running strides behind, with their bodies at different depths and turned along their route. The girl can leave the frame at the side while still running and the boy keeps following; neither child is required to remain centred or fully visible. Their positions change in every successive instant, including the middle of the shot. They do not arrive at a destination, stop beside each other, face the camera, line up, switch activities or climb onto the sofa. This is already-running, still-running, keep-running: the same continuous playful action before the door opens, through the reveal and through the last frame in which they are visible. They may glance up while their feet keep stepping, but their momentum never stops. Real speed, grounded feet and natural weight; no sliding, teleporting or running in place.

CAMERA - eye height, normal wide-angle phone lens, a steady natural phone glide. One constant slow forward-and-upward movement, both components active together from frame zero through frame last, with the same gentle speed and same ratio throughout. No opening rush, acceleration, easing, speed ramp, phase change, level hold, delayed upward tilt, pitch jump, reframe, stop, second move, cut, concealed edit, dissolve, teleport, zoom, orbit, fisheye or lens warping. The camera is the person's eyes; no phone, screen or device in frame.

EXACTLY TWO CHILDREN, no adults, no third child, no pets. Hold the sharpness and exposure of the start image - the panel edges of the door, the brass knob, the forearm and sleeve exactly as shown in the starting image, with no jewellery. Crisp phone footage, in focus first frame to last.

AUDIO - dry documentary sound only: the handle, the door swinging, continuous alternating running footfalls, children laughing, quiet room tone. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS - real-time motion at normal speed. One continuous take. One single slow camera glide with forward translation and upward tilt happening simultaneously at the same unchanging gentle ratio from the first frame through the last. No acceleration at any time and no division into entrance and ceiling-reveal phases. The projected picture is visibly in motion in every single frame, at the start, in the middle and in the last second. The whole tray ceiling is covered in moving picture at the end. BOTH CHILDREN ARE MOVING IN EVERY FRAME THEY APPEAR IN, from the first frame the door uncovers them to the actual last frame of the clip: both children keep running the same open-ended curving chase, separated along the route, mid-footfall at the cut-off with no deceleration or convergence; the camera may tilt them out of view but never catches them settled into a pose. Their movement is natural, unchoreographed, real-speed kid movement. Sharp focus to the final frame.

BANNED - a still or frozen picture; a projection that appears to move only because the camera moves; light that moves for a moment then stops; chimneys without smoke; a ribbon that sits still; a parked sleigh; a existing illustrated villagers and toy/train procession that does not travel or elves that do not move; travelling gold light waves that do not spread outward; flakes that twinkle but never travel; a still ceiling above a moving wall; an empty or un-animated area of ceiling or an un-animated patch of the vault in any frame; the whole picture rotating or sliding as one sheet; a pattern that looks printed, painted or like wallpaper; a glow or bright seam along the door edge or gap; light that grows or fills the room as the door opens; particles falling through the open air of the room; volumetric snow; snow in front of the children, the sofa, the stair or the real tree; a camera that moves, stops and then moves again; two separate camera moves; a forward-only push followed by a late upward tilt; holding a level angle until entering the room; a sudden ceiling swing; any camera acceleration or speed ramp; an opening rush; a tilt that steepens later; treating the room reference as a destination to cut or transition to; either child climbing or jumping onto the sofa; either child standing still, waiting, hesitating, posed or rooted to one spot at any point; a child who only turns her head while her feet stay planted; a child who begins the clip motionless and starts moving later; a child who stops moving before the last frame; children drifting into @Image 2's floor positions or poses; children aligning side by side in front of the sofa; decelerating into a reference tableau; completing the chase before the clip ends; the projector unit visible; slow motion; blur; any music; a cut; an adult; subtitles; on-screen text.

CONTINUOUS MOTION CHECK - from the first visible frame through the very last frame, the wall AND ceiling each contain clearly travelling projected elements at the same time: the sleigh changes position across the ceiling, its reindeer gallop; the existing illustrated villagers and toy/train procession advances along the wall; elves move and pass gifts; bells swing; ribbons carry travelling light waves; snowflakes translate across the surfaces. Twinkle alone and camera movement alone do not count. Maintain that same lively real-time motion with no opening freeze, no settling into a still image and no final freeze. All light bends with the real wall and ceiling geometry and stays on those surfaces.

REFERENCE-ONLY LOCK - @Image 2 is the existing still room reference. It supplies architecture, children's identities, clothing, furniture and artwork appearance ONLY. It is not an end frame, camera target or transition destination. Never dissolve, cut, morph or snap into its exact composition. Only the closed-door @Image 1 defines frame zero; animate the existing room content independently throughout the same uninterrupted physical entrance. The children's reference poses, orientation, spacing and floor coordinates are explicitly excluded from the reference transfer. They continuously run their playful chase at different depths, independent of those stationary poses. Never recreate the two children standing together in front of the sofa, at any point including the final frame. Their motion does not resolve into @Image 2: the recording ends mid-chase while they are still travelling and stepping. The new clip is exactly 5 seconds and has no end frame or driving video.

SURFACE-ONLY LOCK - every animated Christmas shape, including every shape above the real fireplace, is flat projected light attached to the existing plaster, chimney surface and ceiling. Moving drawings follow the surface perspective and bend or clip at actual corners and ceiling details. They have no thickness, volume, free-space parallax or physical cast shadow. The real fireplace opening and mantel remain real stationary architecture. No character, sleigh, ribbon, spark, snowflake, smoke curl or ornament floats between the camera and a wall, emerges from the fireplace, hovers above the mantel, or enters the usable room. Apparent depth belongs only to the drawn illustration on the wall.

ROOM AND IDENTITY - a spacious double-height coastal Georgian Christmas great room with a high TRAY CEILING: a broad flat rectangular raised centre, four gently sloping border planes and a wide flat perimeter ledge with crisp stepped moulding. A tall white-painted fluted chimney breast stands on the back wall with a white marble mantel; three tall sash windows occupy the left wall and a wide rectangular white-trimmed opening sits on the right. Pale ash floorboards, a large dove-grey linen sectional sofa, a rectangular dove-grey upholstered ottoman and a soft blue wool rug. The side opening on the right wall remains lateral to the route, never an extra threshold ahead. a girl of about eight with warm medium-tan skin and long dark-brown hair in a high ponytail tied with a red bow; a boy of about six with warm medium-tan skin and straight dark-brown hair in a short side-swept cut. Both fully dressed in ivory brushed-cotton Christmas pyjama sets patterned with small red Christmas trains, green holly leaves and gold stars, with matching loose pyjama trousers and cranberry wool socks. Preserve these identities and architecture from @Image 2.

PROJECTED SCENE CONTENT - LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a magical NORTH POLE CHRISTMAS EXPRESS: a magnificent red-and-gold Christmas steam train with brass wheels and carriages full of ribboned gifts travels through a snowy North Pole station, surrounded by glowing red-roofed toy workshops, holly wreaths, golden lanterns and tall decorated fir trees. Friendly elves wave beside stacks of presents while Santa greets them on a warmly lit station platform. Along the upper walls, linked gold bells, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands connect the station roofs into a continuous Christmas panorama. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer sweep around a brilliant fine-pointed golden Christmas star, their long curling red-and-gold ribbon trail woven among crisp snowflakes and tiny golden lights. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold and cranberry red dominant with evergreen accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. 

CURRENT BRIEF — STRONG CONTINUOUS MOTION: The existing Christmas express travels steadily along its illustrated route on the walls, wheels and connecting rods turning, white steam puffing repeatedly from its locomotive chimney; elves wave and carry gifts beside the station. Preserve the artwork already visible. Every illustrated chimney emits fresh curling smoke continuously, moving at least one chimney height per second; the sleigh crosses a substantial part of the ceiling with galloping reindeer. Existing ribbon light fields carry clearly travelling aurora-like waves along their length, with brightness crests moving rather than blinking in place. Do not add a new aurora object where none exists; animate the existing sky and ribbon shapes. Extremely high quality candid vertical iPhone photo taken from the floor of a double-height Christmas living room, looking up and across at a woman standing on the mezzanine landing, evening. We see her from below and slightly to the side, her raised arms and the high ceiling in front of her.

FRAMING AND ANGLE: the camera stands on the living-room floor MUCH closer in to the stairs than a wide establishing shot, tilted up, so the woman and the inflatable she is taping fill most of the picture and the room reads as context around them rather than as the subject. The mezzanine landing crosses the frame with its black metal railing along it, and the woman stands on that landing behind the railing DEAD CENTRE on the vertical axis of the frame, framed from roughly the waist up and very large in the picture - she is the biggest thing in the photograph and the taped inflatable is directly above and ahead of her, also near the centre, so her reaching arm and the inflatable together sit in the middle of the frame. THE KEY ELEMENT: a large inflatable Santa Claus decoration is TAPED FLAT TO THE HIGH WHITE CEILING above the double-height space, lying on its back against the plaster and facing down into the room, held by a mess of criss-crossed silver duct tape strips over its legs, arms and hat. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a glowing VICTORIAN CHRISTMAS MARKET: rows of wooden chalet stalls with warmly lit windows and fir-garlanded roofs line a snowy town square, a carousel with gilded horses turns beside a towering decorated Christmas tree, carol singers in top hats and bonnets hold lanterns, and tall snowy gabled townhouses with glowing windows rise behind them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden bulbs, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the stall roofs into a continuous Christmas panorama. ACROSS THE CEILING, a vast wreath of huge glowing crystalline snowflakes circles a bright silver crescent moon, and Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer race around it, their long curling red-and-gold ribbon trail woven among tiny golden lights. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold and cranberry red dominant with evergreen and snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. Build a structurally believable room: a spacious double-height Parisian Haussmann Christmas great room with a high GROIN-VAULTED CEILING: two smooth plaster barrel vaults crossing at right angles, their four curved surfaces meeting along crisp diagonal groin edges that rise to a single central crown. A tall white-painted chimney breast stands on the back wall with a grey-veined marble mantel; two tall French windows with white-painted wooden frames and slim glazing bars occupy the left wall and a wide doorway with a white-painted wooden casing sits on the right. It is night, all house lamps switched off. A real Christmas tree with warm gold lights, gold and blush-pink baubles, cream silk ribbon and wrapped gifts stands beside the fireplace. Evergreen garland with holly berries covers the mantel, with three cream-and-gold knitted stockings below. The projection is the main illumination.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every architectural plane and seam, every beam or cove, and the entire chimney breast all the way to the ceiling. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a glowing VICTORIAN CHRISTMAS MARKET: rows of wooden chalet stalls with warmly lit windows and fir-garlanded roofs line a snowy town square, a carousel with gilded horses turns beside a towering decorated Christmas tree, carol singers in top hats and bonnets hold lanterns, and tall snowy gabled townhouses with glowing windows rise behind them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden bulbs, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the stall roofs into a continuous Christmas panorama. ACROSS THE CEILING, a vast wreath of huge glowing crystalline snowflakes circles a bright silver crescent moon, and Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer race around it, their long curling red-and-gold ribbon trail woven among tiny golden lights. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold and cranberry red dominant with evergreen and snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The four curved vault surfaces and their crisp diagonal groin edges remain clearly three-dimensional. The sleigh and the snowflake wreath bend at every groin line and sweep down each curved vault surface before continuing onto the walls. The tall chimney breast receives a continuous picture with clear folds at its two projecting corners. The white-painted wooden window frames, glazing bars, doorway casing and boiserie panels carry the projection straight across their faces, with thin shadow breaks only at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. THE WOODEN FRAMES CARRY THE PICTURE TOO: the painted wooden window frames, sashes and glazing bars, the door and doorway casings, the skirting boards, the mantel and every other piece of wooden trim the beam crosses are covered by the same continuous projected imagery as the wall beside them - never left as bare white unlit outlines - with only a thin real shadow line at each edge. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The parquet floor, the soft ivory wool rug, the blush-pink velvet sectional sofa, the cream upholstered ottoman and the tree carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. The projection is still dense, bright and colourful, but it reads as the real light of a home Christmas projector falling on real walls, and the shadows keep a little ordinary room detail.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the fine cotton weave of the pyjamas, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the drywall, the surface texture of the white-painted wooden boiserie and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. det.text:
OPENING STATE - frame 0.0s must preserve the supplied start image's already complete, saturated projection on every visible wall, chimney surface, groin-vaulted ceiling panel and ceiling detail. There is no lighting-up event, unveiling, growth, filling, wipe, fade-in or transition from bare plaster. Never erase the ceiling artwork at the beginning and redraw it later.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas.

SUMMARY: two children play in a double-height Christmas great room while a projected Christmas village picture is PLAYING across the back wall and the entire groin-vaulted ceiling and its architectural details, thrown there by a projector standing in the room. 4 seconds, one continuous handheld phone take, vertical.

GLOBAL STYLE: crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed. Sharp and in focus from the first frame to the last, at least as sharp as the start image. No blur, no haze, no soft focus, no washed-out exposure, no colour shift.

ASSET ROLES: @Image 1 is frame 0.0s and controls a spacious double-height Parisian Haussmann Christmas great room with a high GROIN-VAULTED CEILING: two smooth plaster barrel vaults crossing at right angles, their four curved surfaces meeting along crisp diagonal groin edges that rise to a single central crown. White-painted wooden boiserie panelling lines the walls. A tall white-painted chimney breast stands on the back wall with a grey-veined marble mantel; two tall French windows with white-painted wooden frames and slim glazing bars occupy the left wall and a wide doorway with a white-painted wooden casing sits on the right. Herringbone oak parquet, a large blush-pink velvet sectional sofa, a rectangular cream upholstered ottoman and a soft ivory wool rug. Preserve exact child identity, clothing, furniture, colours, full existing projection and opening framing in the supplied image.

SUBJECTS:
THE SMALLER CHILD - a boy of about six with light olive skin and short dark-brown wavy hair, on the rug in front of the sofa, back to camera and slightly to the side, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling with his arms out in wonder, turning slowly on the spot.
THE OTHER CHILD - a girl of about eight with fair skin and long straight light-blonde hair in two plaits tied with red ribbons, jumping on the sofa cushions, caught mid-air above them with her knees bent and her arms flung up, the cushion compressed under where she pushed off, bouncing on the spot.
Both in emerald-green brushed-cotton Christmas pyjama sets patterned with small cream reindeer, red Christmas stockings and gold stars, with matching loose pyjama trousers and red wool socks. Both stay small in frame, in scale with the huge room. Exactly two children. No third child, no adult, no pet.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running in the room, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the back wall and the whole groin-vaulted ceiling. Everything glowing on the plaster, wall material and ceiling details is that one cone landing.
THE PICTURE - the animated scene is the exact Christmas panorama visible in the start image. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a glowing VICTORIAN CHRISTMAS MARKET: rows of wooden chalet stalls with warmly lit windows and fir-garlanded roofs line a snowy town square, a carousel with gilded horses turns beside a towering decorated Christmas tree, carol singers in top hats and bonnets hold lanterns, and tall snowy gabled townhouses with glowing windows rise behind them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden bulbs, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the stall roofs into a continuous Christmas panorama. ACROSS THE CEILING, a vast wreath of huge glowing crystalline snowflakes circles a bright silver crescent moon, and Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer race around it, their long curling red-and-gold ribbon trail woven among tiny golden lights. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold and cranberry red dominant with evergreen and snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. 

HOW THE PICTURE BEHAVES - THIS IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE CLIP. In every previous attempt the picture sat dead still like printed wallpaper and the clip was worthless. THE PICTURE IS A FILM PLAYING ON A CINEMA SCREEN: the screen is the plaster, wall material and ceiling details and holds perfectly still, while everything inside the picture is in constant motion for all four seconds. The start image shows the film already fully projected across the walls AND the entire ceiling. From the first frame continue the moving artwork at the same full coverage and brightness. Start motion within the existing picture, never the appearance of the picture itself. Matching @Image 1 applies to the great room, the furniture, the children and the colours, not to where any element of the picture sits.
THE PICTURE AS A WHOLE IS ANCHORED. It does not rotate, spin, swing, sweep sideways or slide across the room as one sheet. Its outer boundary stays where it is. The motion lives INSIDE it, element by element:
- THE CHIMNEY SMOKE - every single chimney in the village is smoking, not one of them without its plume. Each thin curl climbs upward out of its chimney pot, leaning slightly to the right, rising about one roof height every second, widening and thinning as it climbs and fading out before it reaches the ribbons, while a fresh curl forms at the pot behind it. The plumes are never a fixed painted shape.
- THE RISING SPARKS - a slow steady rise of glowing gold sparks lifts off the village chimneys and climbs the full height of the wall to join the star field, drifting slightly sideways as it goes, new sparks leaving the chimneys continuously so the column never empties.
- THE SNOWFLAKE WREATH AND RIBBONS - the crystalline snowflakes of the wreath turn and travel around the crescent moon, and each red-and-gold ribbon ripples ALONG ITS OWN LENGTH, a slow travelling wave running down the band away from the moon, about a third of the ribbon's length every second, the ribbon swelling brighter and thinner as the wave passes and its lower fringe combing and re-forming. Each ribbon's overall fan stays where it is on the plaster; the wave inside it travels. Every ribbon on the wall and on the ceiling is doing this at the same time.
- THE SLEIGH AND THE REINDEER - they are FLYING. The team travels steadily across the ceiling on a long sweeping curve away from where it sits in the start image, racing around the crescent moon, covering about a fifth of the ceiling's width every second, so by 4.0s it has crossed most of the way. The reindeer's legs gallop, their heads nod, the sleigh rocks gently behind them, the long tapering trail streams out behind, and the whole team rises and dips a little as it goes. The team is never parked.
- THE EXISTING MARKET FIGURES. The illustrated carousel turns steadily along the lower wall, its gilded horses rising and falling; carol singers sway and lift their lanterns; shoppers stroll between the stalls, moving about one body length every second. All keep moving from the first frame to the last.
- THE GOLD LIGHT WAVES. Successive bright gold waves TRAVEL OUTWARD along the existing red-and-gold ribbon and evergreen-garland paths on the ceiling, each bright crest travelling about a third of its ribbon's length every second, fading behind as the next bright crest follows, so the existing ribbons sparkle and flow continuously. No new rings or new objects appear; the moving light stays within the shapes that already exist in the image.
- THE SNOWFLAKES AND THE POINTS OF LIGHT - each one drifts downward and slightly sideways about a quarter of the wall's height every second, the way snow falls past a window at night. Each turns slowly on its own centre as it drifts and breathes brighter and dimmer on its own timing. One that reaches the floor line fades out there while a fresh one fades in high near the plaster ceiling details, so the density holds even.
- THE SMALL TRAVELLERS - the red-and-white striped candy canes and the glowing baubles turn slowly end over end as they drift; the strings of golden bulbs twinkle and sway above the stalls and the big gold bells swing gently on their crimson bow with the clappers moving inside them; the long-tailed shooting stars streak across, their tails thinning out behind them, and fade, with fresh ones setting off elsewhere.
- THE STAR FIELD - the small gold stars hold their places and twinkle, each brightening and dimming on its own timing, never all together.
- THE CRESCENT MOON - the bright silver crescent moon is the ONLY element that holds its centre position. It stays exactly where it is on the ceiling for the whole clip and only brightens and dims very slightly. Nothing else in the picture is allowed to hold still.
Because the back wall and the whole ceiling are lit by the SAME projector, they are one picture and behave identically at the same instant. Whatever the flakes, the ribbons and the stars on the wall are doing, the flakes, the ribbons and the stars on the ceiling are doing at the same moment and at the same speed. There is never a still ceiling above a moving wall. Nothing is painted, printed or stencilled on the plaster, wall material and ceiling details. NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR: the floorboards shown in the starting frame, the rug and sectional sofa shown in the starting frame, the cream ottoman, the tree and the gifts carry no projected shapes at all.

TIMELINE:
0.0-1.0s the person filming takes one clear step forward; the frame moves in and settles. THE OTHER CHILD bounces on the sofa cushions with both arms up, laughing. THE SMALLER CHILD turns on the rug with his face tipped up.
1.0-2.0s the camera holds in the closer position. THE OTHER CHILD pushes up harder and drops back down onto the cushion, her knees bending and springing back. THE SMALLER CHILD keeps turning and tips his head further back.
2.0-4.0s the camera tilts up in one slow smooth move past the top of the tree until the groin-vaulted ceiling fills the upper half of the frame, the ribbons rippling along it, the travelling gold light waves still spreading outward across it from the crescent moon and the sleigh team still racing around that moon. Both children stay low in the frame and keep moving.

AUDIO: room tone, two children laughing and squealing, feet thumping on the sofa cushions, feet on a rug. (no BGM). No subtitles.

POSITIVE LOCKS: real-time motion at normal speed throughout - real children moving at real speed with real weight. Exactly two children, and their cotton pyjamas read clearly. One continuous take with no cut. The camera makes one move per beat and no more. The picture's outer boundary holds still while every element inside it moves. Walls and ceiling always move together. THE OTHER CHILD stays on the sofa. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.

DO NOT INCLUDE: blank or partly blank walls or ceiling at the start; a projection appearing, switching on, fading in, spreading, growing or revealing itself during the shot; an opening before-and-after transformation; a frozen or still pattern; chimneys that are not smoking; a ribbon that sits still; a sleigh and reindeer parked in one place; a carousel that does not turn, carol singers who do not move, or a snowflake wreath that does not turn; travelling gold light waves that do not spread outward; flakes that only twinkle without travelling; a still ceiling above moving walls; an un-animated area of the groin-vaulted ceiling or an un-animated ceiling detail in any frame; the whole picture rotating, spinning, sweeping or sliding as one sheet; slow motion; floating or weightless movement; any music; children standing still; a third child; an adult; the projector unit in shot; jellyfish, fish, coral or bubbles; blur; a cut; on-screen text; subtitles.

CONTINUOUS MOTION CHECK - from the first visible frame through the very last frame, the wall AND ceiling each contain clearly travelling projected elements at the same time: the sleigh changes position across the ceiling, its reindeer gallop; the existing illustrated carousel turns and the carol singers and shoppers move along the wall; market lights twinkle; the snowflake wreath turns; bells swing; ribbons carry travelling light waves; snowflakes translate across the surfaces. Twinkle alone and camera movement alone do not count. Maintain that same lively real-time motion with no opening freeze, no settling into a still image and no final freeze. All light bends with the real wall and ceiling geometry and stays on those surfaces.

SURFACE MAPPING - The four curved vault surfaces and their diagonal groin edges remain stationary. Drawings bend at every groin line, fold around the chimney breast corners and carry across the wooden French window frames, doorway casing and boiserie, with correct surface perspective and occlusion. All physical architecture stays stationary.

CURRENT BRIEF — STRONG CONTINUOUS MOTION: The existing carousel turns steadily in the illustrated town square on the walls, its gilded horses rising and falling; the carol singers sway and lift their lanterns; shoppers stroll between the wooden stalls and the strings of golden bulbs twinkle. Preserve the artwork already visible. Every illustrated chimney emits fresh curling smoke continuously, moving at least one chimney height per second; the sleigh crosses a substantial part of the ceiling with galloping reindeer. Existing ribbon light fields carry clearly travelling aurora-like waves along their length, with brightness crests moving rather than blinking in place. The existing snowflake wreath on the ceiling is ALWAYS in motion: its huge crystalline snowflakes turn slowly on their centres and travel around the crescent moon, sparkling continuously from the first frame to the last, never a still painted ring. The market buildings and the crescent moon stay anchored while characters, vehicles, smoke and light waves travel independently. The only physical motion in the room is the specified children and camera; all Christmas artwork and illustrated smoke remain flat light on real wall/ceiling surfaces. No floating 3D objects. No frozen opening or ending. Use the exact architecture and artwork in this shot's references; animate only illustrated characters actually present, never invent source-template deer or rabbits. Natural room audio only, no music.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo, the same dim hallway, the same antique brass round doorknob in the same place, the same small pine wreath with the red velvet bow hung on the door, the same oak floorboards, the same woman's forearm entering from the lower right with the dusty-blue chunky cable-knit wool sleeve and no jewellery, with light caramel skin, slender adult woman's fingers and short natural nails, her hand closed around the knob, the same camera position and camera height, the same warm low-key evening light.

CHANGE 1 - THE DOOR. It is now a warm mustard-ochre painted solid wood door with one tall recessed upper panel and one short wide lower panel, a satin finish and crisp white-painted surrounding trim, an antique brass round knob and matching brass escutcheon, set in a cream painted frame. Same size, same position in frame, same flat-on angle as @Image 1.

CHANGE 2 - the door is FULLY CLOSED and flush in its frame. There is NO gap at the edge of the door and absolutely NO light spilling out - no rainbow strip, no coloured glow, no bright line, no glare anywhere along the door edge, the jamb, the threshold or the floor. The seam between door and frame is a plain dark shadow line only. Nothing behind the door is visible or lit.

THE WREATH - it hangs on the FACE of the door, centred on the upper half of the door and comfortably inside the frame with clear door surface visible all the way around it. It must NOT be cut off by the right edge of the picture and must NOT drift onto the door frame or the wall. The whole circle of the wreath and the whole red velvet bow are visible.

EXPOSURE - brighter and warmer than @Image 1, which came out too dark. The hallway is dim but comfortably readable: the mustard-ochre paint reads clearly as warm ochre, the brass knob catches a warm highlight, the oak floorboards and the forearm are clearly lit, and the shadows stay deep but still hold detail. Do not crush the blacks and do not let any part of the frame go to a flat dark mass.

SHARPNESS - this frame must be tack sharp edge to edge: every moulding edge and panel corner in the door, the machined edge and the patina of the brass knob, the individual needles of the pine wreath and the woven nap of the red velvet bow, the skin texture and fine hairs on the forearm, the grain of the floorboards. Extremely high quality, perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic. BANNED: blur, soft focus, haze, mushy low-detail surfaces, waxy skin, a dreamy or filtered look, motion blur, noise, upscaling artefacts.

Natural handheld UGC look, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, photorealistic, zero motion blur, no CGI look.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

REFERENCE ROLES: @Image 1 owns the exact layout, product geometry, hand positions and camera. @Image 2 owns the established photographic look and product fidelity only; use the new hands, materials and background specified above. All parts of this photograph, including the background, are in crisp natural iPhone deep focus, no portrait mode, no bokeh, no blur.

det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, framing, scale and poses. Wholesome family Christmas scene. @Image 1 owns composition geometry only. @Image 2 owns the dense saturated photographic projection look; change the architecture and children to the descriptions below. Both reference images are generated stills, not photographs of a documented real house.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing of a whole tall room seen from a doorway, the same natural low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two children - a boy standing TURNED AROUND FACING THE CAMERA, front-on, his face fully visible and lit by the coloured light, looking towards the lens with a delighted open-mouthed smile, arms slightly out in wonder, and a girl beside him seen from behind, still looking up at the projected wall.

The boy is of about seven with deep brown skin and short black coily hair; the girl is of about six with fair skin, rosy cheeks and a short dark-brown bob with a straight fringe. Both children are fully dressed for winter in navy-blue brushed-cotton Christmas pyjama sets patterned with small white snowmen, gold bells and red holly berries, with matching loose pyjama trousers and cream wool socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene.

CHANGE 1 - THE ROOM. Build a structurally believable room: a spacious double-height Hamptons shingle-style Christmas great room with a high TRUSSED CEILING: a steep pitched plaster ceiling crossed by three white-painted wooden king-post trusses, each with a horizontal tie beam, a vertical king post and two angled struts. White-painted wooden shiplap lines the walls. A tall white-painted shiplap chimney breast stands on the back wall with a whitewashed brick fireplace and a white-painted wooden mantel; two tall windows with white-painted wooden frames and slim glazing bars occupy the left wall and a wide doorway with a white-painted wooden casing sits on the right. Wide pale oak floorboards, a large slate-blue linen sectional sofa, a rectangular cream upholstered ottoman and a soft cream jute-and-wool rug. Seen from the doorway; the new a warm mustard-ochre painted solid wood door with one tall recessed upper panel and one short wide lower panel, a satin finish and crisp white-painted surrounding trim is open out of frame.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. A real Christmas tree with warm gold lights, red and gold baubles, candy canes, red velvet ribbon and wrapped gifts stands beside the fireplace. Evergreen garland with holly berries covers the mantel, with three red-and-green knitted stockings below. The projection is the main illumination.

CHANGE 2 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every architectural plane and seam, every beam or cove, and the entire chimney breast all the way to the ceiling. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a SNOWY ALPINE CHRISTMAS MOUNTAIN VILLAGE: wooden chalets with glowing windows climb a snowy mountainside, a little red cable car glides above them on a lit wire, families on wooden sledges slide down lantern-lit slopes, a small stone church with a lit steeple stands among them, and tall snow-laden fir trees rise between them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the chalet roofs into a continuous Christmas panorama. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc through a sky of big glowing six-point snowflakes, twinkling golden stars and softly glowing star-shaped lanterns, their long curling red-and-gold ribbon trail woven among tiny golden lights. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, cranberry red and alpine evergreen dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The steep pitched ceiling planes remain clearly three-dimensional, meeting at a crisp central ridge. The three painted wooden trusses sit in the beam: the sleigh and the ceiling picture continue straight across every tie beam, king post and strut and fold onto their sides, while the ceiling picture continues behind them at its own depth. The tall chimney breast receives a continuous picture with clear folds at its two projecting corners. The white-painted wooden window frames, glazing bars, doorway casing and shiplap boards carry the projection straight across their faces, with thin shadow breaks only at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. THE WOODEN FRAMES CARRY THE PICTURE TOO: the painted wooden window frames, sashes and glazing bars, the door and doorway casings, the skirting boards, the mantel and every other piece of wooden trim the beam crosses are covered by the same continuous projected imagery as the wall beside them - never left as bare white unlit outlines - with only a thin real shadow line at each edge. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 3 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The oak floorboards, the soft cream jute-and-wool rug, the slate-blue linen sectional sofa, the cream upholstered ottoman, the tree and the gifts carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children's faces and their cotton pyjamas catch that spill so both faces read clearly.

CHANGE 4 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no side table, no stool, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain floor and the edge of the rug.

NATURAL, LESS CINEMATIC LOOK - a little less cinematic than a film still: this is a candid photo a parent snapped on an iPhone at home, not a movie frame, a poster or an advert. True-to-life colour and contrast as they come straight out of the phone camera: no colour grading, no teal-and-orange grade, no vignette, no dramatic spotlighting and no heightened fantasy glow on the children. The projection is still dense, bright and colourful, but it reads as the real light of a home Christmas projector falling on real walls, and the shadows keep a little ordinary room detail.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the fine cotton weave of the pyjamas, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the drywall, the surface texture of the white-painted wooden shiplap and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Forward travel and upward aim are mechanically coupled as one motion, already underway together in frame zero. Keep the same gentle pace and the same forward-to-upward ratio for every frame, including while the door opens and while crossing its sill. Travel only about 0.8 metres forward over the entire shot, with an even upward tilt of about 18 degrees over those same five seconds. The wreath, door-panel edges and later the back-wall details drift smoothly downward in the frame from the beginning while perspective advances very gently. There is no forward-only phase and no later tilt-only phase. Never complete an entrance and then begin looking up. Do not accelerate the beginning, hurry through the door, ease in, ease out, steepen the tilt, speed-ramp or catch up to an end composition. The final frame can remain near the threshold with the back wall, furniture and ceiling visible; covering more distance or revealing the whole ceiling is not a goal. The door opens naturally during the same slow glide; its opening is not a camera cue. Preserve the same doorframe and room features across adjacent frames as the camera physically crosses the single sill. No cut, concealed edit, dissolve, match cut, scene replacement, teleport, jump or sudden perspective change. Maintain this single gentle motion unchanged until the clip ends.

CHILD MOVEMENT - PRIMARY CORRECTION: @Image 2 shows the room EMPTY. EXACTLY TWO CHILDREN exist in this clip - the girl and the boy described in this text - and nobody else ever appears: no third child, no extra kids in the background, on the sofa or in the doorway, no adult. There is no pose, spot or arrangement of them to copy, and they never stand still anywhere. They are already running a game of chase behind the closed door, and the chase never ends inside this clip. Per second:
0-1s: in the very first gap of the opening door the girl is already running, caught mid-stride crossing the gap from left to right, one foot off the floor; the boy runs two strides behind her.
1-2s: both run a wide curve across the rug away from the camera, arms swinging; the boy throws one arm up and points at the flying sleigh on the ceiling while still running.
2-3s: the girl spins round once while running, arms out, laughing up at the ceiling; the boy runs round the ottoman after her.
3-4s: the girl runs past the Christmas tree toward the right-hand side of the room; the boy chases two strides behind at a different depth.
4-5s: both are still running mid-stride when the clip ends, the girl near the right edge of the frame, the boy crossing the rug behind her.
They are never side by side, never face the camera, never pause, never stop in front of the sofa. This child action must not alter the camera movement specified above.

DIRECT ROOM ENTRY - PRIMARY GEOMETRY CORRECTION: the closed door in @Image 1 is fitted directly into the living room's entrance wall. Its far face opens immediately into the furnished Christmas living room in @Image 2. There is ONE door and ONE thin normal wall-thickness threshold, about 15 cm deep. The very first gap reveals the living room itself, its already-moving children and active projections, close behind this door. As the camera crosses that single threshold it is already INSIDE the living room beside the near end of the sectional and rug shown in the reference. The living room floor begins at the far edge of the same sill; its side walls and high trussed ceiling meet this entrance wall directly. No intervening hall, foyer, vestibule, tunnel, passage, empty approach space, second doorway or arch to walk under. Do not frame the living room at the far end of another space. The side opening visible on the reference room's RIGHT SIDE WALL is a lateral room feature only, away from the camera's route; never place it in front of the camera or between this door and the living room. Preserve the exact supplied closed-door first frame. After opening that same door, the existing continuous forward movement enters the living room directly.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home at Christmas.

TASK: image-to-video, one continuous handheld phone POV take, vertical 9:16. Frame 0.0s is the start image: a warm mustard-ochre painted solid wood door with one tall recessed upper panel and one short wide lower panel, a satin finish and crisp white-painted surrounding trim fully closed with a wreath, a hand on the brass knob. @Image 2 is a reference photo of the EMPTY room for the layout, trussed ceiling, furniture, colours and projection artwork appearance; it contains no people.
