PER-SECOND ANIMATION TRACK (4 s):
0-1s: the sleigh team is already flying, reindeer galloping; the skaters are already gliding and thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
1-2s: the sleigh has moved a quarter of the ceiling and is crossing the silver moon; the skaters loop across the lake; the horse-drawn sleigh glides over the ice; the owls swoop; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
2-3s: as the camera tilts up the sleigh flies on across the vaulted ceiling; the polar bears walk along the snowbanks; the lanterns sway; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
3-4s: the sleigh keeps flying toward the far side of the ceiling; the skaters keep twirling; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney; a shooting star streaks across - sleigh flying, smoke pouring from every chimney, skaters gliding, owls swooping, snow swirling, all moving in the final frame.
All of this is flat projected light lying on the real plaster, the ash ridge beam and rafters, the basalt chimney breast, the slat panels and the ash window frames: it bends with the surfaces, never floats into the room, and nothing is projected on the floor, furniture or children.

CHILDREN - AMAZED, AND ALWAYS MOVING:
THE GIRL lands from the jump shown in the start image onto the sofa cushions and keeps bouncing along the sofa with small, springy, real-speed bounces - her feet leave the cushion by only 15 to 25 centimetres, about two bounces per second, the cushion visibly sinking on every landing - moving a little further along the sofa with each bounce while she points one arm straight up at Santa's flying sleigh, head tipped back, mouth wide open, squealing with delight.
THE BOY walks slowly backwards across the rug with his head tipped far back, one arm stretched up pointing at the sleigh, turning his body to follow it as it flies across the ceiling; around 2 seconds he glances across at his sister, points up again and laughs, then keeps stepping and gazing up.
Neither child ever stands still, poses or faces the camera. Real children moving at real speed with real weight: quick, snappy bounces under normal gravity, never slow motion, never floating, never a high exaggerated leap, no morphing limbs.

TIMELINE (camera):
0.0-1.0s the person filming takes one small step forward; the frame moves in slightly and settles.
1.0-2.0s the camera holds in the closer position.
2.0-4.0s the camera tilts up in one slow smooth move past the top of the tree, only far enough that the vaulted ceiling fills the upper half of the frame - it never tilts past the projected picture. The ENTIRE vaulted ceiling in view, every plane, beam and corner, is covered with the projection - starry midnight sky, the silver full moon, the snowflakes and the flying sleigh - no bare plaster, no bare wood, no unprojected corner anywhere in view. Both children stay low in the frame and keep moving.

ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, cranberry red and harbour blue dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely. The carved pine window frames and muntins, the deep-set openings and the carved pine doorway carry the projection straight across their faces, with thin shadow breaks only at their actual edges. - THE WATER: waves roll across the harbour and bright glints of light dance on them.
- THE PEOPLE: little families walk along the snowy quay pulling sledges, about one house-width every second; children throw snowballs; skaters glide on the frozen edge of the harbour.
- SHOOTING STARS AND FIREWORKS: a new shooting star streaks across the ceiling about every second, leaving a glittering tail; small round golden and red fireworks burst in the night sky above the harbour one after another, open into sparkles and fade.
- LIGHTS: the strings of golden lights along the upper walls twinkle in running chase patterns that race along the garlands; the red velvet bows sway; the stars twinkle and the silver moon glows.
- SNOWFALL: big projected snowflakes drift and swirl down across the whole picture, about a quarter of the wall height every second, turning as they fall - flat light on the walls and ceiling, never real snow in the room.
- THE HOUSES: the windows of the harbour houses flicker warmly on and off; wreaths on the doors sway.
PER-SECOND ANIMATION TRACK (5 s):
0-1s: through the very first gap of the door the sleigh is already flying, the lighthouse beam is already sweeping, fireworks are bursting and six thick white smoke columns are already rising from the house chimneys.
1-2s: the sleigh travels a quarter of the ceiling; a lit ship sails across the harbour; the families pull their sledges along the quay; a shooting star streaks over; the smoke columns keep climbing the walls.
2-3s: the sleigh flies on; the lighthouse beam sweeps over the ceiling; two fireworks burst above the harbour; the lights chase along the garlands; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
3-4s: the sleigh keeps flying; the boats rock on the waves; skaters glide; snow swirls; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
4-5s: everything still moving at full pace in the final frame - sleigh flying, smoke pouring from every chimney, ship sailing, beam sweeping, fireworks bursting, snow falling.
All of this is flat projected light lying on the real adobe plaster, the round pine vigas and latillas and the carved pine window frames: it bends with the surfaces, never floats into the room, and nothing is projected on the floor, furniture or children.

CHILDREN - SPELLBOUND BY THE CEILING AND ALWAYS MOVING. EXACTLY TWO CHILDREN exist in this clip - THE BOY and THE GIRL described below - and nobody else ever appears: no third child, no extra kids in the background, on the sofa or in the doorway, no adult. The room reference photo is EMPTY, so there is no pose or spot to copy. When the first gap of the door opens, both children are ALREADY in the middle and far side of the room, at least three metres from the door - never standing in or near the doorway, never lined up facing the camera, never side by side. They were already watching the projection before the door opened and they are completely amazed by it: mouths wide open, eyebrows raised, gasping and laughing, eyes glued to the flying sleigh on the ceiling. They keep moving the whole time and follow the sleigh with their eyes, arms and feet. Per second:
0-1s: in the very first gap THE BOY is already walking slowly backwards across the rug, head tipped far back, one arm stretched straight up pointing at Santa's flying sleigh; THE GIRL, a few steps away from him, is up on tiptoe with both hands pressed to her cheeks, mouth open, staring straight up.
1-2s: THE BOY keeps stepping backwards and turns his body to follow the sleigh as it flies overhead, his pointing arm tracking it across the ceiling; THE GIRL runs three quick little steps across the rug in the same direction the sleigh is flying, one hand reaching up toward it.
2-3s: THE BOY looks over at THE GIRL, points up again and shouts with excitement, then looks straight back up; THE GIRL spins round once on the rug with her arms out and her face turned up to the ceiling, laughing.
3-4s: THE GIRL does two small excited bunny-hops on the spot, landing back on the rug at real speed, pointing up at the sweeping lighthouse beam; THE BOY walks sideways past the ottoman with his head still tipped back, following the sleigh.
4-5s: both are still moving in the last frame - THE BOY still stepping and pointing up, THE GIRL trotting toward the Christmas tree while gazing up - never frozen.
They never stand still, never pose, never face the camera and never wait. Their feet stay on the floor: they never climb, jump onto or jump over the sofa, the ottoman or any furniture. Both stay in view: neither ducks behind furniture and pops up somewhere else. Real speed, real weight, grounded feet - no sliding, floating, slow motion or running in place. This child action never alters the camera movement.

CAMERA CONTINUITY: the entire five seconds are ONE slow, uninterrupted forward-and-upward glide. Forward travel and upward aim are coupled as one motion, already underway together in frame zero. Keep the same gentle pace and the same forward-to-upward ratio for every frame, including while the door opens and while crossing its sill. Travel only about 0.8 metres forward over the entire shot, with an even upward tilt of about 18 degrees over those same five seconds. The wreath, door-panel edges and later the back-wall details drift smoothly downward in the frame from the beginning while perspective advances very gently. There is no forward-only phase and no later tilt-only phase. Do not accelerate the beginning, hurry through the door, ease in, ease out, steepen the tilt, speed-ramp or catch up to an end composition. The final frame can remain near the threshold with the back wall, furniture and ceiling visible. The door opens naturally during the same slow glide; its opening is not a camera cue.

DIRECT ROOM ENTRY: the closed door in the start image is fitted directly into the great room's entrance wall and its far face opens straight into the furnished Christmas room shown in the room reference photo. ONE door, ONE thin normal threshold about 15 cm deep. The very first gap reveals the room itself, the already-moving children and the already-playing projection, close behind this door. No hall, foyer, vestibule, passage, empty approach space, second doorway or arch between this door and the room. The side doorway on the reference room's right wall is a lateral feature only and never lies ahead of the camera.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home at Christmas.

TASK AND ASSETS: image-to-video, one continuous handheld phone POV take, vertical 9:16. The START IMAGE is frame 0.0s: a turquoise-painted carved Santa Fe pine door with four square panels, a satin finish and a thick rounded white adobe surround fully closed with a wreath, a woman's hand with fair lightly sun-kissed skin and a forest-green chunky rib-knit wool sleeve on the brass knob. The ROOM REFERENCE IMAGE (attached as an image reference) controls only the room's architecture, furniture, colours and projected artwork; it contains no people and it is not an end frame, camera target or transition destination - never dissolve, cut, morph or snap into its composition. The two children come only from this text.

CONTINUOUS ACTION: during approximately the first 1.5 seconds the hand turns the knob and opens the door with a smooth, ordinary, unhurried push. The room behind it is already running: the projection is already playing and both children are already moving - the widening gap only uncovers more of a scene that was already happening. Nothing ignites or spreads as the door opens, and the door edge and frame stay plain wood - no glowing strip, no coloured fringe, no bright seam in the gap. The shot ends during the same gentle glide with the back wall, furniture and ceiling still visible.

CAMERA - eye height, normal wide-angle phone lens, a steady natural phone glide as described. No zoom, orbit, fisheye, lens warping, stop, second move or cut. The camera is the person's eyes; no phone, screen or device in frame. Hold the sharpness and exposure of the start image - crisp phone footage, in focus from the first frame to the last.

AUDIO - dry documentary sound only: the handle, the door swinging, the children gasping, laughing and calling out in delight, their footsteps on the floor, quiet room tone. (no BGM). No subtitles.

ROOM AND IDENTITY - a spacious double-height Santa Fe pueblo-revival Christmas great room with a high flat VIGA-AND-LATILLA CEILING: a row of massive round dark pine viga beams spans the room from side to side, with pale peeled latilla poles laid in a herringbone pattern across them. Smooth rounded white adobe plaster walls. A tall rounded white adobe chimney breast stands on the back wall with a thick pine beam mantel; a wall of tall deep-set windows with carved pine frames and muntins occupies the left wall and a wide carved pine doorway with a rounded adobe surround sits on the right. A saltillo terracotta tile floor, a large rust-red leather sectional sofa, a round woven-wool ottoman and a soft red-black-and-cream Southwestern-pattern wool rug.
THE BOY - a boy of about six with fair skin and short curly chestnut-brown hair. THE GIRL - a girl of about five with fair skin and long straight platinum-blonde hair in a single braid. Both fully dressed in forest-green and white brushed-cotton Christmas pyjama sets printed with little white snowmen and red mittens, with matching loose pyjama trousers and white wool socks.

PROJECTED SCENE CONTENT - LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a SNOWY CHRISTMAS HARBOUR TOWN: colourful gabled harbour houses with glowing windows and snowy roofs, a curl of white smoke rising from every chimney, little fishing boats strung with Christmas lights bobbing at the quay, a lighthouse sweeping its golden beam across the bay, families pulling sledges along the waterfront, and tall snow-laden fir trees on the hills behind. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with big soft snowflakes drifting down. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, cranberry red and harbour blue dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room.

BANNED - a third child or any extra people appearing at any moment; an adult; a child standing still, frozen, posed or waiting at any moment; the children standing in or next to the doorway when it opens; the children side by side or facing the camera; a child climbing onto or jumping on or over furniture; a child disappearing behind furniture and reappearing elsewhere; slow motion or floaty movement; a camera that moves, stops and moves again; a zoom; a cut; a glow along the door edge; light that grows or fills the room as the door opens; the projector unit visible; blur; music; subtitles.

MOTION GUARDRAILS - Failed if: any house or cottage without a thick rising smoke column; fewer than twelve things moving at once; a calm or slow projection; the sleigh stays in one place or only its legs move; any chimney has no rising smoke; any house without rising smoke; the boats do not bob; the lighthouse beam does not sweep; the families do not travel; snow does not fall; the picture moves only because the camera moves; the animation starts late, pauses or freezes at the end; the whole picture slides as one sheet; any projected shape floats in the room.

cards.desc: Boy bouncing in the viga SHED-ceiling Santa Fe bedroom, projection across the vigas and latillas.

det.text: START FRAME — v28_c06_g4.png

det.label: Image prompt · v28_c06_g4.png
det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, framing, scale and poses. Wholesome family Christmas scene. @Image 1 owns composition geometry only. @Image 2 owns the same boy's identity, Christmas pyjamas and dense saturated photographic projection look for this video; place that boy in the different bedroom described below. Both reference images are generated stills, not photographs of a documented real house.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same framing that shows the wall behind the bed and the ceiling above it both in shot, and the same natural low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself.

CEILING COVERAGE - THE PREVIOUS TAKE WAS REJECTED BECAUSE A BIG PART OF THE CEILING HAD NO PROJECTION: the whole sloping viga ceiling is covered by the dense, fully coloured Christmas picture with no exception - every round viga and every latilla, from the tall back wall all the way forward to the part of the ceiling directly above the camera at the very top edge of the frame, and every corner where the ceiling meets the walls. Stars, snowflakes, the big moon, glowing garland lights and the sleigh's golden trail run continuously over the vigas and the latillas; the part of the ceiling nearest the camera is just as dense, bright and colourful as the part above the bed. The wood reads only as thin shadow lines inside the picture. Not one bare brown plank, not one bare viga, not one dark, dim or unlit zone anywhere on the ceiling.

CHANGE 1 - THE CHILD. A different child from @Image 1: a boy of about six with fair skin and short curly chestnut-brown hair, fully dressed for winter in a forest-green and white brushed-cotton Christmas pyjama set printed with little white snowmen and red mittens, with matching loose pyjama trousers and white wool socks. He is standing up on top of the bed, knees bent and both arms raised out to his sides, caught mid-bounce, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling, laughing. Clearly standing on top of the bed, not sitting on its edge.

CHANGE 2 - THE ROOM. Build a structurally believable room: a bright-proportioned Santa Fe pueblo-revival bedroom with a high SHED CEILING of dark round vigas and pale latillas sloping up from the front of the room to the tall back wall. A carved knotty-pine bed with a wide upholstered cream headboard is centred on the flat rounded white adobe back wall between two tall deep-set windows with carved pine frames and muntins, a carved pine nicho shelf above, white bedding with a red striped Chimayo wool blanket, pine bedside chests, a saltillo terracotta tile floor and a soft cream wool rug. The bed stays in the same place in the frame, leaving the room's ceiling geometry clearly visible.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. The bed keeps the bedding described above, with pillows and a knitted stocking. A small real Christmas tree with gold lights and red and turquoise ornaments stands by the window.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every roof plane and seam, wall above the headboard, window jambs and lintels. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a SNOWY CHRISTMAS HARBOUR TOWN: colourful gabled harbour houses with glowing windows and snowy roofs, a curl of white smoke rising from every chimney, little fishing boats strung with Christmas lights bobbing at the quay, a lighthouse sweeping its golden beam across the bay, families pulling sledges along the waterfront, and tall snow-laden fir trees on the hills behind. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with big soft snowflakes drifting down. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, cranberry red and harbour blue dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The sloping viga ceiling remains clearly three-dimensional, meeting the walls at crisp lines. The sleigh and the ceiling picture are foreshortened along the slope, wrap straight across the round faces of the vigas and the latillas, and fold at the wall line before continuing down the walls. The flat adobe wall, the carved pine window frames and muntins, the nicho and the cream headboard carry properly foreshortened portions of the same continuous projection across their faces. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. THE WOODEN FRAMES CARRY THE PICTURE TOO: the painted wooden window frames, sashes and glazing bars, the door and doorway casings, the skirting boards, the mantel and every other piece of wooden trim the beam crosses are covered by the same continuous projected imagery as the wall beside them - never left as bare white unlit outlines - with only a thin real shadow line at each edge. THIS IS THE KEY CORRECTION FOR THIS SET, AND THE PREVIOUS ATTEMPT FAILED IT: every exposed wooden beam, rafter, truss, purlin, window frame, mullion, muntin, glazing bar, door frame and casing is COVERED by the projection. Treat the projected image as one continuous sheet of coloured light that ignores the wood: where a beam crosses the ceiling, the stars, snowflakes, the sleigh, the reindeer and the golden trail continue straight over the beam's underside and both of its sides, cut into strips by its edges and shifted slightly by its depth, in the same full colour and brightness as the ceiling around it; where a window frame, mullion or door casing crosses the wall, the garlands, lanterns and scenery continue straight over its face in the same full colour as the wall beside it. Seen from the camera, the wooden members are camouflaged inside the picture - their shape reads only from thin shadow lines and a slight shift of the image along their edges, never from their own bare wood colour. NOT ONE beam, rafter, frame, mullion or casing appears as a plain bare wooden stripe, a dark silhouette or an unlit outline cutting through the picture. Only the window GLASS stays the dark night outside; the frames around the glass carry the picture. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The terracotta tile floor, the soft cream wool rug, the bed and its covers, the bench at its foot and the little Christmas tree carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. The boy's face and his cotton pyjama top catch that spill so his face reads clearly.

CHANGE 5 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no stool, no side table, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain wall and floor.

NATURAL, LESS CINEMATIC LOOK - one small notch more natural than a polished film still: this is a candid photo a parent snapped on an iPhone at home, not a movie frame, a poster, a painting or an advert. True-to-life colour and contrast exactly as they come straight out of the phone camera: no colour grading, no teal-and-orange grade, no vignette, no dramatic spotlighting, no heightened fantasy glow on the children, and no storybook-illustration or oil-painting finish on the projection. The projection is still dense, bright and colourful, but its colour sits a touch closer to real life - rich, not neon - and it reads as the real light of a home Christmas projector falling on real walls: the plaster texture and wood grain show faintly through it, and the shadows keep a little more ordinary room detail, with the furniture, rug and floor clearly readable in the soft spill.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the fine cotton weave of the pyjamas, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the plaster, the crisp architectural edges of the ceiling and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

@Image 3 is a wood-coverage example only: it shows the projection lying straight across exposed wooden trusses and braces. Copy only that coverage of the wood; do not copy its room, architecture, children, colours or projected scenes.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.
CLIP — v28_c06_g4.mp4

det.label: Clip prompt · v28_c06_g4.mp4
det.text:
ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE - ABSOLUTE RULE: this 5-second clip is a single uninterrupted real-time shot from the start image to the last frame. No cut, no jump cut, no hidden edit, no time skip, no dissolve, no zoom, no reframe. Everything in it happens continuously, frame to frame.

OPENING STATE - frame 0.0s is EXACTLY the start image: the same framing, the same camera angle and the same view of the ceiling, with the projection already covering every visible part of the walls and the ceiling in full colour. The clip never starts from a higher, wider or different view, never shows any part of the room above the top edge of the start image, and there is no lighting-up, unveiling, growth, wipe or fade-in of the projection. Not one part of the ceiling - no cove band, trim edge, beam, plank or corner, including the strip at the very top edge of the frame - is ever bare, white, brown, dark or unlit in any frame.

PROJECTED ANIMATION - THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS CLIP, AND IT MUST BE BUSY AND ALIVE. The Christmas picture on the walls and the sloping viga ceiling is a hand-drawn ANIMATED CHRISTMAS CARTOON playing at full speed, like a TV screen showing a lively animated Christmas movie - never a still picture, never a calm picture. Only the projected picture is animated; the room and the children stay real photographic phone footage. AT EVERY MOMENT AT LEAST TWELVE DIFFERENT DRAWN THINGS ARE VISIBLY MOVING AT THE SAME TIME, spread across the left wall, the back wall, the right wall and the ceiling, each one with big, bold, easy-to-read motion that a viewer notices on a phone screen at a glance, independent of the camera. Only the drawn buildings, trees and the moon stay put; everything else travels, turns, rises, flutters or bursts. EVERY ANIMAL, BIRD, PERSON AND VEHICLE IN THE PICTURE IS A FLAT HAND-DRAWN CARTOON MADE OF PROJECTED LIGHT lying on the wall or ceiling surface - never a real, photographic, furry or three-dimensional creature. Nothing ever leaves the wall, stands out from it or flies into the room; every drawn thing moves only inside the flat projected picture.
- CHIMNEY SMOKE - A HARD REQUIREMENT, CHECKED FIRST: look at the houses in the start image - the row of red, cream and green gabled harbour houses with snowy roofs and glowing windows along the LEFT wall, and the tall gabled townhouses along the RIGHT wall. Every one of those roofs carries a chimney pot, and from EACH chimney a thick, bright WHITE column of smoke is already pouring out in the very first frame: big round puffs push out of the chimney top one after another, swell, curl and sway, and climb up the wall about one roof-height every second, stretching into long wavy trails that drift toward the ceiling before fading. At every moment at least SIX separate, wide, bright white smoke columns are visibly rising - three or more over the left-wall houses and three or more over the right-wall houses - as obvious as steam from a boiling kettle against the dark night sky. A house without rising smoke makes the clip wrong.
- SANTA'S SLEIGH AND EIGHT REINDEER: the WHOLE TEAM TRAVELS across the ceiling in one smooth sweeping arc, covering about one quarter of the ceiling's width every second, so it is in a clearly different place every second - never parked with only its legs moving. The reindeer gallop, heads bob, the sleigh rocks and dips, Santa waves, and the long golden trail streams and curls behind it, shedding glittering sparks.
- THE SHIPS: the tall ships and fishing boats strung with Christmas lights in the harbour bob and rock on the waves, their lit sails swelling and little red flags fluttering, and one lit ship sails clearly across the harbour from right to left during the clip.
- THE LIGHTHOUSE: its golden beam sweeps round in a continuous circle about every two seconds, raking across the water, the houses and up over the ceiling.
- THE WATER: waves roll across the harbour and bright glints of light dance on them.
- THE PEOPLE: little families walk along the snowy quay pulling sledges, about one house-width every second; children throw snowballs; skaters glide on the frozen edge of the harbour.
- SHOOTING STARS AND FIREWORKS: a new shooting star streaks across the ceiling about every second, leaving a glittering tail; small round golden and red fireworks burst in the night sky above the harbour one after another, open into sparkles and fade.
- LIGHTS: the strings of golden lights along the upper walls twinkle in running chase patterns that race along the garlands; the red velvet bows sway; the stars twinkle and the silver moon glows.
- DRAWN SNOW, FLAT ON THE WALLS ONLY: small flat cartoon snowflakes, drawn like the rest of the picture, slide slowly down the painted night sky on the walls and the ceiling, lying flat on the surface and bending round the corners with the picture - part of the projected drawing, like snow painted on wallpaper, never coming off the wall. THE AIR OF THE ROOM STAYS COMPLETELY CLEAR: no snowflakes, sparkles, glitter, dust or particles float or fall anywhere in the room - not in front of the boy, the bed, the Christmas tree or the camera, and not in the space between the camera and the walls.
- THE HOUSES: the windows of the harbour houses flicker warmly on and off; wreaths on the doors sway.
PER-SECOND ANIMATION TRACK (5 s):
0-1s: from the very first frame the sleigh is flying, the lighthouse beam is sweeping and six thick white smoke columns are rising from the house chimneys on both walls.
1-2s: the sleigh travels a quarter of the ceiling; a lit ship sails across the harbour behind the bed; a firework bursts; the smoke keeps climbing.
2-3s: the sleigh flies on; a shooting star streaks over; the lights chase along the garlands; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
3-4s: the sleigh keeps flying; the boats rock; the families pull their sledges; two fireworks burst; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
4-5s: everything still moving at full pace in the last frame.
All of this is flat projected light lying on the real adobe plaster, the vigas and latillas, the nicho and the carved pine window frames: it bends with the surfaces, never floats into the room, and nothing is projected on the floor, the bed or the boy.

CAMERA - ONE slow, gentle, continuous tilt DOWN from the first frame to the last, like a parent filming - the camera is NEVER static and the movement is clearly visible in every second.
0.0s: the clip starts EXACTLY on the start image framing - never higher, never wider, never showing anything above the top edge of the start image.
0.0-5.0s: the phone tilts DOWN smoothly at an even pace by about 12 degrees in total: the projected ceiling slides up and partly out of the top of the frame while more of the bed, the covers, the bench and the rug come into view at the bottom. Because the camera only ever moves DOWN from the start framing, no ceiling area outside the start image is ever seen. The boy stays fully in frame from head to feet.
One continuous take: no cut, no zoom, no push-in, no pull-back, never a tilt up, never a locked-off static frame.

THE BOY BOUNCES LIKE A REAL CHILD ON A REAL MATTRESS - natural, believable and unexaggerated, at real speed for all five seconds. Small, springy, continuous bounces on the same spot in the middle of the bed: his feet leave the mattress by only about 10 to 20 centimetres, about two bounces per second, the soft mattress visibly sinking under his feet on every landing and pushing him back up. REAL-TIME SPEED, NOT SLOW MOTION: each bounce is quick and snappy, taking only about half a second from push-off to landing under normal gravity, exactly like a real child filmed at normal speed - the footage is never slowed down, never time-stretched and never dreamy. Knees soft, head tipped back, mouth open, laughing up at the ceiling in amazement. While he bounces he throws one arm straight up and points at Santa's sleigh, turning his head to follow it as it flies across the ceiling, then drops the arm and points again. His body keeps exactly the same size, proportions, face and clothing in every frame; he stays in the same spot on the bed. No high leaps, no hanging in the air, no floating, no hopping across the bed, no stiff puppet-like body, no morphing limbs.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, a child at home with his family at Christmas. Crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed, sharp from first frame to last.

det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, framing, scale and poses. Wholesome family Christmas scene. @Image 1 owns composition geometry only. @Image 2 owns the dense saturated photographic projection look and the identity of the children only; this is a different room of the same house, described below. Both reference images are generated stills, not photographs of a documented real house.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing that shows a whole enormous double-height room with its full ceiling in shot, the same natural low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two poses - a girl JUMPING ON THE SOFA, caught mid-air above the cushions, knees bent, arms flung up, hair lifted, the cushion compressed under where she pushed off; and a boy standing on the rug in front of the sofa, seen from behind and slightly to the side, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling with his arms out in wonder. Both are small in frame, in scale with the huge room - keeping them small preserves the sense of how big the space is.

CHANGE 1 - THE CHILDREN. The same new children as @Image 2: a girl of about five with fair skin and long straight platinum-blonde hair in a single braid; a boy of about six with fair skin and short curly chestnut-brown hair. Both fully dressed in forest-green and white brushed-cotton Christmas pyjama sets printed with little white snowmen and red mittens, with matching loose pyjama trousers and white wool socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene.

CHANGE 2 - THE ROOM. Build a structurally believable room: a spacious double-height Santa Fe pueblo-revival Christmas family room with a high VAULTED CEILING: two broad sloping planes of pale latilla poles rising to a crisp central ridge, carried by a massive dark round pine ridge viga and dark round rafter vigas down each slope. Smooth rounded white adobe plaster walls. A tall white adobe chimney breast with a rounded kiva firebox stands on the back wall with a thick pine beam mantel; a full-height wall of deep-set windows with carved pine frames and muntins fills the left wall and a wide pair of carved pine doors sits on the right. A burnished terracotta tile floor, a large cream canvas sectional sofa, a round turquoise leather ottoman and a soft red-and-cream Southwestern wool rug. A different room from @Image 2 - not the same living room - seen from the middle of the family room with the whole ceiling in shot.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. A real Christmas tree with warm gold lights, red, turquoise and gold glass baubles, tinsel and wrapped gifts stands beside the fireplace. Evergreen garland with holly berries covers the mantel, with three red-and-turquoise knitted stockings below. The projection is the main illumination.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every architectural plane and seam, every beam or cove, and the entire chimney breast all the way to the ceiling. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a SNOWY CHRISTMAS HARBOUR TOWN: colourful gabled harbour houses with glowing windows and snowy roofs, a curl of white smoke rising from every chimney, little fishing boats strung with Christmas lights bobbing at the quay, a lighthouse sweeping its golden beam across the bay, families pulling sledges along the waterfront, and tall snow-laden fir trees on the hills behind. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with big soft snowflakes drifting down. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, cranberry red and harbour blue dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The two sloping latilla planes, the ridge viga and the rafter vigas remain clearly three-dimensional. The sleigh and the snowflakes fold at the ridge and continue straight across the round faces of the ridge viga and the rafter vigas, foreshortened along each slope, before continuing onto the walls. The tall adobe chimney breast receives a continuous picture with clear folds at its two projecting corners. The carved pine window frames and muntins and the carved pine doors carry the projection straight across their faces, with thin shadow breaks only at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. THE WOODEN FRAMES CARRY THE PICTURE TOO: the painted wooden window frames, sashes and glazing bars, the door and doorway casings, the skirting boards, the mantel and every other piece of wooden trim the beam crosses are covered by the same continuous projected imagery as the wall beside them - never left as bare white unlit outlines - with only a thin real shadow line at each edge. THIS IS THE KEY CORRECTION FOR THIS SET, AND THE PREVIOUS ATTEMPT FAILED IT: every exposed wooden beam, rafter, truss, purlin, window frame, mullion, muntin, glazing bar, door frame and casing is COVERED by the projection. Treat the projected image as one continuous sheet of coloured light that ignores the wood: where a beam crosses the ceiling, the stars, snowflakes, the sleigh, the reindeer and the golden trail continue straight over the beam's underside and both of its sides, cut into strips by its edges and shifted slightly by its depth, in the same full colour and brightness as the ceiling around it; where a window frame, mullion or door casing crosses the wall, the garlands, lanterns and scenery continue straight over its face in the same full colour as the wall beside it. Seen from the camera, the wooden members are camouflaged inside the picture - their shape reads only from thin shadow lines and a slight shift of the image along their edges, never from their own bare wood colour. NOT ONE beam, rafter, frame, mullion or casing appears as a plain bare wooden stripe, a dark silhouette or an unlit outline cutting through the picture. Only the window GLASS stays the dark night outside; the frames around the glass carry the picture. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The terracotta tile floor, the soft red-and-cream Southwestern wool rug, the cream canvas sectional sofa, the round turquoise leather ottoman and the tree carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children catch that spill so their cotton pyjamas read clearly.

CHANGE 5 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no round side table, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain rug and floor.

NATURAL, LESS CINEMATIC LOOK - one small notch more natural than a polished film still: this is a candid photo a parent snapped on an iPhone at home, not a movie frame, a poster, a painting or an advert. True-to-life colour and contrast exactly as they come straight out of the phone camera: no colour grading, no teal-and-orange grade, no vignette, no dramatic spotlighting, no heightened fantasy glow on the children, and no storybook-illustration or oil-painting finish on the projection. The projection is still dense, bright and colourful, but its colour sits a touch closer to real life - rich, not neon - and it reads as the real light of a home Christmas projector falling on real walls: the plaster texture and wood grain show faintly through it, and the shadows keep a little more ordinary room detail, with the furniture, rug and floor clearly readable in the soft spill.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the fine cotton weave of the pyjamas, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the drywall, the surface texture of the white adobe plaster and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

@Image 3 is a wood-coverage example only: it shows the projection lying straight across exposed wooden trusses and braces. Copy only that coverage of the wood; do not copy its room, architecture, children, colours or projected scenes.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

THE PICTURE - the animated scene is the exact Christmas panorama visible in the start image. PROJECTED ANIMATION - THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS CLIP, AND IT MUST BE BUSY AND ALIVE. The Christmas picture on the walls and the vaulted latilla ceiling is a hand-drawn ANIMATED CHRISTMAS CARTOON playing at full speed, like a TV screen showing a lively animated Christmas movie - never a still picture, never a calm picture. Only the projected picture is animated; the room and the children stay real photographic phone footage. AT EVERY MOMENT AT LEAST TWELVE DIFFERENT DRAWN THINGS ARE VISIBLY MOVING AT THE SAME TIME, spread across the left wall, the back wall, the right wall and the ceiling, each one with big, bold, easy-to-read motion that a viewer notices on a phone screen at a glance, independent of the camera. THE GIRL lands from the jump shown in the start image onto the sofa cushions and keeps bouncing along the sofa with small, springy, real-speed bounces - her feet leave the cushion by only 15 to 25 centimetres, about two bounces per second, the cushion visibly sinking on every landing - moving a little further along the sofa with each bounce while she points one arm straight up at Santa's flying sleigh, head tipped back, mouth wide open, squealing with delight.

Both children stay low in the frame and keep moving.
No zoom - the only forward movement is the one small physical step.

SURFACE MAPPING - The two sloping latilla planes, the ridge viga and the rafter vigas remain stationary. det.text:
TASK: image-to-video. The start image is frame 0.0s. Hold its kitchen, counter, hands, product and lighting exactly. The ONLY things that change are the cable seating into the port and the projector lighting up RED.

[1] SUMMARY
Locked-off close shot: a hand PLUGS a white USB-C connector INTO the small dark socket in the bottom rim of the projector's white dome, and the projector switches on with RED light. 4 seconds, one take, camera completely static.

[2] GLOBAL STYLE
Real phone footage on a stable surface, warm modern kitchen light, extremely sharp and clean, correctly exposed. No cinematic grade, no grain, no slow motion.

[3] ASSET ROLES
The start image controls the kitchen, the counter, both hands, the cable and the product. It is the only authority on the scene.

[4] OBJECTS
THE PROJECTOR - a matte-white dome-shaped body on a separate white four-legged splayed stand, standing left of centre on the counter. Set into the top of the dome is a flat circular BLACK perforated mesh disc. The top face is BLACK and stays black for every frame. No front lens, no camera head, no swivel.
THE LEFT HAND - a woman's hand in an oatmeal-and-red Nordic-patterned wool sweater sleeve pushed back, no jewellery of any kind - no rings, no bangle, no watch - resting on the left side of the dome. It does not move.
THE RIGHT HAND - a woman's hand in the same oatmeal-and-red Nordic-patterned wool sleeve, no jewellery, entering from the right edge of frame, holding a white cable connector near the base of the stand.
THE PORT - a small dark oval USB-C socket set into the white plastic at the very bottom rim of the dome body, just above where the dome meets the white stand, a little right of the dome's centre line. It is clearly visible in the start image and it is the only opening on the product. It is NOT on the stand, NOT on the back, NOT on the top. It stays open and visible until the connector fills it, and it never disappears, closes over or moves.
THE CONNECTOR - a white plastic USB-C plug on a white cable, held between the right thumb and forefinger. Its dark flat metal tongue points LEFT, straight at THE PORT, with a gap of roughly two centimetres between the tip and the socket at 0.0s. The plug and THE PORT are already lined up on the same horizontal axis - all that is missing is the push.
COUNT LOCK: exactly two hands for the whole clip.

DOME COLOUR LOCK - THE MOST IMPORTANT FIX FOR THIS CLIP: the projector's dome body and its stand stay MATTE WHITE plastic in every single frame, exactly as in the start image, before and after the plug goes in. The dome never turns red, pink, orange or any colour, never glows from inside, never becomes translucent and never lights up as a whole - not even half of it. The red light appears in exactly two small places only: (1) a thin, crisp red line in the narrow seam between the dome and the stand, and (2) tiny separate red pinpoints on the BLACK perforated mesh disc on top. Everywhere else the white plastic keeps its white colour and its normal kitchen-light shading; at most a very faint red tint touches the counter right at the foot of the stand.

[5] LOCATION - hold every detail visible in the start image: a honed dark-grey soapstone countertop with faint white veining and a straight eased edge, honed matte rather than glossy; behind it knotty pine inset cabinets with black wrought-iron latch pulls, hand-painted blue-and-white Delft-style backsplash tiles, dark spruce ceiling beams, a forest-green enamel range set into the tall cabinet run on the right, clean warm under-cabinet lights, evergreen garland with red berries and tiny warm fairy lights across the upper cabinets, a small Christmas tree with red and white gingham ornaments and red ribbon in the far corner. Preserve the same left/right placement and framing. The kitchen remains crisp and in focus. Do not remove the countertop or replace the kitchen.

[6] FIRST FRAME - exactly the start image: THE PROJECTOR unlit on the counter, THE LEFT HAND on the dome, THE RIGHT HAND holding the white cable connector beside the base.

[7] TIMELINE
0.0-1.2s - camera completely locked. THE RIGHT HAND drives THE CONNECTOR straight to the LEFT along its own axis and PLUGS IT IN. The two-centimetre gap closes, the dark metal tongue enters THE PORT and disappears completely inside the dome, and the white plastic shoulder of the plug comes to rest flush against the white rim with no gap left between plug and dome. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT EVENT IN THE CLIP: the plug must visibly travel, enter the hole, and stay in it. The hand pushes once, firmly and in one go - it does not hover, hesitate, drift, retreat, tap the outside of the dome, slide along the rim, or hold the plug in mid-air. The white cable trails away to the right across the soapstone and stays slack. THE LEFT HAND stays still on the dome.
1.2-2.0s - THE CONNECTOR is now fully seated and stays seated for the rest of the clip; it never comes back out. A thin RED light ring ignites in the seam between the white dome and the white stand base and glows steadily.
2.0-3.0s - the BLACK perforated mesh disc on top of the dome fills with a dense field of small RED points of light, like a red starfield, brightening from the centre outward across the black disc. The white dome body stays white; only a very faint red tint touches the counter right at the foot of the stand.
3.0-4.0s - the RED light settles and holds at full brightness; the small red points shimmer very slightly. THE RIGHT HAND lets go of the seated plug - which stays in THE PORT - and relaxes onto the counter beside the base. Nothing else moves.

[9] CAMERA AND OPTICS - one absolutely locked-off shot, vertical 9:16, normal wide-angle phone lens, close on the product over the counter. FREEZE MEANS FREEZE: no drift, no wobble, no micro-motion, no push-in, no handheld shake, no reframe, no zoom, no cut. Normal wide-angle only - no fisheye, no barrel distortion.

[10] LIGHTING - warm white under-cabinet kitchen light for the whole clip; the only lighting change is the RED light emitted by THE PROJECTOR itself from 1.0s onward. The red light is a local glow on the product and the soapstone immediately around it - it does not repaint the whole kitchen.

[11] PHYSICS - THE PROJECTOR is a rigid object bolted to the spot; it does not shift, rock, rotate or lift when the cable is pushed in. The cable is flexible and bends slightly as it seats.

[12] AUDIO - natural room sound only: a small plastic click as the connector seats. No music, no speech, no score.

[13] POSITIVE LOCKS - THE CONNECTOR ends the clip FULLY INSERTED into THE PORT, its metal tongue hidden inside the dome and its white shoulder flush against the white rim; anyone watching can see the plug go into the hole. The light is RED and only RED. The top face of THE PROJECTOR is BLACK and the red starfield appears ON that black disc. The countertop and the kitchen behind it are visible in every single frame. Exactly two hands. The camera never moves.
BANNED: the white dome turning red, pink or glowing as a whole or in part; a red wash over the product; a plug that stops short of the socket; a plug that never moves; a plug pressed against the outside of the dome or the stand instead of entering the socket; a plug pushed into the stand, the base tray, the back or the top instead of the rim socket; a plug that goes in and then comes back out; a plug left hovering in mid-air at the end; a hand that only holds or fiddles with the cable; THE PORT closing over, healing, vanishing or moving to another part of the product; a second socket appearing; blue light, white light, green light, amber light, multicoloured or rainbow light; a beam projected onto the ceiling or the walls; the product moving, lifting or rotating; the camera moving in any way; an all-white top face; the countertop or the kitchen disappearing; a third hand; a cut; subtitles; on-screen text; music.

PRODUCT SCALE LOCK: preserve the exact large full-size projector and its size relative to the adult hands in the supplied start frame. Never shrink it to a miniature; the black perforated mesh top, rigid white body and separate four-foot stand keep their proportions.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo, the same dim hallway, the same antique brass round doorknob in the same place, the same small pine wreath with the red velvet bow hung on the door, the same oak floorboards, the same woman's forearm entering from the lower right with the oatmeal-and-red Nordic-patterned wool sleeve and no jewellery, with very fair skin with a few light freckles, slender adult woman's fingers and short natural nails, her hand closed around the knob, the same camera position and camera height, the same warm low-key evening light.

det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, framing, scale and poses. Wholesome family Christmas scene. @Image 1 owns composition geometry only. @Image 2 owns the dense saturated photographic projection look; change the architecture and children to the descriptions below. Both reference images are generated stills, not photographs of a documented real house.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing of a whole tall room seen from a doorway, the same natural low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two children - a boy standing TURNED AROUND FACING THE CAMERA, front-on, his face fully visible and lit by the coloured light, looking towards the lens with a delighted open-mouthed smile, arms slightly out in wonder, and a girl beside him seen from behind, still looking up at the projected wall.

The boy is of about eight with fair skin, rosy cheeks and straight light-brown hair with a short fringe; the girl is of about six with fair skin and long honey-blonde hair in two plaits tied with red ribbons. Both children are fully dressed for winter in cream brushed-cotton Christmas pyjama sets printed with little red Alpine chalets and green fir trees, with matching loose pyjama trousers and red wool socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene.

CHANGE 1 - THE ROOM. Build a structurally believable room: a spacious double-height Alpine chalet Christmas great room with a high A-FRAME CEILING: two steep planes of honey-toned knotty larch boards rising to a sharp central ridge, crossed by three heavy dark-stained spruce collar ties with carved brackets. Whitewashed lime-plaster walls above knotty larch wainscoting. A tall chimney breast of rough grey fieldstone stands on the back wall with a thick larch beam mantel; a wall of tall windows with chunky larch frames and mullions occupies the left wall and a wide larch doorway with carved brackets sits on the right. Wide knotty larch floorboards, a large cream boucle sectional sofa draped with a sheepskin, a round red wool-felt ottoman and a soft red-and-cream Nordic-pattern wool rug. Seen from the doorway; the new heavy honey-toned knotty-larch Alpine chalet plank door with a carved heart cut-out, black iron studs, a satin oil finish and a chunky larch surrounding casing is open out of frame.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. A real Christmas tree with warm gold lights, red, white and natural-wood ornaments with straw stars, tinsel and wrapped gifts stands beside the fireplace. Evergreen garland with holly berries covers the mantel, with three red-and-cream Nordic knitted stockings below. The projection is the main illumination.

CHANGE 2 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every architectural plane and seam, every beam or cove, and the entire chimney breast all the way to the ceiling. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, a SNOWY ALPINE CHRISTMAS VILLAGE: rows of carved wooden chalets with deep snowy roofs, glowing windows and a tall, thick column of white smoke rising from every chimney, a festive Christmas market with glowing wooden stalls, a little red cog train climbing past the chalets, skiers and sledgers gliding down the snowy slopes, and tall snow-laden fir trees and snow-capped mountain peaks rising behind them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with big soft snowflakes drifting down. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars, shooting stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, cranberry red and alpine blue dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The two steep ceiling planes and their sharp central ridge remain clearly three-dimensional, meeting at a crisp ridge line. The sleigh and the ceiling picture fold at the ridge and are foreshortened along each slope, running straight across the faces of the three spruce collar ties and their carved brackets, before continuing onto the walls. The tall fieldstone chimney breast receives a continuous picture with clear folds at its projecting corners. The knotty larch wainscoting, the larch window frames and mullions and the carved larch doorway carry the projection straight across their faces, with thin shadow breaks only at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. THE WOODEN FRAMES CARRY THE PICTURE TOO: the painted wooden window frames, sashes and glazing bars, the door and doorway casings, the skirting boards, the mantel and every other piece of wooden trim the beam crosses are covered by the same continuous projected imagery as the wall beside them - never left as bare white unlit outlines - with only a thin real shadow line at each edge. THIS IS THE KEY CORRECTION FOR THIS SET, AND THE PREVIOUS ATTEMPT FAILED IT: every exposed wooden beam, rafter, truss, purlin, window frame, mullion, muntin, glazing bar, door frame and casing is COVERED by the projection. Treat the projected image as one continuous sheet of coloured light that ignores the wood: where a beam crosses the ceiling, the stars, snowflakes, the sleigh, the reindeer and the golden trail continue straight over the beam's underside and both of its sides, cut into strips by its edges and shifted slightly by its depth, in the same full colour and brightness as the ceiling around it; where a window frame, mullion or door casing crosses the wall, the garlands, lanterns and scenery continue straight over its face in the same full colour as the wall beside it. Seen from the camera, the wooden members are camouflaged inside the picture - their shape reads only from thin shadow lines and a slight shift of the image along their edges, never from their own bare wood colour. NOT ONE beam, rafter, frame, mullion or casing appears as a plain bare wooden stripe, a dark silhouette or an unlit outline cutting through the picture. Only the window GLASS stays the dark night outside; the frames around the glass carry the picture. NO PART OF THE CEILING IS LEFT UNCOVERED: every plane of the ceiling is filled edge to edge - every panel between the beams, the strip along the ridge, and above all the outer strips beyond the outermost beams, high in the top-left and top-right corners of the frame where the ceiling meets the side walls, all carry the same dense projected night sky, stars and snowflakes. Not a single bare, unlit, plain wood or white patch remains anywhere on the ceiling. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 3 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The wide knotty larch floorboards, the soft red-and-cream Nordic-pattern wool rug, the cream boucle sectional sofa, the round red wool-felt ottoman, the tree and the gifts carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children's faces and their cotton pyjamas catch that spill so both faces read clearly.

CHANGE 4 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no side table, no stool, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain floor and the edge of the rug.

NATURAL, LESS CINEMATIC LOOK - one small notch more natural than a polished film still: this is a candid photo a parent snapped on an iPhone at home, not a movie frame, a poster, a painting or an advert. True-to-life colour and contrast exactly as they come straight out of the phone camera: no colour grading, no teal-and-orange grade, no vignette, no dramatic spotlighting, no heightened fantasy glow on the children, and no storybook-illustration or oil-painting finish on the projection. The projection is still dense, bright and colourful, but its colour sits a touch closer to real life - rich, not neon - and it reads as the real light of a home Christmas projector falling on real walls: the plaster texture and wood grain show faintly through it, and the shadows keep a little more ordinary room detail, with the furniture, rug and floor clearly readable in the soft spill.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the fine cotton weave of the pyjamas, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the drywall, the grain of the knotty larch boards and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

@Image 3 is a wood-coverage example only: it shows the projection lying straight across exposed wooden trusses and braces. Copy only that coverage of the wood; do not copy its room, architecture, children, colours or projected scenes.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.
