det.label: Image prompt · v30_c05_r1.png
det.text:
Recreate @Image 1's camera, framing, scale and poses. Wholesome family Christmas scene. @Image 1 owns composition geometry only. @Image 2 owns the dense saturated photographic projection look; change the architecture and children to the descriptions below. Both reference images are generated stills, not photographs of a documented real house.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing of a whole tall room seen from a doorway, the same natural low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two children - a boy standing TURNED AROUND FACING THE CAMERA, front-on, his face fully visible and lit by the coloured light, looking towards the lens with a delighted open-mouthed smile, arms slightly out in wonder, and a girl beside him seen from behind, still looking up at the projected wall.

The boy is of about five with pale skin and a mop of white-blond curls; the girl is of about seven with fair skin, light freckles and shoulder-length auburn hair held back with a green velvet headband. Both children are fully dressed for winter in black-and-white buffalo-check flannel Christmas pyjama sets with red cuff trim, with matching loose pyjama trousers and grey wool socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene.

CHANGE 1 - THE ROOM. Build a structurally believable room: a spacious double-height modern farmhouse Christmas great room with a high CATHEDRAL CEILING of white shiplap boards rising to a crisp central ridge, crossed by four chunky reclaimed-oak scissor trusses with black steel plates. White shiplap walls. A tall chimney breast of whitewashed brick stands on the back wall with a reclaimed-oak beam mantel; a wall of tall black steel-framed windows with slim black mullions occupies the left wall and a wide black steel-framed glass doorway sits on the right. Wide white-oak floorboards, a large cream linen sectional sofa, a round cognac leather ottoman and a soft black-and-cream striped wool rug. Seen from the doorway; the new matte black painted modern farmhouse door with four tall flat panels, a satin finish and a crisp white-painted surrounding casing is open out of frame.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. A real Christmas tree with warm gold lights, black, silver and white glass baubles, tinsel and wrapped gifts stands beside the fireplace. Evergreen garland with holly berries covers the mantel, with three black-and-white buffalo-check stockings below. The projection is the main illumination.

CHANGE 2 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every architectural plane and seam, every beam or cove, and the entire chimney breast all the way to the ceiling. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, SANTA'S SNOWY NORTH POLE TOY VILLAGE: rows of little red-and-white gingerbread-trimmed workshop cottages with glowing windows and a tall, thick column of white smoke rising from every chimney, busy elves carrying stacks of presents, a candy-striped toy train puffing white steam past piles of wrapped gifts, reindeer in a snowy stable yard, and tall snow-laden fir trees rising between them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with big soft snowflakes drifting down. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars, shooting stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, candy red and emerald green dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The two sloping shiplap planes and their central ridge remain clearly three-dimensional, meeting at a crisp ridge line. The sleigh and the ceiling picture fold at the ridge and are foreshortened along each slope, running straight across the faces of the four reclaimed-oak scissor trusses, before continuing onto the walls. The tall whitewashed brick chimney breast receives a continuous picture with clear folds at its projecting corners. The white shiplap boards, the black steel window frames and mullions and the glass doorway frame carry the projection straight across their faces, with thin shadow breaks only at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. THE WOODEN FRAMES CARRY THE PICTURE TOO: the painted wooden window frames, sashes and glazing bars, the door and doorway casings, the skirting boards, the mantel and every other piece of wooden trim the beam crosses are covered by the same continuous projected imagery as the wall beside them - never left as bare white unlit outlines - with only a thin real shadow line at each edge. THIS IS THE KEY CORRECTION FOR THIS SET, AND THE PREVIOUS ATTEMPT FAILED IT: every exposed wooden beam, rafter, truss, purlin, window frame, mullion, muntin, glazing bar, door frame and casing is COVERED by the projection. Treat the projected image as one continuous sheet of coloured light that ignores the wood: where a beam crosses the ceiling, the stars, snowflakes, the sleigh, the reindeer and the golden trail continue straight over the beam's underside and both of its sides, cut into strips by its edges and shifted slightly by its depth, in the same full colour and brightness as the ceiling around it; where a window frame, mullion or door casing crosses the wall, the garlands, lanterns and scenery continue straight over its face in the same full colour as the wall beside it. Seen from the camera, the wooden members are camouflaged inside the picture - their shape reads only from thin shadow lines and a slight shift of the image along their edges, never from their own bare wood colour. NOT ONE beam, rafter, frame, mullion or casing appears as a plain bare wooden stripe, a dark silhouette or an unlit outline cutting through the picture. Only the window GLASS stays the dark night outside; the frames around the glass carry the picture. NO PART OF THE CEILING IS LEFT UNCOVERED: every plane of the ceiling is filled edge to edge - every panel between the beams, the strip along the ridge, and above all the outer strips beyond the outermost beams, high in the top-left and top-right corners of the frame where the ceiling meets the side walls, all carry the same dense projected night sky, stars and snowflakes. Not a single bare, unlit, plain wood or white patch remains anywhere on the ceiling. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 3 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The wide white-oak floorboards, the soft black-and-cream striped wool rug, the cream linen sectional sofa, the round cognac leather ottoman, the tree and the gifts carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children's faces and their cotton pyjamas catch that spill so both faces read clearly.

CHANGE 4 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no side table, no stool, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain floor and the edge of the rug.

NATURAL, LESS CINEMATIC LOOK - one small notch more natural than a polished film still: this is a candid photo a parent snapped on an iPhone at home, not a movie frame, a poster, a painting or an advert. True-to-life colour and contrast exactly as they come straight out of the phone camera: no colour grading, no teal-and-orange grade, no vignette, no dramatic spotlighting, no heightened fantasy glow on the children, and no storybook-illustration or oil-painting finish on the projection. The projection is still dense, bright and colourful, but its colour sits a touch closer to real life - rich, not neon - and it reads as the real light of a home Christmas projector falling on real walls: the plaster texture and wood grain show faintly through it, and the shadows keep a little more ordinary room detail, with the furniture, rug and floor clearly readable in the soft spill.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the fine cotton weave of the pyjamas, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the drywall, the grooves of the white shiplap and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

@Image 3 is a wood-coverage example only: it shows the projection lying straight across exposed wooden trusses and braces. Copy only that coverage of the wood; do not copy its room, architecture, children, colours or projected scenes.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

det.text:
ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE - ABSOLUTE RULE: this 5-second clip is a single uninterrupted real-time shot from the start image to the last frame. No cut, no jump cut, no hidden edit, no time skip, no dissolve, no zoom, no reframe. Everything in it happens continuously, frame to frame.

PROJECTED ANIMATION - THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS CLIP, AND IT MUST BE BUSY AND ALIVE. The Christmas picture on the walls and the shiplap cathedral ceiling is a hand-drawn ANIMATED CHRISTMAS CARTOON playing at full speed, like a TV screen showing a lively animated Christmas movie - never a still picture, never a calm picture. Only the projected picture is animated; the room and the children stay real photographic phone footage. AT EVERY MOMENT AT LEAST TWELVE DIFFERENT DRAWN THINGS ARE VISIBLY MOVING AT THE SAME TIME, spread across the left wall, the back wall, the right wall and the ceiling, each one with big, bold, easy-to-read motion that a viewer notices on a phone screen at a glance, independent of the camera. Only the drawn buildings, trees and the moon stay put; everything else travels, turns, rises, flutters or bursts. EVERY ANIMAL, BIRD, PERSON AND VEHICLE IN THE PICTURE IS A FLAT HAND-DRAWN CARTOON MADE OF PROJECTED LIGHT lying on the wall or ceiling surface - never a real, photographic, furry or three-dimensional creature. Nothing ever leaves the wall, stands out from it or flies into the room; every drawn thing moves only inside the flat projected picture.
- CHIMNEY SMOKE - A HARD REQUIREMENT, CHECKED FIRST: look at the start image - the rows of little red-and-white gingerbread-trimmed workshop cottages with glowing windows along the LEFT wall, the RIGHT wall and around the back wall. Every cottage roof carries a chimney, and from EACH chimney a thick, bright WHITE column of smoke is already pouring out in the very first frame: big round puffs push out one after another, swell, curl and sway, and climb up the wall about one roof-height every second, stretching into long wavy trails that drift toward the ceiling before fading. At every moment at least SIX separate, wide, bright white smoke columns are visibly rising - three or more on each side wall - as obvious as steam from a boiling kettle against the dark night sky. A cottage without rising smoke makes the clip wrong.
- SANTA'S SLEIGH AND EIGHT REINDEER: the WHOLE TEAM TRAVELS across the ceiling in one smooth sweeping arc, covering about one quarter of the ceiling's width every second, so it is in a clearly different place every second - never parked with only its legs moving. The reindeer gallop, heads bob, the sleigh rocks and dips, Santa waves, and the long golden trail streams and curls behind it, shedding glittering sparks.
- THE TOY TRAIN: the candy-striped toy train chugs steadily along its track past the piles of gifts, puffing round white steam clouds, travelling about one cottage-width every second.
- THE ELVES: busy little drawn elves hurry between the cottages carrying stacks of presents, one pushes a sledge of gifts, another waves.
- THE REINDEER YARD: the drawn reindeer in the stable yard prance, toss their antlers and trot in a circle.
- THE COTTAGES: the workshop windows flicker warmly on and off; wreaths on the doors sway; gift piles sparkle.
- SHOOTING STARS AND FIREWORKS: a new shooting star streaks across the ceiling about every second, leaving a glittering tail; small round golden and red fireworks burst in the night sky above the toy village one after another, open into sparkles and fade.
- LIGHTS: the strings of golden lights along the upper walls twinkle in running chase patterns that race along the garlands; the red velvet bows sway; the stars twinkle and the silver moon glows.
- DRAWN SNOW, FLAT ON THE WALLS ONLY: small flat cartoon snowflakes, drawn like the rest of the picture, slide slowly down the painted night sky on the walls and the ceiling, lying flat on the surface and bending round the corners with the picture - part of the projected drawing, like snow painted on wallpaper, never coming off the wall. THE AIR OF THE ROOM STAYS COMPLETELY CLEAR: no snowflakes, sparkles, glitter, dust or particles float or fall anywhere in the room - not in front of the children, the sofa, the fireplace, the Christmas tree or the camera, and not in the space between the camera and the walls.
PER-SECOND ANIMATION TRACK (5 s):
0-1s: through the very first gap of the door the sleigh is already flying, the toy train is chugging, the elves are hurrying with presents, fireworks are bursting and six thick white smoke columns are already rising from the cottage chimneys.
1-2s: the sleigh travels a quarter of the ceiling; the toy train chugs past the gift piles puffing steam; the elves carry presents between the cottages; a shooting star streaks over; the smoke columns keep climbing the walls.
2-3s: the sleigh flies on; two fireworks burst over the village; the reindeer prance in the yard; the lights chase along the garlands; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
3-4s: the sleigh keeps flying; an elf pushes a sledge of gifts; the drawn snow keeps sliding down the painted sky on the walls; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
4-5s: everything still moving at full pace in the last frame - sleigh flying, smoke pouring from every chimney, toy train chugging, elves hurrying, fireworks bursting, the drawn snow sliding down the walls, and the air of the room still completely clear.
All of this is flat projected light lying on the real shiplap boards, the reclaimed-oak scissor trusses, the whitewashed brick chimney breast and the black steel window frames: it bends with the surfaces, never floats into the room, and nothing is projected on the floor, furniture or children.

CHILDREN - SPELLBOUND BY THE CEILING AND ALWAYS MOVING. EXACTLY TWO CHILDREN exist in this clip - THE BOY and THE GIRL described below - and nobody else ever appears: no third child, no extra kids in the background, on the sofa or in the doorway, no adult. The room reference photo is EMPTY, so there is no pose or spot to copy. When the first gap of the door opens, both children are ALREADY in the middle and far side of the room, at least three metres from the door - never standing in or near the doorway, never lined up facing the camera, never side by side. They were already watching the projection before the door opened and they are completely amazed by it: mouths wide open, eyebrows raised, gasping and laughing, eyes glued to the flying sleigh on the ceiling. They keep moving the whole time and follow the sleigh with their eyes, arms and feet. Per second:
0-1s: in the very first gap THE BOY is already walking slowly backwards across the rug, head tipped far back, one arm stretched straight up pointing at Santa's flying sleigh; THE GIRL, a few steps away from him, is up on tiptoe with both hands pressed to her cheeks, mouth open, staring straight up.
1-2s: THE BOY keeps stepping backwards and turns his body to follow the sleigh as it flies overhead, his pointing arm tracking it across the ceiling; THE GIRL runs three quick little steps across the rug in the same direction the sleigh is flying, one hand reaching up toward it.
2-3s: THE BOY looks over at THE GIRL, points up again and shouts with excitement, then looks straight back up; THE GIRL spins round once on the rug with her arms out and her face turned up to the ceiling, laughing.
3-4s: THE GIRL does two small excited bunny-hops on the spot, landing back on the rug at real speed, pointing up at the candy-striped toy train puffing steam; THE BOY walks sideways past the ottoman with his head still tipped back, following the sleigh.
4-5s: both are still moving in the last frame - THE BOY still stepping and pointing up, THE GIRL trotting toward the Christmas tree while gazing up - never frozen.
They never stand still, never pose, never face the camera and never wait. Their feet stay on the floor: they never climb, jump onto or jump over the sofa, the ottoman or any furniture. Both stay in view: neither ducks behind furniture and pops up somewhere else. Real speed, real weight, grounded feet - no sliding, floating, slow motion or running in place. This child action never alters the camera movement.

CAMERA CONTINUITY: the entire five seconds are ONE slow, uninterrupted forward-and-upward glide. Forward travel and upward aim are coupled as one motion, already underway together in frame zero. Keep the same gentle pace and the same forward-to-upward ratio for every frame, including while the door opens and while crossing its sill. Travel only about 0.8 metres forward over the entire shot, with an even upward tilt of about 18 degrees over those same five seconds. The wreath, door-panel edges and later the back-wall details drift smoothly downward in the frame from the beginning while perspective advances very gently. There is no forward-only phase and no later tilt-only phase. Do not accelerate the beginning, hurry through the door, ease in, ease out, steepen the tilt, speed-ramp or catch up to an end composition. The final frame can remain near the threshold with the back wall, furniture and ceiling visible. The door opens naturally during the same slow glide; its opening is not a camera cue.

DIRECT ROOM ENTRY: the closed door in the start image is fitted directly into the great room's entrance wall and its far face opens straight into the furnished Christmas room shown in the room reference photo. ONE door, ONE thin normal threshold about 15 cm deep. The very first gap reveals the room itself, the already-moving children and the already-playing projection, close behind this door. No hall, foyer, vestibule, passage, empty approach space, second doorway or arch between this door and the room. The side doorway on the reference room's right wall is a lateral feature only and never lies ahead of the camera.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home at Christmas.

TASK AND ASSETS: image-to-video, one continuous handheld phone POV take, vertical 9:16. The START IMAGE is frame 0.0s: a matte black painted modern farmhouse door with four tall flat panels, a satin finish and a crisp white-painted surrounding casing fully closed with a wreath, a woman's hand with pale porcelain skin with pink undertones and a dusty-rose chunky rib-knit wool sleeve on the brass knob. The ROOM REFERENCE IMAGE (attached as an image reference) controls only the room's architecture, furniture, colours and projected artwork; it contains no people and it is not an end frame, camera target or transition destination - never dissolve, cut, morph or snap into its composition. The two children come only from this text.

CONTINUOUS ACTION: during approximately the first 1.5 seconds the hand turns the knob and opens the door with a smooth, ordinary, unhurried push. The room behind it is already running: the projection is already playing and both children are already moving - the widening gap only uncovers more of a scene that was already happening. Nothing ignites or spreads as the door opens, and the door edge and frame stay plain wood - no glowing strip, no coloured fringe, no bright seam in the gap. The shot ends during the same gentle glide with the back wall, furniture and ceiling still visible.

CAMERA - eye height, normal wide-angle phone lens, a steady natural phone glide as described. No zoom, orbit, fisheye, lens warping, stop, second move or cut. The camera is the person's eyes; no phone, screen or device in frame. Hold the sharpness and exposure of the start image - crisp phone footage, in focus from the first frame to the last.

AUDIO - dry documentary sound only: the handle, the door swinging, the children gasping, laughing and calling out in delight, their footsteps on the floor, quiet room tone. (no BGM). No subtitles.

ROOM AND IDENTITY - a spacious double-height modern farmhouse Christmas great room with a high CATHEDRAL CEILING of white shiplap boards rising to a crisp central ridge, crossed by four chunky reclaimed-oak scissor trusses with black steel plates. White shiplap walls. A tall chimney breast of whitewashed brick stands on the back wall with a reclaimed-oak beam mantel; a wall of tall black steel-framed windows with slim black mullions occupies the left wall and a wide black steel-framed glass doorway sits on the right. Wide white-oak floorboards, a large cream linen sectional sofa, a round cognac leather ottoman and a soft black-and-cream striped wool rug.
THE BOY - a boy of about five with pale skin and a mop of white-blond curls. THE GIRL - a girl of about seven with fair skin, light freckles and shoulder-length auburn hair held back with a green velvet headband. Both fully dressed in black-and-white buffalo-check flannel Christmas pyjama sets with red cuff trim, with matching loose pyjama trousers and grey wool socks.

PROJECTED SCENE CONTENT - LOW ALONG THE WALLS, SANTA'S SNOWY NORTH POLE TOY VILLAGE: rows of little red-and-white gingerbread-trimmed workshop cottages with glowing windows and a tall, thick column of white smoke rising from every chimney, busy elves carrying stacks of presents, a candy-striped toy train puffing white steam past piles of wrapped gifts, reindeer in a snowy stable yard, and tall snow-laden fir trees rising between them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with small flat drawn snowflakes sliding down the painted sky. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars, shooting stars and small flat drawn snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. BANNED - a third child or any extra people appearing at any moment; an adult; a child standing still, frozen, posed or waiting at any moment; the children standing in or next to the doorway when it opens; the children side by side or facing the camera; a child climbing onto or jumping on or over furniture; a child disappearing behind furniture and reappearing elsewhere; slow motion or floaty movement; a camera that moves, stops and moves again; a zoom; a cut; a glow along the door edge; light that grows or fills the room as the door opens; the projector unit visible; blur; music; subtitles.

A different child from @Image 1: a boy of about five with pale skin and a mop of white-blond curls, fully dressed for winter in a black-and-white buffalo-check flannel Christmas pyjama set with red cuff trim, with matching loose pyjama trousers and grey wool socks. He is standing up on top of the bed, knees bent and both arms raised out to his sides, caught mid-bounce, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling, laughing. Clearly standing on top of the bed, not sitting on its edge.

Build a structurally believable room: a bright-proportioned modern farmhouse bedroom with a high COFFERED BOX-BEAM CEILING: a flat white shiplap ceiling divided into a large grid of deep squares by reclaimed-oak box beams. A black iron bed with a wide upholstered oatmeal linen headboard is centred on the flat white shiplap back wall between two tall black steel-framed windows, white board-and-batten panelling behind the bed, white bedding with a black-and-white buffalo-check throw, reclaimed-oak bedside tables, wide white-oak floorboards and a soft cream wool rug. The bed stays in the same place in the frame, leaving the room's ceiling geometry clearly visible.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. The bed keeps the bedding described above, with pillows and a knitted stocking. A small real Christmas tree with gold lights and black, silver and white ornaments stands by the window.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every roof plane and seam, wall above the headboard, window jambs and lintels. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, SANTA'S SNOWY NORTH POLE TOY VILLAGE: rows of little red-and-white gingerbread-trimmed workshop cottages with glowing windows and a tall, thick column of white smoke rising from every chimney, busy elves carrying stacks of presents, a candy-striped toy train puffing white steam past piles of wrapped gifts, reindeer in a snowy stable yard, and tall snow-laden fir trees rising between them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with big soft snowflakes drifting down. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars, shooting stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, candy red and emerald green dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The coffered ceiling and its box beams remain clearly three-dimensional, meeting the walls at crisp lines. The sleigh and the ceiling picture run straight across the flat coffers and over the faces and undersides of the reclaimed-oak box beams, foreshortened across the ceiling, before continuing down the walls. The flat wall, the board-and-batten panelling, the black steel window frames and the oatmeal headboard carry properly foreshortened portions of the same continuous projection across their faces. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. THE WOODEN FRAMES CARRY THE PICTURE TOO: the painted wooden window frames, sashes and glazing bars, the door and doorway casings, the skirting boards, the mantel and every other piece of wooden trim the beam crosses are covered by the same continuous projected imagery as the wall beside them - never left as bare white unlit outlines - with only a thin real shadow line at each edge. THIS IS THE KEY CORRECTION FOR THIS SET, AND THE PREVIOUS ATTEMPT FAILED IT: every exposed wooden beam, rafter, truss, purlin, window frame, mullion, muntin, glazing bar, door frame and casing is COVERED by the projection. Treat the projected image as one continuous sheet of coloured light that ignores the wood: where a beam crosses the ceiling, the stars, snowflakes, the sleigh, the reindeer and the golden trail continue straight over the beam's underside and both of its sides, cut into strips by its edges and shifted slightly by its depth, in the same full colour and brightness as the ceiling around it; where a window frame, mullion or door casing crosses the wall, the garlands, lanterns and scenery continue straight over its face in the same full colour as the wall beside it. Seen from the camera, the wooden members are camouflaged inside the picture - their shape reads only from thin shadow lines and a slight shift of the image along their edges, never from their own bare wood colour. NOT ONE beam, rafter, frame, mullion or casing appears as a plain bare wooden stripe, a dark silhouette or an unlit outline cutting through the picture. Only the window GLASS stays the dark night outside; the frames around the glass carry the picture. NO PART OF THE CEILING IS LEFT UNCOVERED: every plane of the ceiling is filled edge to edge - every panel between the beams, the strip along the ridge, and above all the outer strips beyond the outermost beams, high in the top-left and top-right corners of the frame where the ceiling meets the side walls, all carry the same dense projected night sky, stars and snowflakes. Not a single bare, unlit, plain wood or white patch remains anywhere on the ceiling. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The wide white-oak floorboards, the soft cream wool rug, the bed and its covers, the bench at its foot and the little Christmas tree carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. The boy's face and his cotton pyjama top catch that spill so his face reads clearly.

CHANGE 5 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no stool, no side table, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain wall and floor.

NATURAL, LESS CINEMATIC LOOK - one small notch more natural than a polished film still: this is a candid photo a parent snapped on an iPhone at home, not a movie frame, a poster, a painting or an advert. True-to-life colour and contrast exactly as they come straight out of the phone camera: no colour grading, no teal-and-orange grade, no vignette, no dramatic spotlighting, no heightened fantasy glow on the children, and no storybook-illustration or oil-painting finish on the projection. The projection is still dense, bright and colourful, but its colour sits a touch closer to real life - rich, not neon - and it reads as the real light of a home Christmas projector falling on real walls: the plaster texture and wood grain show faintly through it, and the shadows keep a little more ordinary room detail, with the furniture, rug and floor clearly readable in the soft spill.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the fine cotton weave of the pyjamas, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the plaster, the crisp architectural edges of the ceiling and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

@Image 3 is a wood-coverage example only: it shows the projection lying straight across exposed wooden trusses and braces. Copy only that coverage of the wood; do not copy its room, architecture, children, colours or projected scenes.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE - ABSOLUTE RULE: this 5-second clip is a single uninterrupted real-time shot from the start image to the last frame. No cut, no jump cut, no hidden edit, no time skip, no dissolve, no zoom, no reframe. Everything in it happens continuously, frame to frame.

OPENING STATE - frame 0.0s is EXACTLY the start image: the same framing, the same camera angle and the same view of the ceiling, with the projection already covering every visible part of the walls and the ceiling in full colour. The clip never starts from a higher, wider or different view, never shows any part of the room above the top edge of the start image, and there is no lighting-up, unveiling, growth, wipe or fade-in of the projection.

PROJECTED ANIMATION - THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS CLIP, AND IT MUST BE BUSY AND ALIVE. The Christmas picture on the walls and the coffered box-beam ceiling is a hand-drawn ANIMATED CHRISTMAS CARTOON playing at full speed, like a TV screen showing a lively animated Christmas movie - never a still picture, never a calm picture. Only the projected picture is animated; the room and the children stay real photographic phone footage. AT EVERY MOMENT AT LEAST TWELVE DIFFERENT DRAWN THINGS ARE VISIBLY MOVING AT THE SAME TIME, spread across the left wall, the back wall, the right wall and the ceiling, each one with big, bold, easy-to-read motion that a viewer notices on a phone screen at a glance, independent of the camera. Only the drawn buildings, trees and the moon stay put; everything else travels, turns, rises, flutters or bursts. EVERY ANIMAL, BIRD, PERSON AND VEHICLE IN THE PICTURE IS A FLAT HAND-DRAWN CARTOON MADE OF PROJECTED LIGHT lying on the wall or ceiling surface - never a real, photographic, furry or three-dimensional creature. Nothing ever leaves the wall, stands out from it or flies into the room; every drawn thing moves only inside the flat projected picture.
- CHIMNEY SMOKE - A HARD REQUIREMENT, CHECKED FIRST: look at the start image - the rows of little red-and-white gingerbread-trimmed workshop cottages with glowing windows along the LEFT wall, the RIGHT wall and around the back wall. Every cottage roof carries a chimney, and from EACH chimney a thick, bright WHITE column of smoke is already pouring out in the very first frame: big round puffs push out one after another, swell, curl and sway, and climb up the wall about one roof-height every second, stretching into long wavy trails that drift toward the ceiling before fading. At every moment at least SIX separate, wide, bright white smoke columns are visibly rising - three or more on each side wall - as obvious as steam from a boiling kettle against the dark night sky. A cottage without rising smoke makes the clip wrong.
- SANTA'S SLEIGH AND EIGHT REINDEER: the WHOLE TEAM TRAVELS across the ceiling in one smooth sweeping arc, covering about one quarter of the ceiling's width every second, so it is in a clearly different place every second - never parked with only its legs moving. The reindeer gallop, heads bob, the sleigh rocks and dips, Santa waves, and the long golden trail streams and curls behind it, shedding glittering sparks.
- THE TOY TRAIN: the candy-striped toy train chugs steadily along its track past the piles of gifts, puffing round white steam clouds, travelling about one cottage-width every second.
- THE ELVES: busy little drawn elves hurry between the cottages carrying stacks of presents, one pushes a sledge of gifts, another waves.
- THE REINDEER YARD: the drawn reindeer in the stable yard prance, toss their antlers and trot in a circle.
- THE COTTAGES: the workshop windows flicker warmly on and off; wreaths on the doors sway; gift piles sparkle.
- SHOOTING STARS AND FIREWORKS: a new shooting star streaks across the ceiling about every second, leaving a glittering tail; small round golden and red fireworks burst in the night sky above the toy village one after another, open into sparkles and fade.
- LIGHTS: the strings of golden lights along the upper walls twinkle in running chase patterns that race along the garlands; the red velvet bows sway; the stars twinkle and the silver moon glows.
- SNOWFALL: big projected snowflakes drift and swirl down across the whole picture, about a quarter of the wall height every second, turning as they fall - flat light on the walls and ceiling, never real snow in the room.
PER-SECOND ANIMATION TRACK (5 s):
0-1s: from the very first frame the sleigh is flying, the toy train is chugging, the elves are hurrying with presents, fireworks are bursting and six thick white smoke columns are already rising from the cottage chimneys.
1-2s: the sleigh travels a quarter of the ceiling; the toy train chugs past the gift piles puffing steam; the elves carry presents between the cottages; a shooting star streaks over; the smoke columns keep climbing the walls.
2-3s: the sleigh flies on; two fireworks burst over the village; the reindeer prance in the yard; the lights chase along the garlands; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
3-4s: the sleigh keeps flying; an elf pushes a sledge of gifts; snow swirls; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
4-5s: everything still moving at full pace in the last frame - sleigh flying, smoke pouring from every chimney, toy train chugging, elves hurrying, fireworks bursting, snow falling.
All of this is flat projected light lying on the real shiplap, the reclaimed-oak box beams, the board-and-batten panelling and the black steel window frames: it bends with the surfaces, never floats into the room, and nothing is projected on the floor, the bed or the boy.

CAMERA - ONE slow, gentle, continuous tilt DOWN from the first frame to the last, like a parent filming - the camera is NEVER static and the movement is clearly visible in every second.
0.0s: the clip starts EXACTLY on the start image framing - never higher, never wider, never showing anything above the top edge of the start image.
0.0-5.0s: the phone tilts DOWN smoothly at an even pace by about 12 degrees in total: the projected ceiling slides up and partly out of the top of the frame while more of the bed, the covers, the bench and the rug come into view at the bottom. Because the camera only ever moves DOWN from the start framing, no ceiling area outside the start image is ever seen. The boy stays fully in frame from head to feet.
One continuous take: no cut, no zoom, no push-in, no pull-back, never a tilt up, never a locked-off static frame.

THE BOY BOUNCES LIKE A REAL CHILD ON A REAL MATTRESS - natural, believable and unexaggerated, at real speed for all five seconds. Small, springy, continuous bounces on the same spot in the middle of the bed: his feet leave the mattress by only about 10 to 20 centimetres, about two bounces per second, the soft mattress visibly sinking under his feet on every landing and pushing him back up. REAL-TIME SPEED, NOT SLOW MOTION: each bounce is quick and snappy, taking only about half a second from push-off to landing under normal gravity, exactly like a real child filmed at normal speed - the footage is never slowed down, never time-stretched and never dreamy. Knees soft, head tipped back, mouth open, laughing up at the ceiling in amazement. While he bounces he throws one arm straight up and points at Santa's sleigh, turning his head to follow it as it flies across the ceiling, then drops the arm and points again. His body keeps exactly the same size, proportions, face and clothing in every frame; he stays in the same spot on the bed. No high leaps, no hanging in the air, no floating, no hopping across the bed, no stiff puppet-like body, no morphing limbs.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, a child at home with his family at Christmas. Crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed, sharp from first frame to last.

ASSET ROLES: the start image is the approved still that controls a bright-proportioned modern farmhouse bedroom with a high COFFERED BOX-BEAM CEILING: a flat white shiplap ceiling divided into a large grid of deep squares by reclaimed-oak box beams. THE BOY - exactly one child, a boy of about five with pale skin and a mop of white-blond curls, fully dressed for winter in a long-sleeved black-and-white buffalo-check flannel Christmas top with red cuff trim, with matching loose lounge trousers and grey wool socks, standing on the bed. No second child, no adult, no pet.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running on the bedroom floor, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the walls and the whole coffered box-beam ceiling. Everything glowing on the plaster and the wood is that one cone landing.
THE PICTURE - the animated scene is the exact Christmas panorama visible in the start image. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, SANTA'S SNOWY NORTH POLE TOY VILLAGE: rows of little red-and-white gingerbread-trimmed workshop cottages with glowing windows and a tall, thick column of white smoke rising from every chimney, busy elves carrying stacks of presents, a candy-striped toy train puffing white steam past piles of wrapped gifts, reindeer in a snowy stable yard, and tall snow-laden fir trees rising between them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with big soft snowflakes drifting down. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars, shooting stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, candy red and emerald green dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room.

AUDIO: room tone, mattress springs compressing on each landing, bedding rustling, a boy laughing and gasping in delight. (no BGM). No subtitles.

DO NOT INCLUDE: a still, frozen or printed-looking projection; a projection that only twinkles; a sleigh parked in one place; chimneys without smoke; a cottage without rising smoke; a toy train or elves that do not travel; snow that does not fall; bare, white or unprojected ceiling or wall; a camera that starts higher, wider or anywhere other than the start image; a static, locked-off camera; a tilt up; a zoom, push-in or pull-back; bare or unprojected ceiling in the first frame; any drawn animal or figure that looks real or leaves the wall; any house or cottage without a thick rising smoke column; fewer than twelve things moving at once; a calm or slow projection; slow-motion or floaty jumping; high exaggerated leaps; the boy changing size or shape; real snow or particles in the air of the room; any music; the projector unit in shot; a second child; an adult; blur; a cut; on-screen text; subtitles.

KEEP IDENTICAL: the same vertical 9:16 iPhone photo look, the same camera position and camera height, the same wide framing that shows a whole enormous double-height room with its full ceiling in shot, the same natural low-key evening light in which the only light in the room is the projection itself, and the same two poses - a girl JUMPING ON THE SOFA, caught mid-air above the cushions, knees bent, arms flung up, hair lifted, the cushion compressed under where she pushed off; and a boy standing on the rug in front of the sofa, seen from behind and slightly to the side, head tipped back looking up at the projected ceiling with his arms out in wonder. Both are small in frame, in scale with the huge room - keeping them small preserves the sense of how big the space is.

CHANGE 1 - THE CHILDREN. The same new children as @Image 2: a girl of about seven with fair skin, light freckles and shoulder-length auburn hair held back with a green velvet headband; a boy of about five with pale skin and a mop of white-blond curls. Both fully dressed in black-and-white buffalo-check flannel Christmas pyjama sets with red cuff trim, with matching loose pyjama trousers and grey wool socks. Wholesome family Christmas scene.

CHANGE 2 - THE ROOM. Build a structurally believable room: a spacious double-height modern farmhouse Christmas family room with a high VAULTED CEILING: two broad sloping planes of white shiplap rising to a crisp central ridge, with a chunky reclaimed-oak ridge beam and reclaimed-oak collar-tie trusses spanning the room. White board-and-batten walls. A tall floor-to-ceiling chimney breast of whitewashed stone stands on the back wall with a reclaimed-oak beam mantel; a full-height wall of black steel-framed windows fills the left wall and a wide black barn door on a steel track sits on the right. Wide white-oak floorboards, a large camel leather sectional sofa, a round chunky-knit cream pouf ottoman and a soft black-and-cream geometric wool rug. A different room from @Image 2 - not the same living room - seen from the middle of the family room with the whole ceiling in shot.

It is night, all house lamps switched off. A real Christmas tree with warm gold lights, black, silver and white glass baubles, tinsel and wrapped gifts stands beside the fireplace. Evergreen garland with holly berries covers the mantel, with three black-and-white buffalo-check stockings below. The projection is the main illumination.

CHANGE 3 - THE PROJECTION. ONE continuous Christmas panorama covers every visible wall and the entire ceiling, including the whole ceiling, every architectural plane and seam, every beam or cove, and the entire chimney breast all the way to the ceiling. No rectangle, no screen, no blank ceiling or wall patch. Architectural occlusion shadows remain real and narrow. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, SANTA'S SNOWY NORTH POLE TOY VILLAGE: rows of little red-and-white gingerbread-trimmed workshop cottages with glowing windows and a tall, thick column of white smoke rising from every chimney, busy elves carrying stacks of presents, a candy-striped toy train puffing white steam past piles of wrapped gifts, reindeer in a snowy stable yard, and tall snow-laden fir trees rising between them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with big soft snowflakes drifting down. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars, shooting stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, candy red and emerald green dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room. AND THE NIGHT SKY BETWEEN THE ELEMENTS IS DEEP AND DARK: everywhere the picture is not occupied by a lit element it is a rich near-black midnight sky of blackened indigo and very dark crimson, NOT white paint, NOT pale drywall and NOT a grey haze. It is that darkness between the elements that makes the bright ones burn.  HOW THE LIGHT SITS ON THE SURFACES, and this has to be exactly right. THE PROJECTION IS DENSE AND ROUGHLY NINETY PERCENT OPAQUE, and it is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame. It lies on the room like an enormous backlit stained-glass window: deep, dense, fully saturated colour at full strength, crimson and ruby and warm gold and emerald at their richest, and it OVERPOWERS the colour of the surface underneath completely.  The material colour is overpowered by the projected colour; only surface texture and physical shadows remain legible through it. It is NOT pale, NOT pastel, NOT milky, NOT hazy, NOT semi-transparent, NOT a faint tint and NOT a washed-out overlay; there is no grey veil over any of it, and no part of the projection is so faint that the bare surface shows through as white.  AND IT WRAPS THE ARCHITECTURE. ONE SINGLE PROJECTOR sitting low in the near corner of the room throws all of this from that one point, so the entire picture keystones away from that origin and every surface takes it at its own angle. This is real projected light crossing a real three-dimensional room, so it obeys every surface it lands on.   The two sloping shiplap planes, the reclaimed-oak ridge beam and the collar-tie trusses remain clearly three-dimensional. The sleigh and the snowflakes fold at the ridge and continue straight across the faces of the ridge beam and the trusses, foreshortened along each slope, before continuing onto the walls. The tall whitewashed stone chimney breast receives a continuous picture with clear folds at its two projecting corners. The black steel window frames, the board-and-batten and the black barn door carry the projection straight across their faces, with thin shadow breaks only at their actual edges. Bright imagery follows the built curves and planes, never a flat picture hovering across the room. All raised trim casts a real hard-edged shadow behind it. THE WOODEN FRAMES CARRY THE PICTURE TOO: the painted wooden window frames, sashes and glazing bars, the door and doorway casings, the skirting boards, the mantel and every other piece of wooden trim the beam crosses are covered by the same continuous projected imagery as the wall beside them - never left as bare white unlit outlines - with only a thin real shadow line at each edge. THIS IS THE KEY CORRECTION FOR THIS SET, AND THE PREVIOUS ATTEMPT FAILED IT: every exposed wooden beam, rafter, truss, purlin, window frame, mullion, muntin, glazing bar, door frame and casing is COVERED by the projection. Treat the projected image as one continuous sheet of coloured light that ignores the wood: where a beam crosses the ceiling, the stars, snowflakes, the sleigh, the reindeer and the golden trail continue straight over the beam's underside and both of its sides, cut into strips by its edges and shifted slightly by its depth, in the same full colour and brightness as the ceiling around it; where a window frame, mullion or door casing crosses the wall, the garlands, lanterns and scenery continue straight over its face in the same full colour as the wall beside it. Seen from the camera, the wooden members are camouflaged inside the picture - their shape reads only from thin shadow lines and a slight shift of the image along their edges, never from their own bare wood colour. NOT ONE beam, rafter, frame, mullion or casing appears as a plain bare wooden stripe, a dark silhouette or an unlit outline cutting through the picture. Only the window GLASS stays the dark night outside; the frames around the glass carry the picture. NO PART OF THE CEILING IS LEFT UNCOVERED: every plane of the ceiling is filled edge to edge - every panel between the beams, the strip along the ridge, and above all the outer strips beyond the outermost beams, high in the top-left and top-right corners of the frame where the ceiling meets the side walls, all carry the same dense projected night sky, stars and snowflakes. Not a single bare, unlit, plain wood or white patch remains anywhere on the ceiling. There is NO falloff anywhere. The picture stays strong, dense and fully coloured right into all four corners of the frame and right up into the corners of the ceiling, with no dim zone, no dark gap, no faded edge and no bare patch at any boundary of the room.  EVERY ELEMENT OF THE PROJECTION IS RAZOR SHARP: every elf, toy, ribbon, nutcracker detail, antler, snowflake, fir needle and window has precise edges. The thousands of points of light are DISCRETE PINPOINTS - tiny, tight, individually separated dots - and not soft round blobs, not fuzzy balls and not smeared streaks. There is NO bloom, NO glow halo, NO lens flare, NO atmospheric haze, NO soft-focus glaze and NO gaussian softness anywhere over the picture, and the brightest cores stay tight and do not bleed into what surrounds them. The whole frame is in focus from the nearest person to the farthest corner of the ceiling: nothing is out of focus, nothing is soft, and there is no depth-of-field blur and no bokeh anywhere in the image.

CHANGE 4 - NOTHING IS PROJECTED ON THE FLOOR. The projected imagery lives on the WALLS and the CEILING only. The wide white-oak floorboards, the soft black-and-cream geometric wool rug, the camel leather sectional sofa, the round chunky-knit cream pouf ottoman and the tree carry NO projected shapes at all - no snowflakes, no stars, no village, no Christmas figures, no gift village, no star, no sleigh, no falling light on them - they are lit only by the soft warm colour spill coming off the walls and sit in gentle shadow. Both children catch that spill so their cotton pyjamas read clearly.

CHANGE 5 - the projector unit must NOT be visible. No projector, no round side table, no glowing device anywhere in frame. The corner it would occupy is plain rug and floor.

NATURAL, LESS CINEMATIC LOOK - one small notch more natural than a polished film still: this is a candid photo a parent snapped on an iPhone at home, not a movie frame, a poster, a painting or an advert. True-to-life colour and contrast exactly as they come straight out of the phone camera: no colour grading, no teal-and-orange grade, no vignette, no dramatic spotlighting, no heightened fantasy glow on the children, and no storybook-illustration or oil-painting finish on the projection. The projection is still dense, bright and colourful, but its colour sits a touch closer to real life - rich, not neon - and it reads as the real light of a home Christmas projector falling on real walls: the plaster texture and wood grain show faintly through it, and the shadows keep a little more ordinary room detail, with the furniture, rug and floor clearly readable in the soft spill.

Vertical 9:16 photo, shot on an iPhone 16 Pro, natural handheld UGC look, extremely high quality, RAZOR SHARP EDGE TO EDGE AND CORNER TO CORNER at full 2K resolution with fine micro-detail legible everywhere - the fine cotton weave of the pyjamas, the grain of the floorboards, the tooth of the drywall, the surface texture of the board-and-batten walls and every individual pinpoint of the projection all crisply resolved - perfect lighting, perfectly exposed, hyper realistic, zero motion blur, zero depth-of-field blur, zero bokeh, zero bloom, zero glow haze, zero soft focus, nothing blurry, nothing smeared and nothing soft or gauzy anywhere in the frame, no CGI look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

@Image 3 is a wood-coverage example only: it shows the projection lying straight across exposed wooden trusses and braces. Copy only that coverage of the wood; do not copy its room, architecture, children, colours or projected scenes.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

det.text:
ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE - ABSOLUTE RULE: this 4-second clip is a single uninterrupted real-time shot from the start image to the last frame. No cut, no jump cut, no hidden edit, no time skip, no dissolve, no zoom, no reframe. Everything in it happens continuously, frame to frame.

OPENING STATE - frame 0.0s preserves the start image's complete, saturated projection on every visible wall, the chimney breast, the whole vaulted shiplap ceiling and every beam. The projector has been running for a long time before filming. Full coverage and brightness stay on for all four seconds while the drawn elements are already moving. There is no lighting-up, unveiling, growth, wipe or fade-in, and the ceiling artwork is never erased and redrawn.

Wholesome family Christmas scene, children at home with their family at Christmas.

SUMMARY: two children in a double-height Christmas family room are amazed by a projected Christmas picture that is PLAYING across the back wall and the entire vaulted shiplap ceiling, thrown there by a projector standing in the room. 4 seconds, one continuous handheld phone take, vertical 9:16.

GLOBAL STYLE: crisp real iPhone footage at night, handheld, real-time speed. Sharp and in focus from the first frame to the last, at least as sharp as the start image. No blur, no haze, no washed-out exposure, no colour shift.

ASSET ROLES: the start image is frame 0.0s and controls a spacious double-height modern farmhouse Christmas family room with a high VAULTED CEILING: two broad sloping planes of white shiplap rising to a crisp central ridge, with a chunky reclaimed-oak ridge beam and reclaimed-oak collar-tie trusses spanning the room. White board-and-batten walls. A tall floor-to-ceiling chimney breast of whitewashed stone stands on the back wall with a reclaimed-oak beam mantel; a full-height wall of black steel-framed windows fills the left wall and a wide black barn door on a steel track sits on the right. Wide white-oak floorboards, a large camel leather sectional sofa, a round chunky-knit cream pouf ottoman and a soft black-and-cream geometric wool rug. Preserve the exact child identity, clothing, furniture, colours, full existing projection and opening framing.

SUBJECTS:
THE GIRL - a girl of about seven with fair skin, light freckles and shoulder-length auburn hair held back with a green velvet headband, on the sofa, caught mid-jump in the start image.
THE BOY - a boy of about five with pale skin and a mop of white-blond curls, on the rug in front of the sofa, back to camera and slightly to the side, looking up at the projected ceiling with his arms out.
Both in black-and-white buffalo-check flannel Christmas pyjama sets with red cuff trim, with matching loose pyjama trousers and grey wool socks. Both stay small in frame, in scale with the huge room. EXACTLY TWO CHILDREN - no third child, no adult, no pet.
THE PROJECTOR - a single Christmas projector switched on and running in the room, out of shot. One lens throws one wide cone of light across the back wall and the whole vaulted shiplap ceiling.
THE PICTURE - the animated scene is the exact Christmas panorama visible in the start image. LOW ALONG THE WALLS, SANTA'S SNOWY NORTH POLE TOY VILLAGE: rows of little red-and-white gingerbread-trimmed workshop cottages with glowing windows and a tall, thick column of white smoke rising from every chimney, busy elves carrying stacks of presents, a candy-striped toy train puffing white steam past piles of wrapped gifts, reindeer in a snowy stable yard, and tall snow-laden fir trees rising between them. Along the upper walls, strings of golden lights, red velvet bows and dense emerald garlands link the rooftops into a continuous Christmas panorama, with big soft snowflakes drifting down. ACROSS THE CEILING, Santa's red sleigh and eight reindeer fly in a wide arc past a big silver full moon, among twinkling golden stars, shooting stars and big glowing snowflakes, a long sparkling golden trail streaming behind them. Unmistakably Christmas Eve, glowing gold, candy red and emerald green dominant with snow-white accents against a near-black midnight sky. One dense continuous panorama of projected light across the architecture, no isolated sticker icons, no carnival, no galaxy, no vortex. No projected shape floats physically in the room.

PROJECTED ANIMATION - THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS CLIP, AND IT MUST BE BUSY AND ALIVE. The Christmas picture on the walls and the vaulted shiplap ceiling is a hand-drawn ANIMATED CHRISTMAS CARTOON playing at full speed, like a TV screen showing a lively animated Christmas movie - never a still picture, never a calm picture. Only the projected picture is animated; the room and the children stay real photographic phone footage. AT EVERY MOMENT AT LEAST TWELVE DIFFERENT DRAWN THINGS ARE VISIBLY MOVING AT THE SAME TIME, spread across the left wall, the back wall, the right wall and the ceiling, each one with big, bold, easy-to-read motion that a viewer notices on a phone screen at a glance, independent of the camera. Only the drawn buildings, trees and the moon stay put; everything else travels, turns, rises, flutters or bursts. EVERY ANIMAL, BIRD, PERSON AND VEHICLE IN THE PICTURE IS A FLAT HAND-DRAWN CARTOON MADE OF PROJECTED LIGHT lying on the wall or ceiling surface - never a real, photographic, furry or three-dimensional creature. Nothing ever leaves the wall, stands out from it or flies into the room; every drawn thing moves only inside the flat projected picture.
- CHIMNEY SMOKE - A HARD REQUIREMENT, CHECKED FIRST: look at the start image - the rows of little red-and-white gingerbread-trimmed workshop cottages with glowing windows along the LEFT wall, the RIGHT wall and around the back wall. Every cottage roof carries a chimney, and from EACH chimney a thick, bright WHITE column of smoke is already pouring out in the very first frame: big round puffs push out one after another, swell, curl and sway, and climb up the wall about one roof-height every second, stretching into long wavy trails that drift toward the ceiling before fading. At every moment at least SIX separate, wide, bright white smoke columns are visibly rising - three or more on each side wall - as obvious as steam from a boiling kettle against the dark night sky. A cottage without rising smoke makes the clip wrong.
- SANTA'S SLEIGH AND EIGHT REINDEER: the WHOLE TEAM TRAVELS across the ceiling in one smooth sweeping arc, covering about one quarter of the ceiling's width every second, so it is in a clearly different place every second - never parked with only its legs moving. The reindeer gallop, heads bob, the sleigh rocks and dips, Santa waves, and the long golden trail streams and curls behind it, shedding glittering sparks.
- THE TOY TRAIN: the candy-striped toy train chugs steadily along its track past the piles of gifts, puffing round white steam clouds, travelling about one cottage-width every second.
- THE ELVES: busy little drawn elves hurry between the cottages carrying stacks of presents, one pushes a sledge of gifts, another waves.
- THE REINDEER YARD: the drawn reindeer in the stable yard prance, toss their antlers and trot in a circle.
- THE COTTAGES: the workshop windows flicker warmly on and off; wreaths on the doors sway; gift piles sparkle.
- SHOOTING STARS AND FIREWORKS: a new shooting star streaks across the ceiling about every second, leaving a glittering tail; small round golden and red fireworks burst in the night sky above the toy village one after another, open into sparkles and fade.
- LIGHTS: the strings of golden lights along the upper walls twinkle in running chase patterns that race along the garlands; the red velvet bows sway; the stars twinkle and the silver moon glows.
- SNOWFALL: big projected snowflakes drift and swirl down across the whole picture, about a quarter of the wall height every second, turning as they fall - flat light on the walls and ceiling, never real snow in the room.
PER-SECOND ANIMATION TRACK (4 s):
0-1s: the sleigh team is already flying; the toy train is chugging, the elves are hurrying with presents, fireworks are bursting and six thick white smoke columns are already rising from the cottage chimneys.
1-2s: the sleigh has moved a quarter of the ceiling and is crossing the silver moon; the toy train chugs past the gift piles puffing steam; the elves carry presents between the cottages; a shooting star streaks over; the smoke columns keep climbing the walls.
2-3s: as the camera tilts up the sleigh flies on; two fireworks burst over the village; the reindeer prance in the yard; the lights chase along the garlands; thick white smoke keeps pouring from every chimney.
3-4s: sleigh flying, smoke pouring from every chimney, toy train chugging, elves hurrying, fireworks bursting, snow falling - all moving in the final frame.
All of this is flat projected light lying on the real shiplap, the reclaimed-oak ridge beam and collar-tie trusses, the whitewashed stone chimney breast, the board-and-batten and the black steel window frames: it bends with the surfaces, never floats into the room, and nothing is projected on the floor, furniture or children.

CHILDREN - AMAZED, AND ALWAYS MOVING:
THE GIRL lands from the jump shown in the start image onto the sofa cushions and keeps bouncing along the sofa with small, springy, real-speed bounces - her feet leave the cushion by only 15 to 25 centimetres, about two bounces per second, the cushion visibly sinking on every landing - moving a little further along the sofa with each bounce while she points one arm straight up at Santa's flying sleigh, head tipped back, mouth wide open, squealing with delight.
THE BOY walks slowly backwards across the rug with his head tipped far back, one arm stretched up pointing at the sleigh, turning his body to follow it as it flies across the ceiling; around 2 seconds he glances across at his sister, points up again and laughs, then keeps stepping and gazing up.
Neither child ever stands still, poses or faces the camera. Real children moving at real speed with real weight: quick, snappy bounces under normal gravity, never slow motion, never floating, never a high exaggerated leap, no morphing limbs.

TIMELINE (camera):
0.0-1.0s the person filming takes one small step forward; the frame moves in slightly and settles.
1.0-2.0s the camera holds in the closer position.
2.0-4.0s the camera tilts up only a little, about 8 degrees, in one slow smooth move, so the vaulted shiplap ceiling fills no more than the top third of the frame - it stays inside the projected picture the whole time. The ENTIRE vaulted shiplap ceiling in view, every plane, beam and corner, is covered with the projection - starry midnight sky, the silver full moon, the snowflakes and the flying sleigh - no bare plaster, no bare wood, no unprojected corner anywhere in view. Both children stay low in the frame and keep moving.
No zoom - the only forward movement is the one small physical step.

AUDIO: room tone, two children laughing, gasping and squealing, cushions thumping, feet on a rug. (no BGM). No subtitles.

SURFACE MAPPING - The two sloping shiplap planes, the reclaimed-oak ridge beam and the collar-tie trusses remain stationary. The drawings fold at the ridge and run across the faces of the ridge beam and every truss, fold around the whitewashed stone chimney corners and carry across the black steel window frames, the board-and-batten and the black barn door, with correct surface perspective and occlusion. All physical architecture stays stationary.

DO NOT INCLUDE: bare, blank, white or partly unprojected ceiling, beam, corner or wall in any frame, especially at the end when the camera looks up; a camera that tilts up beyond the projected picture; a projection appearing, fading in or revealing itself; children standing still; slow motion; floating or weightless movement; a third child; an adult; any music; the projector unit in shot; a zoom; blur; a cut; on-screen text; subtitles.

MOTION GUARDRAILS - Failed if: any drawn animal or figure that looks real or leaves the wall; any house or cottage without a thick rising smoke column; fewer than twelve things moving at once; a calm or slow projection; the sleigh stays in one place or only its legs move; any chimney has no rising smoke; any cottage without a thick rising smoke column; the toy train or the elves do not travel; snow does not fall; the picture moves only because the camera moves; the animation starts late, pauses or freezes at the end; the whole picture slides as one sheet; any projected shape floats in the room. Real-time speed, no slow motion, no music, no subtitles.
